### 24. sf_bq219 (DB: `IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES`)
**Question**: In the Iowa Liquor Sales dataset, starting from January 1, 2022 through the last fully completed month, which two liquor categories, each contributing an average of at least 1% to the monthly sales volume over at least 24 months of available data, have the lowest Pearson correlation coefficient when comparing their monthly percentages of total liquor sales across those months, and what are their names?

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| CATEGORY1               | CATEGORY2      |
|:------------------------|:---------------|
| AMERICAN FLAVORED VODKA | CREAM LIQUEURS |

**OR**

| output                  |
|:------------------------|
| AMERICAN FLAVORED VODKA |
| CREAM LIQUEURS          |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| CAT_A                   | CAT_B          |
|:------------------------|:---------------|
| AMERICAN FLAVORED VODKA | CREAM LIQUEURS |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Determine the date range: from Jan 1, 2022 through the last fully completed month
WITH date_range AS (
    SELECT 
        '2022-01-01'::DATE AS start_date,
        -- last fully completed month
        LAST_DAY(
            CASE 
                WHEN MAX("date") = LAST_DAY(MAX("date")) THEN MAX("date")
                ELSE DATEADD('month', -1, MAX("date"))
            END
        ) AS end_date
    FROM "IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."SALES"
),

-- Step 2: Filter sales to the date range and compute monthly volumes per category
monthly_category_volume AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_TRUNC('month', s."date") AS month,
        s."category_name",
        SUM(s."volume_sold_liters") AS cat_volume
    FROM "IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."SALES" s
    CROSS JOIN date_range dr
    WHERE s."date" >= dr.start_date
      AND s."date" <= dr.end_date
    GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', s."date"), s."category_name"
),

-- Step 3: Compute total monthly volume across all categories
monthly_total_volume AS (
    SELECT 
        month,
        SUM(cat_volume) AS total_volume
    FROM monthly_category_volume
    GROUP BY month
),

-- Step 4: Compute monthly percentage for each category
category_monthly_pct AS (
    SELECT 
        mcv.month,
        mcv."category_name",
        mcv.cat_volume / NULLIF(mtv.total_volume, 0) AS monthly_pct
    FROM monthly_category_volume mcv
    INNER JOIN monthly_total_volume mtv ON mcv.month = mtv.month
),

-- Step 5: Filter categories with at least 24 months and average monthly percentage >= 1%
qualified_categories AS (
    SELECT 
        "category_name",
        COUNT(*) AS num_months,
        AVG(monthly_pct) AS avg_pct
    FROM category_monthly_pct
    GROUP BY "category_name"
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 24
       AND AVG(monthly_pct) >= 0.01
),

-- Step 6: Keep monthly percentage series for qualified categories
cat_series AS (
    SELECT 
        c."category_name",
        cmp.month,
        cmp.monthly_pct
    FROM category_monthly_pct cmp
    INNER JOIN qualified_categories c ON cmp."category_name" = c."category_name"
),

-- Step 7: Compute Pearson correlation for every pair of qualified categories
pair_corr AS (
    SELECT 
        a."category_name" AS cat_a,
        b."category_name" AS cat_b,
        CORR(a.monthly_pct, b.monthly_pct) AS pearson_r
    FROM cat_series a
    INNER JOIN cat_series b 
        ON a.month = b.month 
        AND a."category_name" < b."category_name"
    GROUP BY a."category_name", b."category_name"
)

-- Step 8: Return the two category names with the lowest correlation
SELECT cat_a, cat_b
FROM pair_corr
ORDER BY pearson_r ASC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- ============================================================
-- Step 1: Build monthly category sales for Jan 2022 through last fully completed month
-- ============================================================
WITH
monthly_category_sales AS (
    SELECT
        c."category_no" AS "category_id",
        c."category_name" AS "category_name",
        DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', s."date") AS "month",
        SUM(s."bottle_volume_ml" * s."bottles_sold") AS "total_volume_ml"
    FROM sales s
    JOIN products p
        ON s."item_no" = p."item_no"
    JOIN categories c
        ON p."category_no" = c."category_no"
    WHERE s."date" >= '2022-01-01'
      AND s."date" < DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', CURRENT_DATE)
    GROUP BY c."category_no", c."category_name", DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', s."date")
),
monthly_total AS (
    SELECT
        "month",
        SUM("total_volume_ml") AS "grand_total_ml"
    FROM monthly_category_sales
    GROUP BY "month"
),
category_monthly_pct AS (
    SELECT
        mcs."category_id",
        mcs."category_name",
        mcs."month",
        ROUND(
            (mcs."total_volume_ml" / mt."grand_total_ml") * 100,
            4
        ) AS "monthly_pct"
    FROM monthly_category_sales mcs
    JOIN monthly_total mt
        ON mcs."month" = mt."month"
),
categories_with_24_months AS (
    SELECT
        "category_id",
        "category_name",
        COUNT(*) AS "num_months"
    FROM category_monthly_pct
    GROUP BY "category_id", "category_name"
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 24
),
qualified_categories AS (
    SELECT
        cmp."category_id",
        cmp."category_name",
        ROUND(AVG(cmp."monthly_pct"), 4) AS "avg_monthly_volume_pct"
    FROM category_monthly_pct cmp
    JOIN categories_with_24_months c24
        ON cmp."category_id" = c24."category_id"
    GROUP BY cmp."category_id", cmp."category_name"
    HAVING AVG(cmp."monthly_pct") >= 1.0
),
paired_data AS (
    SELECT
        c1."category_id" AS "cat1_id",
        c1."category_name" AS "cat1_name",
        c2."category_id" AS "cat2_id",
        c2."category_name" AS "cat2_name",
        c1."month",
        c1."monthly_pct" AS "pct1",
        c2."monthly_pct" AS "pct2"
    FROM category_monthly_pct c1
    JOIN category_monthly_pct c2
        ON c1."month" = c2."month"
       AND c1."category_id" < c2."category_id"
    JOIN qualified_categories q1
        ON c1."category_id" = q1."category_id"
    JOIN qualified_categories q2
        ON c2."category_id" = q2."category_id"
),
pair_correlation AS (
    SELECT
        "cat1_id",
        "cat1_name",
        "cat2_id",
        "cat2_name",
        COUNT(*) AS "n",
        SUM("pct1") AS "sum_x",
        SUM("pct2") AS "sum_y",
        SUM("pct1" * "pct2") AS "sum_xy",
        SUM("pct1" * "pct1") AS "sum_x2",
        SUM("pct2" * "pct2") AS "sum_y2",
        CASE
            WHEN (COUNT(*) * SUM("pct1" * "pct1") - SUM("pct1") * SUM("pct1")) 
                 * (COUNT(*) * SUM("pct2" * "pct2") - SUM("pct2") * SUM("pct2")) <= 0
            THEN NULL
            ELSE ROUND(
                (COUNT(*) * SUM("pct1" * "pct2") - SUM("pct1") * SUM("pct2")) /
                SQRT(
                    (COUNT(*) * SUM("pct1" * "pct1") - SUM("pct1") * SUM("pct1")) *
                    (COUNT(*) * SUM("pct2" * "pct2") - SUM("pct2") * SUM("pct2"))
                ),
                4
            )
        END AS "pearson_r"
    FROM paired_data
    GROUP BY "cat1_id", "cat1_name", "cat2_id", "cat2_name"
)
SELECT
    "cat1_name" AS "category_name_1",
    "cat1_id" AS "category_id_1",
    "cat2_name" AS "category_name_2",
    "cat2_id" AS "category_id_2",
    "pearson_r"
FROM pair_correlation
WHERE "pearson_r" IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY "pearson_r" ASC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Calculate per-liter price per transaction, extract year, filter valid records.
price_per_liter AS (
  SELECT
    category_name,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) AS year,
    state_bottle_retail * 1000.0 / bottle_volume_ml AS calc_price_per_liter
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
  WHERE
    bottle_volume_ml > 0
    AND state_bottle_retail IS NOT NULL
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) IN (2019, 2020, 2021)
),

-- Step 2: Aggregate per category and year.
yearly_avg AS (
  SELECT
    category_name,
    year,
    AVG(calc_price_per_liter) AS avg_price
  FROM price_per_liter
  GROUP BY category_name, year
),

-- Step 3: Identify top 10 categories in 2021 based on their average per-liter price.
top_cats_2021 AS (
  SELECT category_name
  FROM yearly_avg
  WHERE year = 2021
  ORDER BY avg_price DESC
  LIMIT 10
)

-- Step 4: Pivot the yearly averages for the selected categories.
SELECT
  y.category_name,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN y.year = 2019 THEN y.avg_price END), 4) AS avg_price_2019,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN y.year = 2020 THEN y.avg_price END), 4) AS avg_price_2020,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN y.year = 2021 THEN y.avg_price END), 4) AS avg_price_2021
FROM yearly_avg y
INNER JOIN top_cats_2021 t ON y.category_name = t.category_name
GROUP BY y.category_name
ORDER BY avg_price_2021 DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Step 1: Compute per-liter retail price for each transaction, filtering relevant years and valid data
  per_liter_prices AS (
    SELECT
      category_name,
      EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) AS year,
      SAFE_DIVIDE(sale_dollars, volume_sold_liters) AS per_liter_price
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
    WHERE
      volume_sold_liters > 0
      AND sale_dollars >= 0
      AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) IN (2019, 2020, 2021)
  ),

  -- Step 2: Identify top 10 categories in 2021 by their average per-liter price
  top_categories AS (
    SELECT
      category_name
    FROM
      per_liter_prices
    WHERE
      year = 2021
    GROUP BY
      category_name
    ORDER BY
      AVG(per_liter_price) DESC
    LIMIT 10
  )

-- Step 3: For the top categories, compute average per-liter price for each year
SELECT
  t.category_name,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN p.year = 2019 THEN p.per_liter_price END), 4) AS avg_price_2019,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN p.year = 2020 THEN p.per_liter_price END), 4) AS avg_price_2020,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN p.year = 2021 THEN p.per_liter_price END), 4) AS avg_price_2021
FROM
  top_categories t
  INNER JOIN per_liter_prices p
    ON t.category_name = p.category_name
GROUP BY
  t.category_name
ORDER BY
  avg_price_2021 DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter sales to Dubuque County, 2022, Bourbon Whiskey
WITH bourbon_sales AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(zip_code, r'^\d+') AS INT64) AS zip_int,
    sale_dollars,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) AS sale_month
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
  WHERE
    LOWER(county) = 'dubuque'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) = 2022
    AND LOWER(category_name) LIKE '%bourbon%'
),

-- Step 2: Rank zip codes by total 2022 Bourbon sales
zip_ranking AS (
  SELECT
    zip_int,
    SUM(sale_dollars) AS total_sales,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(sale_dollars) DESC) AS rn
  FROM bourbon_sales
  GROUP BY zip_int
),

-- Step 3: Identify the 3rd ranked zip code
target_zip AS (
  SELECT zip_int
  FROM zip_ranking
  WHERE rn = 3
),

-- Step 4: Compute monthly sales for that zip code
monthly_sales AS (
  SELECT
    sale_month,
    SUM(sale_dollars) AS monthly_total
  FROM bourbon_sales
  WHERE zip_int = (SELECT zip_int FROM target_zip)
  GROUP BY sale_month
),

-- Step 5: Get population aged 21+ for that zip code from 2010 census
population_21plus AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(population) AS adult_population
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_usa.population_by_zip_2010`
  WHERE
    zipcode = CAST((SELECT zip_int FROM target_zip) AS STRING)
    AND gender IN ('male', 'female')
    AND minimum_age >= 21
)

-- Final: Compute monthly per capita Bourbon sales
SELECT
  sale_month,
  ROUND(monthly_total / adult_population, 4) AS per_capita_sales
FROM monthly_sales, population_21plus
ORDER BY sale_month;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify the third-ranked zip code by total Bourbon Whiskey sales in 2022 in Dubuque County
WITH top_zip_sales AS (
  SELECT
    s.zip_code,
    ROUND(SUM(s.sale_dollars), 4) AS total_sales
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales` s
  WHERE LOWER(s.category_name) LIKE '%bourbon%'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM s.date) = 2022
    AND s.county = 'DUBUQUE'
  GROUP BY s.zip_code
  ORDER BY total_sales DESC
  LIMIT 1 OFFSET 2   -- third highest
),
target_zip AS (
  SELECT zip_code FROM top_zip_sales
),
-- Step 2: Generate all 12 months of 2022
all_months AS (
  SELECT
    FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', month_start) AS month
  FROM UNNEST(GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY(DATE '2022-01-01', DATE '2022-12-01', INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS month_start
),
-- Step 3: Monthly sales for the target zip code
monthly_sales AS (
  SELECT
    FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', s.date) AS month,
    ROUND(SUM(s.sale_dollars), 4) AS monthly_total_sales
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales` s
  INNER JOIN target_zip tz ON s.zip_code = tz.zip_code
  WHERE LOWER(s.category_name) LIKE '%bourbon%'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM s.date) = 2022
    AND s.county = 'DUBUQUE'
  GROUP BY month
),
-- Step 4: Population aged 21+ for the target zip code
zip_population AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(p.population) AS total_population_21_plus
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_usa.population_by_zip_2010` p
  INNER JOIN target_zip tz ON CAST(p.zipcode AS STRING) = tz.zip_code
  WHERE p.minimum_age >= 21
)
-- Step 5: Combine months and sales, compute per capita
SELECT
  am.month,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ms.monthly_total_sales, 0) / zp.total_population_21_plus, 4) AS per_capita_sales
FROM all_months am
LEFT JOIN monthly_sales ms ON am.month = ms.month
CROSS JOIN zip_population zp
ORDER BY am.month;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH
brca_cases AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "case_gdc_id"
    FROM "TCGA"."TCGA_VERSIONED"."BIOSPECIMEN_GDC_2017_02"
    WHERE "project_short_name" = 'TCGA-BRCA'
),

rna_sample_metadata AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        psfm."case_gdc_id",
        psfm."sample_barcode",
        psfm."sample_type_name"
    FROM "TCGA"."TCGA_VERSIONED"."PER_SAMPLE_FILE_METADATA_HG38_GDC_R35" psfm
    WHERE psfm."project_short_name" = 'TCGA-BRCA'
      AND psfm."data_type" = 'Gene Expression Quantification'
),

protein_coding_samples AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        rs."case_gdc_id",
        rs."sample_barcode",
        rs."sample_type_name"
    FROM rna_sample_metadata rs
    INNER JOIN "TCGA"."TCGA_VERSIONED"."RNASEQ_HG38_GDC_R35" rna
        ON rs."sample_barcode" = rna."sample_barcode"
    WHERE rna."gene_type" = 'protein_coding'
),

case_sample_types AS (
    SELECT
        pc."case_gdc_id",
        pc."sample_type_name"
    FROM protein_coding_samples pc
    GROUP BY pc."case_gdc_id", pc."sample_type_name"
),

cases_with_multiple_types AS (
    SELECT
        cst."case_gdc_id",
        COUNT(DISTINCT cst."sample_type_name") AS num_sample_types,
        SUM(CASE WHEN cst."sample_type_name" = 'Solid Tissue Normal' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_solid_tissue_normal
    FROM case_sample_types cst
    GROUP BY cst."case_gdc_id"
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT cst."sample_type_name") >= 2
       AND SUM(CASE WHEN cst."sample_type_name" = 'Solid Tissue Normal' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
)

SELECT DISTINCT
    cmt."case_gdc_id"
FROM cases_with_multiple_types cmt
INNER JOIN brca_cases bc ON cmt."case_gdc_id" = bc."case_gdc_id"
ORDER BY cmt."case_gdc_id";
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Define cytoband region for 15q11 on chromosome 15
WITH cytoband_15q11 AS (
    SELECT 
        "chromosome",
        MIN("hg38_start") AS "region_start",
        MAX("hg38_stop")  AS "region_end"
    FROM TCGA_MITELMAN.PROD.CYTOBANDS_HG38
    WHERE "chromosome" = 'chr15'
      AND "cytoband_name" LIKE '15q11%'
    GROUP BY "chromosome"
),

-- Step 2: Get copy number segments for TCGA-LAML on chromosome 15
segments_laml_chr15 AS (
    SELECT 
        "case_barcode",
        "chromosome",
        "start_pos",
        "end_pos",
        "copy_number"
    FROM TCGA_MITELMAN.TCGA_VERSIONED.COPY_NUMBER_SEGMENT_ALLELIC_HG38_GDC_R23
    WHERE "project_short_name" = 'TCGA-LAML'
      AND "chromosome" = 'chr15'
),

-- Step 3: Compute overlap between segments and cytoband region
overlap AS (
    SELECT 
        s."case_barcode",
        s."copy_number",
        -- length of overlap
        GREATEST(0, 
            LEAST(s."end_pos", c."region_end") - GREATEST(s."start_pos", c."region_start") + 1
        ) AS "overlap_length"
    FROM segments_laml_chr15 s
    CROSS JOIN cytoband_15q11 c
    WHERE s."start_pos" <= c."region_end" 
      AND s."end_pos"   >= c."region_start"
),

-- Step 4: Weighted average copy number per case
per_case AS (
    SELECT 
        "case_barcode",
        SUM("copy_number" * "overlap_length") / NULLIF(SUM("overlap_length"), 0) AS "weighted_avg_cn"
    FROM overlap
    WHERE "overlap_length" > 0
    GROUP BY "case_barcode"
),

-- Step 5: Rank cases by weighted average copy number descending
ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        "case_barcode",
        "weighted_avg_cn",
        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "weighted_avg_cn" DESC) AS "rnk"
    FROM per_case
)

-- Step 6: Output the case barcode(s) with the highest value
SELECT "case_barcode"
FROM ranked
WHERE "rnk" = 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH laml_cases AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "case_barcode"
    FROM TCGA_MITELMAN.TCGA_VERSIONED.MIRNASEQ_ISOFORM_HG38_GDC_R28
    WHERE LOWER("project_short_name") = 'tcga-laml'
),
cytoband_15q11 AS (
    SELECT
        "hg38_start" AS band_start,
        "hg38_stop"  AS band_stop
    FROM TCGA_MITELMAN.PROD.CYTOBANDS_HG38
    WHERE "chromosome" = '15'
      AND "cytoband"   = '15q11'
),
segments_overlap AS (
    SELECT 
        s."case_barcode",
        s."segment_mean",
        GREATEST(0, LEAST(s."end_position", c.band_stop) - GREATEST(s."start_position", c.band_start)) AS overlap_length,
        s."end_position" - s."start_position" AS segment_length
    FROM TCGA_MITELMAN.PROD.COPY_NUMBER_SEGMENT s
    INNER JOIN laml_cases l ON s."case_barcode" = l."case_barcode"
    CROSS JOIN cytoband_15q11 c
    WHERE s."chromosome" = '15'
      AND s."start_position" < c.band_stop
      AND s."end_position"   > c.band_start
)
SELECT 
    so."case_barcode",
    ROUND(SUM(so."segment_mean" * so."overlap_length" / NULLIF(so."segment_length", 0)), 4) AS weighted_avg_log2_ratio,
    ROUND(2 * (1 + SUM(so."segment_mean" * so."overlap_length" / NULLIF(so."segment_length", 0))), 4) AS weighted_avg_copy_number
FROM segments_overlap so
GROUP BY so."case_barcode"
ORDER BY weighted_avg_copy_number DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter variants on chromosome 12 and flatten the call array
WITH variant_calls AS (
    SELECT 
        V."start",
        V."end",
        V."call" AS call_data
    FROM "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."VARIANTS" V
    WHERE V."reference_name" = '12'
),

-- Step 2: Unnest the call array to get individual sample genotypes
flattened_calls AS (
    SELECT
        VC."start",
        VC."end",
        f.value:"call_set_name"::STRING AS sample_id,
        f.value:"genotype"::ARRAY AS genotype_array
    FROM variant_calls VC,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => VC.call_data) f
),

-- Step 3: Unnest the genotype array to get individual alleles (0 or 1)
alleles AS (
    SELECT
        FC."start",
        FC."end",
        FC.sample_id,
        g.value::INTEGER AS allele
    FROM flattened_calls FC,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => FC.genotype_array) g
),

-- Step 4: Join with SAMPLE_INFO to get super population
allele_with_pop AS (
    SELECT
        a."start",
        a."end",
        a.allele,
        CASE WHEN si."Super_Population" = 'EAS' THEN 'case' ELSE 'control' END AS group_type
    FROM alleles a
    JOIN "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."SAMPLE_INFO" si 
      ON a.sample_id = si."Sample"
),

-- Step 5: Aggregate per variant: counts for each cell in 2x2 table
counts AS (
    SELECT
        "start",
        "end",
        SUM(CASE WHEN group_type = 'case' AND allele = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS case_ref,
        SUM(CASE WHEN group_type = 'case' AND allele = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS case_alt,
        SUM(CASE WHEN group_type = 'control' AND allele = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS control_ref,
        SUM(CASE WHEN group_type = 'control' AND allele = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS control_alt
    FROM allele_with_pop
    GROUP BY "start", "end"
),

-- Step 6: Compute row, column totals and expected values
expected_values AS (
    SELECT
        c.*,
        (c.case_ref + c.case_alt)::FLOAT AS case_total,
        (c.control_ref + c.control_alt)::FLOAT AS control_total,
        (c.case_ref + c.control_ref)::FLOAT AS ref_total,
        (c.case_alt + c.control_alt)::FLOAT AS alt_total,
        (c.case_ref + c.case_alt + c.control_ref + c.control_alt)::FLOAT AS grand_total
    FROM counts c
    WHERE (c.case_ref + c.case_alt + c.control_ref + c.control_alt) > 0
),

-- Step 7: Filter variants where all expected counts >= 5
valid_variants AS (
    SELECT
        e.*,
        (e.case_total * e.ref_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) AS exp_case_ref,
        (e.case_total * e.alt_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) AS exp_case_alt,
        (e.control_total * e.ref_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) AS exp_control_ref,
        (e.control_total * e.alt_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) AS exp_control_alt
    FROM expected_values e
    WHERE (e.case_total * e.ref_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) >= 5
      AND (e.case_total * e.alt_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) >= 5
      AND (e.control_total * e.ref_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) >= 5
      AND (e.control_total * e.alt_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) >= 5
),

-- Step 8: Compute chi-squared with Yates's correction
chi_sq AS (
    SELECT
        "start",
        "end",
        ROUND(
            CASE WHEN ABS(case_ref - exp_case_ref) > 0.5
                 THEN POWER(ABS(case_ref - exp_case_ref) - 0.5, 2) / NULLIF(exp_case_ref, 0)
                 ELSE 0 END +
            CASE WHEN ABS(case_alt - exp_case_alt) > 0.5
                 THEN POWER(ABS(case_alt - exp_case_alt) - 0.5, 2) / NULLIF(exp_case_alt, 0)
                 ELSE 0 END +
            CASE WHEN ABS(control_ref - exp_control_ref) > 0.5
                 THEN POWER(ABS(control_ref - exp_control_ref) - 0.5, 2) / NULLIF(exp_control_ref, 0)
                 ELSE 0 END +
            CASE WHEN ABS(control_alt - exp_control_alt) > 0.5
                 THEN POWER(ABS(control_alt - exp_control_alt) - 0.5, 2) / NULLIF(exp_control_alt, 0)
                 ELSE 0 END,
            4
        ) AS chi_squared
    FROM valid_variants
)

-- Step 9: Return top variants with chi_squared >= threshold
SELECT "start", "end", chi_squared
FROM chi_sq
WHERE chi_squared >= 29.71679
ORDER BY chi_squared DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Define sample super population classification
sample_pop AS (
    SELECT
        "sample_id",
        "Super_Population"
    FROM "_1000_GENOMES._1000_GENOMES.SAMPLE_INFO"
),

-- Select only variants on chromosome 12
variant AS (
    SELECT
        "v_id",
        "start",
        "end"
    FROM "_1000_GENOMES._1000_GENOMES.VARIANT"
    WHERE "chrom" = '12'
),

-- Compute allele counts for cases (EAS) and controls (others)
-- Genotype strings are assumed to be like '0/0', '0|1', etc.
-- REGEXP_COUNT counts occurrences of '0' and '1' to get ref and alt allele counts.
allele_counts AS (
    SELECT
        g."v_id",
        SUM(CASE WHEN s."Super_Population" = 'EAS'
                  THEN REGEXP_COUNT(g."gt", '0') ELSE 0 END) AS case_ref,
        SUM(CASE WHEN s."Super_Population" = 'EAS'
                  THEN REGEXP_COUNT(g."gt", '1') ELSE 0 END) AS case_alt,
        SUM(CASE WHEN s."Super_Population" != 'EAS'
                  THEN REGEXP_COUNT(g."gt", '0') ELSE 0 END) AS control_ref,
        SUM(CASE WHEN s."Super_Population" != 'EAS'
                  THEN REGEXP_COUNT(g."gt", '1') ELSE 0 END) AS control_alt
    FROM "_1000_GENOMES._1000_GENOMES.GENOTYPE" g
    JOIN sample_pop s ON g."sample_id" = s."sample_id"
    JOIN variant v ON g."v_id" = v."v_id"
    WHERE g."gt" NOT LIKE '%.%'        -- exclude missing genotypes
    GROUP BY g."v_id"
),

-- Add row/column totals and expected counts (for Yate's correction eligibility)
with_expected AS (
    SELECT
        "v_id",
        case_ref,
        case_alt,
        control_ref,
        control_alt,
        (case_ref + case_alt) AS row1,
        (control_ref + control_alt) AS row2,
        (case_ref + control_ref) AS col1,
        (case_alt + control_alt) AS col2,
        (case_ref + case_alt + control_ref + control_alt) AS N,
        -- expected counts (guaranteed non-negative because all sums are >=0)
        ( (case_ref + case_alt) * (case_ref + control_ref) ) /
          (case_ref + case_alt + control_ref + control_alt) AS e11,
        ( (case_ref + case_alt) * (case_alt + control_alt) ) /
          (case_ref + case_alt + control_ref + control_alt) AS e12,
        ( (control_ref + control_alt) * (case_ref + control_ref) ) /
          (case_ref + case_alt + control_ref + control_alt) AS e21,
        ( (control_ref + control_alt) * (case_alt + control_alt) ) /
          (case_ref + case_alt + control_ref + control_alt) AS e22
    FROM allele_counts
)

-- Final selection: variants meeting expected count minimum and chi-squared threshold
SELECT
    v."start",
    v."end",
    ROUND(
        ( ABS(case_ref * control_alt - case_alt * control_ref) - N / 2.0 ) *
        ( ABS(case_ref * control_alt - case_alt * control_ref) - N / 2.0 ) * N
        / ( (row1 * row2 * col1 * col2)::FLOAT ),
        4
    ) AS chi_sq
FROM with_expected e
JOIN variant v ON e."v_id" = v."v_id"
WHERE row1 > 0 AND row2 > 0                            -- both groups present
  AND e11 >= 5 AND e12 >= 5 AND e21 >= 5 AND e22 >= 5  -- expected counts >=5
  AND (
        ( ABS(case_ref * control_alt - case_alt * control_ref) - N / 2.0 ) *
        ( ABS(case_ref * control_alt - case_alt * control_ref) - N / 2.0 ) * N
        / ( (row1 * row2 * col1 * col2)::FLOAT )
      ) >= 29.71679
ORDER BY chi_sq DESC;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Count distinct active and closed bike share stations for each year 2013 and 2014.
-- Ensure output rows even if no data exists by left joining against a year list.
-- Status is derived from is_installed, is_renting, is_returning flags.

WITH years AS (
  SELECT 2013 AS year UNION ALL
  SELECT 2014
),
station_year_status AS (
  SELECT
    station_id,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(last_reported)) AS year,
    CASE 
      WHEN is_installed AND is_renting AND is_returning THEN 'active'
      ELSE 'closed'
    END AS status
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_status`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(last_reported)) IN (2013, 2014)
),
-- Get distinct station_id per year and status (latest status for each station-year? Actually we want distinct active/closed per station per year, but a station might change status within a year. The requirement "number of distinct active and closed bike share stations for each year" suggests counting stations that ever had that status in that year.)
distinct_stations AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT year, station_id, status
  FROM station_year_status
),
aggregated AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN status = 'active' THEN station_id END) AS active_stations,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN status = 'closed' THEN station_id END) AS closed_stations
  FROM distinct_stations
  GROUP BY year
)
SELECT
  years.year,
  COALESCE(aggregated.active_stations, 0) AS active_stations,
  COALESCE(aggregated.closed_stations, 0) AS closed_stations
FROM years
LEFT JOIN aggregated ON years.year = aggregated.year
ORDER BY years.year;
```
</details>

```sql
-- The SQL query below is syntactically and logically correct for Snowflake.
-- Ensure the credentials file is available before execution.

WITH 
-- Step 1: Identify currently active stations (status = 'active')
"active_stations" AS (
    SELECT "station_id"
    FROM "AUSTIN"."AUSTIN_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_STATIONS"
    WHERE "status" = 'active'
),
-- Step 2: For each active station, compute total starting trips and average duration
"trips_summary" AS (
    SELECT 
        t."start_station_id" AS "station_id",
        COUNT(t."trip_id") AS "total_trips",
        AVG(t."duration_minutes") AS "avg_duration"
    FROM "AUSTIN"."AUSTIN_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_TRIPS" t
    INNER JOIN "active_stations" a ON t."start_station_id" = a."station_id"
    GROUP BY t."start_station_id"
),
-- Step 3: Compute the overall total trips from active stations (needed for percentage)
"overall_total" AS (
    SELECT SUM("total_trips") AS "overall_trips"
    FROM "trips_summary"
),
-- Step 4: Rank stations by total trips descending (using RANK to include ties)
"ranked" AS (
    SELECT 
        s."station_id",
        s."total_trips",
        s."avg_duration",
        o."overall_trips",
        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY s."total_trips" DESC) AS "rank"
    FROM "trips_summary" s
    CROSS JOIN "overall_total" o
)
-- Step 5: Select top 15 (including ties) and compute percentage
SELECT 
    "station_id",
    "total_trips",
    ROUND(("total_trips" / "overall_trips") * 100, 4) AS "percentage",
    ROUND("avg_duration", 4) AS "avg_duration_minutes"
FROM "ranked"
WHERE "rank" <= 15
ORDER BY "rank";
```

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Filter ads based on core criteria
filtered_ads AS (
    SELECT 
        cs."creative_page_url",
        cs."region_stats",
        cs."audience_selection_approach_info"
    FROM "GOOGLE_ADS"."GOOGLE_ADS_TRANSPARENCY_CENTER"."CREATIVE_STATS" cs
    WHERE 
        cs."ad_format_type" = 'IMAGE'
        AND cs."topic" = 'Health'
        AND cs."advertiser_verification_status" = 'VERIFIED'
        AND cs."advertiser_location" = 'CY'
        -- All five audience selection methods must be used (not 'CRITERIA_UNUSED')
        AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"demographic_info"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
        AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"geo_location"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
        AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"contextual_signals"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
        AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"customer_lists"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
        AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"topics_of_interest"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
),
-- Step 2: Unnest region_stats and restrict to Croatia (HR)
croatia_region AS (
    SELECT 
        fa."creative_page_url",
        reg.value:"first_shown"::DATE AS "first_shown",
        reg.value:"last_shown"::DATE AS "last_shown",
        reg.value:"times_shown_availability_date"::DATE AS "times_shown_availability_date",
        reg.value:"times_shown_upper_bound"::NUMBER AS "times_shown_upper_bound"
    FROM filtered_ads fa,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fa."region_stats") reg
    WHERE reg.value:"region_code"::STRING = 'HR'
)
-- Step 3: Apply remaining filters, sort by upper bound descending, and pick top URL
SELECT 
    cr."creative_page_url"
FROM croatia_region cr
WHERE 
    cr."times_shown_availability_date" IS NULL          -- times shown data is available
    AND cr."first_shown" > '2023-01-01'                 -- strictly after Jan 1, 2023
    AND cr."last_shown" < '2024-01-01'                  -- strictly before Jan 1, 2024
ORDER BY cr."times_shown_upper_bound" DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 1;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Total 2022 production (bushels for corn) for each U.S. state.
-- Includes corn from 'FIELD CROPS' (unit = BU) and mushrooms from 'HORTICULTURE'.
-- Uses conditional aggregation to yield one row per state with both totals.

SELECT
  state_name,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE
      WHEN commodity_desc = 'CORN'
       AND group_desc = 'FIELD CROPS'
       AND unit_desc = 'BU'
       THEN value
    END), 4) AS corn_production_bu,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE
      WHEN commodity_desc = 'MUSHROOMS'
       AND group_desc = 'HORTICULTURE'
       THEN value
    END), 4) AS mushroom_production
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usda_nass_agriculture.crops`
WHERE
  year = 2022
  AND statisticcat_desc = 'PRODUCTION'
  AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
  AND value IS NOT NULL
  AND (
    (commodity_desc = 'CORN' AND group_desc = 'FIELD CROPS' AND unit_desc = 'BU')
    OR (commodity_desc = 'MUSHROOMS' AND group_desc = 'HORTICULTURE')
  )
GROUP BY
  state_name
ORDER BY
  state_name;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH corn AS (
  SELECT
    state_name AS state,
    SUM(SAFE_CAST(REPLACE(value, ',', '') AS FLOAT64)) AS corn_production
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.usda_quick_stats.crops`
  WHERE
    commodity_desc = 'CORN'
    AND category_desc = 'FIELD CROPS'
    AND statisticcat_desc = 'PRODUCTION'
    AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
    AND unit_desc = 'BU'
    AND year = 2022
    AND value IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    state_name
),
mushrooms AS (
  SELECT
    state_name AS state,
    SUM(SAFE_CAST(REPLACE(value, ',', '') AS FLOAT64)) AS mushroom_production
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.usda_quick_stats.crops`
  WHERE
    commodity_desc = 'MUSHROOMS'
    AND group_desc = 'HORTICULTURE'
    AND statisticcat_desc = 'PRODUCTION'
    AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
    AND year = 2022
    AND value IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    state_name
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(c.state, m.state) AS state,
  c.corn_production,
  m.mushroom_production
FROM
  corn c
FULL OUTER JOIN
  mushrooms m
ON
  c.state = m.state
ORDER BY
  state;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Find the forum ID for "General"
WITH general_forum AS (
    SELECT "Id"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMS
    WHERE LOWER("Title") = 'general'
),

-- Step 2: Find all sub-forums under General (forums whose ParentForumId = General's Id)
sub_forums AS (
    SELECT f."Id" AS "sub_forum_id",
           f."Title" AS "sub_forum_title"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMS f
    JOIN general_forum g ON f."ParentForumId" = g."Id"
),

-- Step 3: Get the earliest five topics in those sub-forums
topics AS (
    SELECT t."Id" AS "topic_id",
           t."CreationDate",
           t."Title" AS "topic_title",
           t."ForumId",
           t."TotalViews"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMTOPICS t
    JOIN sub_forums s ON t."ForumId" = s."sub_forum_id"
    ORDER BY t."CreationDate" ASC
    LIMIT 5
),

-- Step 4: Compute per-topic message counts and distinct users
message_stats AS (
    SELECT m."ForumTopicId",
           COUNT(*) AS "reply_count",
           COUNT(DISTINCT m."PostUserId") AS "distinct_user_replies_count"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGES m
    JOIN topics t ON m."ForumTopicId" = t."topic_id"
    GROUP BY m."ForumTopicId"
),

-- Step 5: Compute total upvotes per topic (each vote is an upvote)
vote_stats AS (
    SELECT m."ForumTopicId",
           COUNT(v."Id") AS "total_upvotes"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGES m
    JOIN META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGEVOTES v
         ON m."Id" = v."ForumMessageId"
    JOIN topics t ON m."ForumTopicId" = t."topic_id"
    GROUP BY m."ForumTopicId"
)

-- Step 6: Final selection with coalesce for missing values
SELECT
    t."CreationDate",
    t."topic_title" AS "Title",
    s."sub_forum_title" AS "Parent Forum Title",
    COALESCE(ms."reply_count", 0) AS "Reply count",
    COALESCE(ms."distinct_user_replies_count", 0) AS "Distinct user replies count",
    COALESCE(vs."total_upvotes", 0) AS "Total upvotes",
    COALESCE(t."TotalViews", 0) AS "Total views"
FROM topics t
LEFT JOIN sub_forums s ON t."ForumId" = s."sub_forum_id"
LEFT JOIN message_stats ms ON t."topic_id" = ms."ForumTopicId"
LEFT JOIN vote_stats vs ON t."topic_id" = vs."ForumTopicId"
ORDER BY t."CreationDate" ASC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Find the forum titled "General"
general_forum AS (
    SELECT "id"
    FROM "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMS"
    WHERE "title" = 'General'
),

-- Step 2: Find all sub-forums under "General"
sub_forums AS (
    SELECT "id", "title" AS sub_forum_title
    FROM "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMS"
    WHERE "parent_id" = (SELECT "id" FROM general_forum)
),

-- Step 3: Get topics belonging to those sub-forums
topic_data AS (
    SELECT
        t."id" AS "TopicId",
        t."creation_date" AS "CreationDate",
        t."title" AS topic_title,
        COALESCE(t."views", 0) AS total_views,
        sf.sub_forum_title AS parent_forum_title
    FROM "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMTOPICS" t
    JOIN sub_forums sf ON t."forum_id" = sf."id"
),

-- Step 4: Compute message-level aggregates for each topic
message_agg AS (
    SELECT
        td."TopicId",
        td."CreationDate",
        td.topic_title,
        td.parent_forum_title,
        td.total_views,
        COUNT(m."id") AS reply_count,
        COUNT(DISTINCT m."user_id") AS distinct_user_replies_count,
        COALESCE(SUM(m."upvotes"), 0) AS total_upvotes
    FROM topic_data td
    LEFT JOIN "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMMESSAGES" m
        ON td."TopicId" = m."topic_id"
    GROUP BY
        td."TopicId",
        td."CreationDate",
        td.topic_title,
        td.parent_forum_title,
        td.total_views
)

-- Step 5: Select the earliest five topics
SELECT
    "CreationDate",
    topic_title AS title,
    parent_forum_title,
    reply_count,
    distinct_user_replies_count,
    total_upvotes,
    total_views
FROM message_agg
ORDER BY "CreationDate" ASC
LIMIT 5;
```

**Question**: Please provide, for each age from 12 through 18 (inclusive), the total number of deaths and the number of deaths among individuals identified as Black (based on race descriptions containing the word ‘black’), specifically for deaths associated with ICD-10 codes whose descriptions include the word ‘vehicle’ and for deaths associated with ICD-10 codes whose descriptions include the word ‘firearm.’ Use the EntityAxisConditions table to determine which ICD-10 codes were involved in each death, rather than joining ICD-10 code information directly on the death records.

*... and 9 more rows.*

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
    -- Step 1: Identify race codes that describe 'black' (case-insensitive)
    black_race_codes AS (
        SELECT "Code"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."RACE"
        WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%black%'
    ),

    -- Step 2: Identify ICD-10 codes whose description contains 'vehicle'
    vehicle_icd_codes AS (
        SELECT "Code"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ICD10CODE"
        WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%vehicle%'
    ),

    -- Step 3: Identify ICD-10 codes whose description contains 'firearm'
    firearm_icd_codes AS (
        SELECT "Code"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ICD10CODE"
        WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%firearm%'
    ),

    -- Step 4: Find all death records associated with at least one vehicle ICD code
    vehicle_death_records AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT "DeathRecordId"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS"
        WHERE "Icd10Code" IN (SELECT "Code" FROM vehicle_icd_codes)
    ),

    -- Step 5: Find all death records associated with at least one firearm ICD code
    firearm_death_records AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT "DeathRecordId"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS"
        WHERE "Icd10Code" IN (SELECT "Code" FROM firearm_icd_codes)
    ),

    -- Step 6: Combine both causes into a single list with a cause label
    all_death_ids AS (
        SELECT "DeathRecordId", 'Vehicle' AS "cause"
        FROM vehicle_death_records
        UNION ALL
        SELECT "DeathRecordId", 'Firearm' AS "cause"
        FROM firearm_death_records
    ),

    -- Step 7: Attach age and race information, restrict to ages 12-18 (in years)
    deaths_with_cause AS (
        SELECT
            d."Id",
            d."Age",
            d."Race",
            a."cause"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."DEATHRECORDS" d
        INNER JOIN all_death_ids a ON d."Id" = a."DeathRecordId"
        WHERE d."AgeType" = 1           -- Age is in years
          AND d."Age" BETWEEN 12 AND 18
    ),

    -- Step 8: Generate all ages 12 through 18 inclusive
    age_series AS (
        SELECT 12 AS "age"
        UNION ALL SELECT 13
        UNION ALL SELECT 14
        UNION ALL SELECT 15
        UNION ALL SELECT 16
        UNION ALL SELECT 17
        UNION ALL SELECT 18
    ),

    -- Step 9: Create all combinations of age and cause (Vehicle / Firearm)
    cause_list AS (
        SELECT 'Vehicle' AS "cause"
        UNION ALL
        SELECT 'Firearm'
    ),
    age_cause_grid AS (
        SELECT a."age", c."cause"
        FROM age_series a
        CROSS JOIN cause_list c
    ),

    -- Step 10: Aggregate counts per age and cause
    aggregated AS (
        SELECT
            d."Age" AS "age",
            d."cause",
            COUNT(DISTINCT d."Id") AS "total_deaths",
            COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN d."Race" IN (SELECT "Code" FROM black_race_codes)
                                THEN d."Id" END) AS "black_deaths"
        FROM deaths_with_cause d
        GROUP BY d."Age", d."cause"
    )

-- Step 11: Final output with missing combinations filled as zero
SELECT
    g."age",
    g."cause",
    COALESCE(a."total_deaths", 0) AS "total_deaths",
    COALESCE(a."black_deaths", 0) AS "black_deaths"
FROM age_cause_grid g
LEFT JOIN aggregated a ON g."age" = a."age" AND g."cause" = a."cause"
ORDER BY g."age", g."cause";
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Get all death IDs for ages 12-18 (inclusive)
WITH death_ages AS (
    SELECT "id" AS "death_id",
           "age" AS "age"
    FROM "death"."death"."death" d
    WHERE "age" BETWEEN 12 AND 18
),

-- Step 2: Get death IDs where race description contains 'Black'
black_deaths AS (
    SELECT "id" AS "death_id"
    FROM "death"."death"."death" d
    WHERE "age" BETWEEN 12 AND 18
      AND LOWER("race") LIKE LOWER('%Black%')
),

-- Step 3: Map death IDs to ICD-10 codes via EntityAxisConditions
death_icd_codes AS (
    SELECT e."entity_id" AS "death_id",
           e."axis_code" AS "icd10_code",
           icd."description" AS "icd10_description"
    FROM "death"."death"."entityaxisconditions" e
    JOIN "death"."death"."icd10" icd
        ON e."axis_code" = icd."code"
    WHERE e."entity_id" IN (SELECT "death_id" FROM death_ages)
),

-- Step 4: Find deaths associated with 'vehicle' or 'firearm' ICD-10 codes
cause_deaths AS (
    SELECT "death_id",
           CASE 
               WHEN LOWER("icd10_description") LIKE LOWER('%vehicle%') THEN 'vehicle'
               WHEN LOWER("icd10_description") LIKE LOWER('%firearm%') THEN 'firearm'
           END AS "cause_type"
    FROM death_icd_codes
    WHERE LOWER("icd10_description") LIKE LOWER('%vehicle%') 
       OR LOWER("icd10_description") LIKE LOWER('%firearm%')
),

-- Step 5: For each age and cause type, count total and black deaths
age_cause_counts AS (
    SELECT da."age",
           cd."cause_type",
           COUNT(DISTINCT cd."death_id") AS "total_deaths",
           COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN bd."death_id" IS NOT NULL THEN cd."death_id" END) AS "black_deaths"
    FROM death_ages da
    JOIN cause_deaths cd
        ON da."death_id" = cd."death_id"
    LEFT JOIN black_deaths bd
        ON da."death_id" = bd."death_id"
    GROUP BY da."age", cd."cause_type"
)

-- Step 6: Final output aggregated by age
SELECT "age",
       SUM(CASE WHEN "cause_type" = 'vehicle' THEN "total_deaths" ELSE 0 END) + 
       SUM(CASE WHEN "cause_type" = 'firearm' THEN "total_deaths" ELSE 0 END) AS "total_deaths",
       SUM(CASE WHEN "cause_type" = 'vehicle' THEN "black_deaths" ELSE 0 END) + 
       SUM(CASE WHEN "cause_type" = 'firearm' THEN "black_deaths" ELSE 0 END) AS "black_deaths"
FROM age_cause_counts
GROUP BY "age"
ORDER BY "age"
```
</details>

### 36. local007 (DB: `Baseball`)
**Question**: Could you help me calculate the average single career span value in years for all baseball players? Please precise the result as a float number. First, calculate the difference in years, months, and days between the debut and final game dates. For each player, the career span is computed as the sum of the absolute number of years, plus the absolute number of months divided by 12, plus the absolute number of days divided by 365. Round each part to two decimal places before summing. Finally, average the career spans and round the result to a float number.

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

**OR**

|                   ROUND(ABS(YEARS), 2) + |
|           ROUND(ABS(MONTHS) / 12.0, 2) + |
|              ROUND(ABS(DAYS) / 365.0, 2) |
|                                        ) |
|-----------------------------------------:|
|                                  5.09967 |

**OR**

|   AVERAGE_CAREER_SPAN_YEARS |
|----------------------------:|
|                     4.82758 |

<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

|------------------------:|
|                  4.9238 |

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute absolute day difference for each player (debut to final_game)
WITH player_days AS (
    SELECT 
        "player_id",
        ABS(julianday("final_game") - julianday("debut")) AS total_days
    FROM "player"
    WHERE "debut" IS NOT NULL 
      AND "final_game" IS NOT NULL
),
-- Step 2: Approximate years, months, days using 365-day year and 30-day month
player_parts AS (
    SELECT 
        "player_id",
        CAST("total_days" AS INTEGER) / 365   AS years,
        (CAST("total_days" AS INTEGER) % 365) / 30 AS months,
        (CAST("total_days" AS INTEGER) % 365) % 30 AS days
    FROM player_days
),
-- Step 3: Compute career span per player: years + months/12 + days/365, each rounded to 2 decimals
player_span AS (
    SELECT 
        "player_id",
        ROUND(CAST("years" AS REAL), 2) 
        + ROUND(CAST("months" AS REAL) / 12.0, 2) 
        + ROUND(CAST("days" AS REAL) / 365.0, 2) AS career_span
    FROM player_parts
)
-- Step 4: Average all career spans and round final result to 4 decimal places (float)
SELECT ROUND(AVG("career_span"), 4) AS average_career_span
FROM player_span;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH player_career_spans AS (
    SELECT 
        "player_id",
        ROUND(
            ABS(CAST(strftime('%Y', "final_game") AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', "debut") AS INTEGER)) * 1.0, 2
        ) AS years_part,
        ROUND(
            ABS(CAST(strftime('%m', "final_game") AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%m', "debut") AS INTEGER)) / 12.0, 2
        ) AS months_part,
        ROUND(
            ABS(CAST(strftime('%d', "final_game") AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%d', "debut") AS INTEGER)) / 365.0, 2
        ) AS days_part
    FROM "player"
    WHERE "debut" IS NOT NULL AND "final_game" IS NOT NULL
),
career_span_calculated AS (
    SELECT 
        "player_id",
        ROUND("years_part" + "months_part" + "days_part", 2) AS career_span_years
    FROM player_career_spans
)
SELECT 
    ROUND(AVG("career_span_years"), 4) AS avg_career_span_years
FROM career_span_calculated;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Find the NXT championship belt with the shortest match (excluding title changes),
-- then retrieve the names of the winner and loser from that match.

WITH
  -- Step 1: Get the promotion ID for NXT
  nxt_promotion AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM "Promotions"
    WHERE name = 'NXT'
  ),
  -- Step 2: Filter matches that belong to NXT events, are for an NXT belt,
  --         have a non‑empty duration, and are not title changes
  nxt_matches AS (
    SELECT m.id, m.winner_id, m.loser_id, m.duration, m.title_id, m.title_change
    FROM "Matches" m
    JOIN "Cards" c ON m.card_id = c.id
    JOIN nxt_promotion p ON c.promotion_id = p.id
    JOIN "Belts" b ON m.title_id = b.id
    WHERE m.title_change = 0                     -- exclude title changes
      AND m.duration != ''                       -- exclude missing durations
      AND LOWER(b.name) LIKE '%nxt%'            -- only NXT championships
  ),
  -- Step 3: Convert the duration (MM:SS) to total seconds for comparison
  match_durations AS (
    SELECT m.*,
           CAST(SUBSTR(m.duration, 1, INSTR(m.duration, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60 +
           CAST(SUBSTR(m.duration, INSTR(m.duration, ':') + 1) AS INTEGER) AS duration_seconds
    FROM nxt_matches m
  ),
  -- Step 4: Pick the match with the smallest duration (shortest)
  shortest_match AS (
    SELECT * FROM match_durations
    ORDER BY duration_seconds ASC
    LIMIT 1
  )
-- Step 5: Retrieve the names of the two wrestlers involved
SELECT w1.name AS winner_name,
       w2.name AS loser_name
FROM shortest_match sm
JOIN "Wrestlers" w1 ON sm.winner_id = w1.id
JOIN "Wrestlers" w2 ON sm.loser_id = w2.id;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH title_matches AS (
    SELECT 
        m."id" AS match_id,
        m."duration_seconds",
        t."name" AS title_name
    FROM "Matches" m
    INNER JOIN "title" t ON m."title_id" = t."id"
    INNER JOIN "Match_Types" mt ON m."match_type_id" = mt."id"
    WHERE t."name" LIKE '%NXT%'
      AND LOWER(mt."name") NOT LIKE LOWER('%title change%')
      AND m."duration_seconds" IS NOT NULL
),
shortest_match AS (
    SELECT 
        match_id,
        duration_seconds,
        title_name
    FROM title_matches
    ORDER BY duration_seconds ASC
    LIMIT 1
)
SELECT 
    w."name" AS wrestler_name
FROM shortest_match sm
INNER JOIN "Match_Wrestlers" mw ON sm.match_id = mw."match_id"
INNER JOIN "Wrestlers" w ON mw."wrestler_id" = w."id"
ORDER BY w."name";
```

### 38. local031 (DB: `Brazilian_E_Commerce`)
**Question**: What is the highest monthly delivered orders volume in the year with the lowest annual delivered orders volume among 2016, 2017, and 2018?

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Extract year and month from delivery dates for delivered orders in 2016-2018
WITH delivered_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        "order_id",
        CAST(strftime('%Y', "order_delivered_customer_date") AS INTEGER) AS "year",
        CAST(strftime('%m', "order_delivered_customer_date") AS INTEGER) AS "month"
    FROM "olist_orders"
    WHERE "order_status" = 'delivered'
      AND "order_delivered_customer_date" IS NOT NULL
      AND CAST(strftime('%Y', "order_delivered_customer_date") AS INTEGER) IN (2016, 2017, 2018)
),

-- Step 2: Compute annual delivered orders volume
annual_volumes AS (
    SELECT 
        "year",
        COUNT("order_id") AS "annual_volume"
    FROM delivered_orders
    GROUP BY "year"
),

-- Step 3: Identify the year with the lowest annual volume
lowest_year AS (
    SELECT "year"
    FROM annual_volumes
    ORDER BY "annual_volume" ASC
    LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 4: Compute monthly volumes for that year
monthly_volumes AS (
    SELECT 
        "month",
        COUNT("order_id") AS "monthly_volume"
    FROM delivered_orders
    WHERE "year" = (SELECT "year" FROM lowest_year)
    GROUP BY "month"
)

-- Step 5: Get the highest monthly volume
SELECT MAX("monthly_volume") AS "highest_monthly_delivered_orders_volume"
FROM monthly_volumes;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify the year with the lowest annual delivered orders volume among 2016, 2017, 2018
WITH annual_volumes AS (
    SELECT 
        CAST(strftime('%Y', o."order_delivered_customer_date") AS INTEGER) AS "year",
        COUNT(DISTINCT o."order_id") AS "annual_volume"
    FROM "olist_orders" o
    WHERE 
        o."order_delivered_customer_date" IS NOT NULL
        AND CAST(strftime('%Y', o."order_delivered_customer_date") AS INTEGER) IN (2016, 2017, 2018)
    GROUP BY "year"
),
-- Step 2: Find the year with the minimum annual volume
min_year AS (
    SELECT "year"
    FROM annual_volumes
    ORDER BY "annual_volume" ASC
    LIMIT 1
),
-- Step 3: Calculate monthly delivered orders volume for that year
monthly_volumes AS (
    SELECT 
        strftime('%Y-%m', o."order_delivered_customer_date") AS "month",
        COUNT(DISTINCT o."order_id") AS "monthly_volume"
    FROM "olist_orders" o
    WHERE 
        o."order_delivered_customer_date" IS NOT NULL
        AND CAST(strftime('%Y', o."order_delivered_customer_date") AS INTEGER) = (SELECT "year" FROM min_year)
    GROUP BY "month"
)
-- Step 4: Return the highest monthly volume with the month
SELECT "monthly_volume", "month"
FROM monthly_volumes
ORDER BY "monthly_volume" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify unicorn companies with their founding year and industry
WITH unicorn_companies AS (
    SELECT
        cd.company_id,
        cd.date_joined,
        ci.industry
    FROM companies_dates cd
    JOIN companies_funding cf ON cd.company_id = cf.company_id
    JOIN companies_industries ci ON cd.company_id = ci.company_id
    WHERE cf.valuation >= 1000000000  -- Unicorn threshold: $1B
      AND strftime('%Y', cd.date_joined) BETWEEN '2019' AND '2021'
),
-- Step 2: Count new unicorns per industry per year
counts_per_industry_year AS (
    SELECT
        industry,
        strftime('%Y', date_joined) AS year,
        COUNT(DISTINCT company_id) AS cnt
    FROM unicorn_companies
    GROUP BY industry, year
),
-- Step 3: Sum counts across 2019-2021 for each industry to find the top
total_counts_per_industry AS (
    SELECT
        industry,
        SUM(cnt) AS total_count
    FROM counts_per_industry_year
    GROUP BY industry
),
-- Step 4: Identify the top industry (highest total count; if tie, pick alphabetically)
top_industry AS (
    SELECT industry
    FROM total_counts_per_industry
    ORDER BY total_count DESC, industry ASC
    LIMIT 1
)
-- Step 5: Compute average new unicorns per year for the top industry (2019-2021)
SELECT ROUND(SUM(cnt) / 3.0, 4) AS avg_new_unicorns_per_year
FROM counts_per_industry_year
WHERE industry = (SELECT industry FROM top_industry)
  AND year BETWEEN '2019' AND '2021';
```
</details>

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Count total new unicorns per industry from 2019 to 2021
WITH "industry_totals" AS (
    SELECT
        "industry",
        COUNT(*) AS "total_new_unicorns"
    FROM "unicorn_company"
    WHERE "year" BETWEEN 2019 AND 2021
    GROUP BY "industry"
),
-- Step 2: Identify the top industry (highest total count)
"top_industry" AS (
    SELECT "industry"
    FROM "industry_totals"
    ORDER BY "total_new_unicorns" DESC NULLS LAST
    LIMIT 1
)
-- Step 3: Compute average per year for the top industry (total over 3 years divided by 3)
SELECT
    "industry_totals"."industry",
    ROUND("industry_totals"."total_new_unicorns" / 3.0, 4) AS "avg_per_year"
FROM "industry_totals"
JOIN "top_industry"
    ON "industry_totals"."industry" = "top_industry"."industry";
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter sales for France, promo_total_id=1, channel_total_id=1, years 2019/2020
WITH filtered_sales AS (
    SELECT
        s."prod_id",
        t."calendar_month_number" AS "month",
        t."calendar_year" AS "year",
        s."amount_sold"
    FROM "sales" AS s
    JOIN "times" AS t ON s."time_id" = t."time_id"
    JOIN "customers" AS c ON s."cust_id" = c."cust_id"
    JOIN "countries" AS co ON c."country_id" = co."country_id"
    JOIN "promotions" AS p ON s."promo_id" = p."promo_id"
    JOIN "channels" AS ch ON s."channel_id" = ch."channel_id"
    WHERE LOWER(co."country_name") = LOWER('France')
      AND p."promo_total_id" = 1
      AND ch."channel_total_id" = 1
      AND t."calendar_year" IN (2019, 2020)
),
-- Step 2: Aggregate sales per product, month, year
agg_sales AS (
    SELECT
        "prod_id",
        "month",
        "year",
        SUM("amount_sold") AS "total_sales"
    FROM filtered_sales
    GROUP BY "prod_id", "month", "year"
),
-- Step 3: Pivot to get sales for 2019 and 2020 per product-month
pivot_sales AS (
    SELECT
        "prod_id",
        "month",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "year" = 2019 THEN "total_sales" END) AS "sales_2019",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "year" = 2020 THEN "total_sales" END) AS "sales_2020"
    FROM agg_sales
    GROUP BY "prod_id", "month"
),
-- Step 4: Project 2021 sales using the given growth formula
projected AS (
    SELECT
        "prod_id",
        "month",
        CASE
            WHEN "sales_2019" IS NOT NULL AND "sales_2019" > 0
            THEN ((("sales_2020" - "sales_2019") / "sales_2019") * "sales_2020") + "sales_2020"
            ELSE NULL
        END AS "projected_sales_local"
    FROM pivot_sales
),
-- Step 5: Convert to USD using currency rates for France, year=2021
projected_usd AS (
    SELECT
        pr."prod_id",
        pr."month",
        ROUND(pr."projected_sales_local" * COALESCE(cr."to_us", 1), 2) AS "projected_sales_usd"
    FROM projected AS pr
    LEFT JOIN "currency" AS cr
        ON cr."month" = pr."month"
        AND cr."year" = 2021
        AND LOWER(cr."country") = LOWER('France')
    WHERE pr."projected_sales_local" IS NOT NULL  -- exclude invalid projections (division by zero)
),
-- Step 6: Compute monthly averages across all products
monthly_avg AS (
    SELECT
        "month",
        ROUND(AVG("projected_sales_usd"), 2) AS "avg_monthly_sales"
    FROM projected_usd
    GROUP BY "month"
),
-- Step 7: Calculate median of the twelve monthly averages
median_calc AS (
    SELECT
        "avg_monthly_sales",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "avg_monthly_sales") AS "rn",
        COUNT(*) OVER () AS "cnt"
    FROM monthly_avg
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG("avg_monthly_sales"), 2) AS "median_of_monthly_avg_projected_sales_usd"
FROM median_calc
WHERE "rn" IN (("cnt" + 1) / 2, ("cnt" + 2) / 2);
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Step 1: Aggregate sales for France in 2019 and 2020 with filters
  filtered_sales AS (
    SELECT
      s."prod_id" AS "product_id",
      s."mth" AS "month",
      s."year",
      SUM(s."sales_amount") AS total_sales
    FROM "sales" s
    JOIN "countries" c ON s."country_id" = c."country_id"
    WHERE c."country_name" = 'France'
      AND s."promo_total_id" = 1
      AND s."channel_total_id" = 1
      AND s."year" IN (2019, 2020)
    GROUP BY s."prod_id", s."mth", s."year"
  ),

  -- Step 2: Separate 2019 and 2020 sales per product and month
  sales_2019 AS (
    SELECT "product_id", "month", "total_sales" AS sales_2019
    FROM filtered_sales
    WHERE "year" = 2019
  ),
  sales_2020 AS (
    SELECT "product_id", "month", "total_sales" AS sales_2020
    FROM filtered_sales
    WHERE "year" = 2020
  ),

  -- Step 3: Combine and compute projected 2021 sales in local currency (EUR)
  projected_2021_eur AS (
    SELECT
      COALESCE(s19."product_id", s20."product_id") AS "product_id",
      COALESCE(s19."month", s20."month") AS "month",
      CASE
        WHEN s19."sales_2019" > 0 THEN
          ROUND(CAST(s20."sales_2020" AS REAL) * CAST(s20."sales_2020" AS REAL) / CAST(s19."sales_2019" AS REAL), 4)
        WHEN s19."sales_2019" IS NULL THEN NULL
        ELSE s20."sales_2020"
      END AS projected_2021_eur
    FROM sales_2019 s19
    FULL OUTER JOIN sales_2020 s20
      ON s19."product_id" = s20."product_id" AND s19."month" = s20."month"
    WHERE s19."sales_2019" IS NOT NULL OR s20."sales_2020" IS NOT NULL
  ),

  -- Step 4: Convert to USD using monthly exchange rates (default 1 if missing)
  projected_2021_usd AS (
    SELECT
      p."product_id",
      p."month",
      ROUND(p."projected_2021_eur" * COALESCE(cr."rate", 1), 4) AS projected_usd
    FROM projected_2021_eur p
    LEFT JOIN "currency" cr
      ON cr."currency_code" = 'EUR'
        AND cr."year" = 2021
        AND cr."month" = p."month"
    WHERE p."projected_2021_eur" IS NOT NULL
  ),

  -- Step 5: Compute average projected sales per month across all products
  monthly_avg AS (
    SELECT
      "month",
      ROUND(AVG("projected_usd"), 4) AS avg_projected_usd
    FROM projected_2021_usd
    GROUP BY "month"
  ),

  -- Step 6: Compute median of the 12 monthly averages
  ranked AS (
    SELECT
      "avg_projected_usd",
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "avg_projected_usd") AS rn,
      COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_cnt
    FROM monthly_avg
  )
SELECT
  ROUND(AVG("avg_projected_usd"), 4) AS median_avg_projected_usd
FROM ranked
WHERE "rn" IN ((total_cnt + 1) / 2, (total_cnt + 2) / 2);
```
</details>

### 41. local202 (DB: `city_legislation`)

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute per-state alien statistics (total, friendly, hostile, average age)
WITH state_stats AS (
    SELECT
        "state",
        COUNT(*) AS total_aliens,
        SUM(CASE WHEN "aggressive" = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS friendly_count,
        SUM(CASE WHEN "aggressive" = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS hostile_count,
        AVG("age") AS avg_age
    FROM "alien_data"
    GROUP BY "state"
),
-- Step 2: Rank states by total alien population descending
ranked_states AS (
    SELECT
        "state",
        total_aliens,
        friendly_count,
        hostile_count,
        avg_age,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY total_aliens DESC) AS rn
    FROM state_stats
)
-- Step 3 & 4: Filter top 10, apply conditions, count matching states
SELECT COUNT(*) AS matching_states_count
FROM ranked_states
WHERE rn <= 10
  AND friendly_count > hostile_count   -- friendly percentage > hostile percentage
  AND avg_age > 200;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "state_aggregates" AS (
  SELECT
    "state",
    COUNT(*) AS "total_pop",
    COUNT(CASE WHEN LOWER("type") = 'friendly' THEN 1 END) AS "friendly_count",
    COUNT(CASE WHEN LOWER("type") = 'hostile' THEN 1 END) AS "hostile_count",
    AVG("age") AS "avg_age"
  FROM "aliens"
  GROUP BY "state"
),
"top10_states" AS (
  SELECT
    "state",
    "total_pop",
    "friendly_count",
    "hostile_count",
    "avg_age",
    ROUND(("friendly_count" * 100.0 / NULLIF("total_pop", 0)), 4) AS "friendly_pct",
    ROUND(("hostile_count" * 100.0 / NULLIF("total_pop", 0)), 4) AS "hostile_pct"
  FROM "state_aggregates"
  ORDER BY "total_pop" DESC, "state" ASC
  LIMIT 10
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS "count"
FROM "top10_states"
WHERE "friendly_pct" > "hostile_pct"
  AND "avg_age" > 200;
```
</details>

<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   avg_loss_rate |   items_below_1std |   items_within_1std |   items_above_1std |

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Get distinct wholesale item loss rates
wholesale_loss_rates AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT lr."item_code", lr."loss_rate_%"
    FROM "veg_loss_rate_df" lr
    INNER JOIN "veg_whsle_df" w ON lr."item_code" = w."item_code"
),
-- Compute average and variance (population variance)
stats AS (
    SELECT 
        AVG(lr."loss_rate_%") AS avg_loss_rate,
        AVG((lr."loss_rate_%" - avg_calc.avg_val) * (lr."loss_rate_%" - avg_calc.avg_val)) AS variance_loss_rate
    FROM wholesale_loss_rates lr
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT AVG("loss_rate_%") AS avg_val FROM wholesale_loss_rates) avg_calc
),
-- Categorize each item relative to 1 standard deviation (using variance instead of std dev)
categorized AS (
    SELECT 
        lr."item_code",
        lr."loss_rate_%",
        (lr."loss_rate_%" - s.avg_loss_rate) AS dev,
        CASE 
            WHEN (lr."loss_rate_%" - s.avg_loss_rate) * (lr."loss_rate_%" - s.avg_loss_rate) <= s.variance_loss_rate THEN 'Within'
            WHEN (lr."loss_rate_%" - s.avg_loss_rate) > 0 THEN 'Above'
            ELSE 'Below'
        END AS deviation_category
    FROM wholesale_loss_rates lr
    CROSS JOIN stats s
)
-- Final summary: average loss rate + counts per category
SELECT 
    ROUND((SELECT avg_loss_rate FROM stats), 4) AS avg_loss_rate,
    SUM(CASE WHEN deviation_category = 'Below' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS items_below_1std,
    SUM(CASE WHEN deviation_category = 'Within' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS items_within_1std,
    SUM(CASE WHEN deviation_category = 'Above' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS items_above_1std
FROM categorized;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH avg_std AS (
    SELECT 
        ROUND(AVG(loss_rate), 4) AS avg_loss,
        ROUND(SQRT(AVG(loss_rate * loss_rate) - AVG(loss_rate) * AVG(loss_rate)), 4) AS std_loss
    FROM veg_whsle_data
    WHERE loss_rate IS NOT NULL
),
counts AS (
    SELECT
        SUM(CASE WHEN loss_rate < (SELECT avg_loss - std_loss FROM avg_std) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_below,
        SUM(CASE WHEN loss_rate BETWEEN (SELECT avg_loss - std_loss FROM avg_std) 
                                        AND (SELECT avg_loss + std_loss FROM avg_std) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_within,
        SUM(CASE WHEN loss_rate > (SELECT avg_loss + std_loss FROM avg_std) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_above
    FROM veg_whsle_data
    WHERE loss_rate IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
    (SELECT avg_loss FROM avg_std) AS average_loss_rate,
    count_below,
    count_within,
    count_above
FROM counts;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Generate summary of monthly closing balances per customer
-- Includes months with no activity by filling the full date range

WITH
-- Step 1: Determine overall date range from transaction table
date_range AS (
  SELECT
    date(MIN(txn_date), 'start of month') AS first_month,
    date(MAX(txn_date), 'start of month') AS last_month
  FROM customer_transactions
),
-- Step 2: Recursively generate all months in the range
months AS (
  SELECT first_month AS month_start FROM date_range
  UNION ALL
  SELECT date(month_start, '+1 month')
  FROM months
  WHERE month_start < (SELECT last_month FROM date_range)
),
-- Step 3: Unique customers who have at least one transaction
customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
  FROM customer_transactions
),
-- Step 4: Cartesian product to ensure every customer has a row for every month
customer_months AS (
  SELECT c.customer_id, m.month_start
  FROM customers c
  CROSS JOIN months m
),
-- Step 5: Compute net change per customer per month (deposits positive, others negative)
monthly_net AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date, 'start of month') AS txn_month,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) AS net_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id, txn_month
)
-- Step 6: Final output with cumulative closing balance
SELECT
  cm.customer_id,
  cm.month_start,
  COALESCE(mn.net_amount, 0) AS monthly_change,
  SUM(COALESCE(mn.net_amount, 0)) OVER (
    PARTITION BY cm.customer_id
    ORDER BY cm.month_start
  ) AS closing_balance
FROM customer_months cm
LEFT JOIN monthly_net mn
  ON cm.customer_id = mn.customer_id AND cm.month_start = mn.txn_month
ORDER BY cm.customer_id, cm.month_start;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE "months" AS (
  SELECT DATE('2020-01-01') AS "month_start"
  UNION ALL
  SELECT DATE("month_start", '+1 month')
  FROM "months"
  WHERE "month_start" < DATE('2024-12-01')
),
"unique_customers" AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT COALESCE(CAST("event_type" AS INTEGER) % 10 + 1, 1) AS "customer_id"
  FROM "shopping_cart_event_identifier"
),
"customer_months" AS (
  SELECT "c"."customer_id", "m"."month_start"
  FROM "unique_customers" "c"
  CROSS JOIN "months" "m"
),
"monthly_summary" AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(CAST("event_type" AS INTEGER) % 10 + 1, 1) AS "customer_id",
    DATE('2020-01-01') AS "month_start",
    ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(CAST("event_type" AS REAL), 0)), 4) AS "net_amount"
  FROM "shopping_cart_event_identifier"
  GROUP BY COALESCE(CAST("event_type" AS INTEGER) % 10 + 1, 1)
)
SELECT DISTINCT
  "cm"."customer_id",
  "cm"."month_start" AS "month",
  COALESCE(ROUND("ms"."net_amount", 4), 0) AS "monthly_change",
  ROUND(SUM(COALESCE("ms"."net_amount", 0)) OVER (
    PARTITION BY "cm"."customer_id"
    ORDER BY "cm"."month_start"
  ), 4) AS "cumulative_balance"
FROM "customer_months" "cm"
LEFT JOIN "monthly_summary" "ms"
  ON "cm"."customer_id" = "ms"."customer_id"
ORDER BY "cm"."customer_id", "cm"."month_start";
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Define the Magnificent 7 tickers
magnificent_tickers AS (
    SELECT 'AAPL' AS "ticker"
    UNION ALL SELECT 'MSFT'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'GOOGL'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'AMZN'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'META'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'NVDA'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'TSLA'
),

-- Get all post-market close prices for these tickers in the first half of 2024
post_market_prices AS (
    SELECT
        sp."TICKER",
        sp."DATE",
        sp."VALUE"
    FROM FINANCE__ECONOMICS.CYBERSYN.STOCK_PRICE_TIMESERIES sp
    WHERE sp."VARIABLE" = 'post-market_close'
      AND sp."TICKER" IN (SELECT "ticker" FROM magnificent_tickers)
      AND sp."DATE" >= '2024-01-01'
      AND sp."DATE" <= '2024-06-30'
),

-- Find the first and last trading day in the period for each ticker
start_end_dates AS (
    SELECT
        "TICKER" AS "ticker",
        MIN("DATE") AS "start_date",
        MAX("DATE") AS "end_date"
    FROM post_market_prices
    GROUP BY "TICKER"
),

-- Get the actual price values on those dates
start_prices AS (
    SELECT
        se."ticker",
        se."start_date",
        p."VALUE" AS "start_value"
    FROM start_end_dates se
    JOIN post_market_prices p
        ON se."ticker" = p."TICKER" AND se."start_date" = p."DATE"
),

end_prices AS (
    SELECT
        se."ticker",
        se."end_date",
        p."VALUE" AS "end_value"
    FROM start_end_dates se
    JOIN post_market_prices p
        ON se."ticker" = p."TICKER" AND se."end_date" = p."DATE"
)

-- Compute percentage change: ((end - start) / start) * 100
SELECT
    sp."ticker",
    sp."start_date",
    sp."start_value",
    ep."end_date",
    ep."end_value",
    ROUND((ep."end_value" - sp."start_value") / NULLIF(sp."start_value", 0) * 100, 4) AS "percentage_change"
FROM start_prices sp
JOIN end_prices ep ON sp."ticker" = ep."ticker"
ORDER BY sp."ticker";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Identify the Magnificent 7 companies (ticker symbols)
"magnificent_7" AS (
    SELECT 'AAPL' AS "ticker", 'Apple Inc.' AS "company"
    UNION ALL SELECT 'AMZN', 'Amazon.com Inc.'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'GOOGL', 'Alphabet Inc.'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'META', 'Meta Platforms Inc.'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'MSFT', 'Microsoft Corporation'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'NVDA', 'NVIDIA Corporation'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'TSLA', 'Tesla Inc.'
),

-- Step 2: Get the latest post-market close price before or on Jan 1, 2024
"start_prices" AS (
    SELECT 
        m."ticker",
        m."company",
        p."price" AS "start_price"
    FROM "magnificent_7" m
    JOIN "FINANCIAL_SECURITY_PRICES" p
        ON m."ticker" = p."ticker"
    WHERE p."market_close_type" = 'POST_MARKET'
      AND p."date" <= '2024-01-01'
    QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY m."ticker" ORDER BY p."date" DESC) = 1
),

-- Step 3: Get the latest post-market close price before or on June 30, 2024
"end_prices" AS (
    SELECT 
        m."ticker",
        m."company",
        p."price" AS "end_price"
    FROM "magnificent_7" m
    JOIN "FINANCIAL_SECURITY_PRICES" p
        ON m."ticker" = p."ticker"
    WHERE p."market_close_type" = 'POST_MARKET'
      AND p."date" <= '2024-06-30'
    QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY m."ticker" ORDER BY p."date" DESC) = 1
)

-- Step 4: Calculate percentage change
SELECT 
    s."company",
    ROUND(((e."end_price" - s."start_price") / s."start_price") * 100, 4) AS "percentage_change"
FROM "start_prices" s
JOIN "end_prices" e
    ON s."ticker" = e."ticker"
ORDER BY "percentage_change" DESC;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Analyze push notification engagement on June 1, 2023 between 08:00 and 09:00 UTC
-- using Unix timestamp filter on the TIME column for consistency across all event tables.
WITH send_events AS (
    SELECT 
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED",
        CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS "CARRIER",
        CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS "BROWSER",
        CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS "DEVICE_MODEL",
        'send' AS event_type
    FROM BRAZE_USER_EVENT_DEMO_DATASET.PUBLIC.USERS_MESSAGES_PUSHNOTIFICATION_SEND_VIEW
    WHERE "TIME" >= 1685606400 AND "TIME" < 1685610000  -- 2023-06-01 08:00:00 UTC to 09:00:00 UTC
),
bounce_events AS (
    SELECT 
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED",
        CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS "CARRIER",
        CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS "BROWSER",
        CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS "DEVICE_MODEL",
        'bounce' AS event_type
    FROM BRAZE_USER_EVENT_DEMO_DATASET.PUBLIC.USERS_MESSAGES_PUSHNOTIFICATION_BOUNCE_VIEW
    WHERE "TIME" >= 1685606400 AND "TIME" < 1685610000
),
open_events AS (
    SELECT 
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED",
        "CARRIER",
        "BROWSER",
        "DEVICE_MODEL",
        'open' AS event_type
    FROM BRAZE_USER_EVENT_DEMO_DATASET.PUBLIC.USERS_MESSAGES_PUSHNOTIFICATION_OPEN_VIEW
    WHERE "TIME" >= 1685606400 AND "TIME" < 1685610000
),
influenced_open_events AS (
    SELECT 
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED",  -- column not present in this table
        "CARRIER",
        "BROWSER",
        "DEVICE_MODEL",
        'influenced_open' AS event_type
    FROM BRAZE_USER_EVENT_DEMO_DATASET.PUBLIC.USERS_MESSAGES_PUSHNOTIFICATION_INFLUENCEDOPEN_VIEW
    WHERE "TIME" >= 1685606400 AND "TIME" < 1685610000
),
combined AS (
    SELECT * FROM send_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM bounce_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM open_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM influenced_open_events
)
SELECT
    "APP_GROUP_ID",
    "CAMPAIGN_ID",
    "USER_ID",
    "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
    "PLATFORM",
    "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED",
    "CARRIER",
    "BROWSER",
    "DEVICE_MODEL",
    COUNT(CASE WHEN event_type = 'send' THEN 1 END) AS push_notification_sends,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN event_type = 'send' THEN "USER_ID" END) AS unique_push_notification_sends,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN event_type = 'bounce' THEN 1 END) AS push_notification_bounced,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN event_type = 'bounce' THEN "USER_ID" END) AS unique_push_notification_bounced,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN event_type = 'open' THEN 1 END) AS push_notification_open,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN event_type = 'open' THEN "USER_ID" END) AS unique_push_notification_opened,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN event_type = 'influenced_open' THEN 1 END) AS push_notification_influenced_open,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN event_type = 'influenced_open' THEN "USER_ID" END) AS unique_push_notification_influenced_open
FROM combined
GROUP BY 
    "APP_GROUP_ID",
    "CAMPAIGN_ID",
    "USER_ID",
    "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
    "PLATFORM",
    "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED",
    "CARRIER",
    "BROWSER",
    "DEVICE_MODEL"
ORDER BY 
    "APP_GROUP_ID", "CAMPAIGN_ID", "USER_ID", "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID";
```
