```sql
-- Analyze push notification engagement on June 1, 2023 between 08:00 and 09:00 UTC
-- Timestamps: 08:00 UTC = 1685606400, 09:00 UTC = 1685610000

WITH 
send_events AS (
    SELECT
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "TIME"
    FROM BRAZE_USER_EVENT_DEMO_DATASET.PUBLIC.USERS_MESSAGES_PUSHNOTIFICATION_SEND_VIEW
    WHERE "TIME" >= 1685606400 AND "TIME" < 1685610000
),

bounce_events AS (
    SELECT
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "TIME"
    FROM BRAZE_USER_EVENT_DEMO_DATASET.PUBLIC.USERS_MESSAGES_PUSHNOTIFICATION_BOUNCE_VIEW
    WHERE "TIME" >= 1685606400 AND "TIME" < 1685610000
),

open_events AS (
    SELECT
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "DEVICE_MODEL",
        "CARRIER",
        "BROWSER",
        "TIME"
    FROM BRAZE_USER_EVENT_DEMO_DATASET.PUBLIC.USERS_MESSAGES_PUSHNOTIFICATION_OPEN_VIEW
    WHERE "TIME" >= 1685606400 AND "TIME" < 1685610000
),

influenced_open_events AS (
    SELECT
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "DEVICE_MODEL",
        "CARRIER",
        "BROWSER",
        "TIME"
    FROM BRAZE_USER_EVENT_DEMO_DATASET.PUBLIC.USERS_MESSAGES_PUSHNOTIFICATION_INFLUENCEDOPEN_VIEW
    WHERE "TIME" >= 1685606400 AND "TIME" < 1685610000
),

-- Aggregate counts per unique combination of grouping keys
send_agg AS (
    SELECT
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        NULL::TEXT AS "DEVICE_MODEL",
        NULL::TEXT AS "CARRIER",
        NULL::TEXT AS "BROWSER",
        COUNT(*) AS "TOTAL_SENDS",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "USER_ID") AS "UNIQUE_SENDS"
    FROM send_events
    GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
),

bounce_agg AS (
    SELECT
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        NULL::TEXT AS "DEVICE_MODEL",
        NULL::TEXT AS "CARRIER",
        NULL::TEXT AS "BROWSER",
        COUNT(*) AS "TOTAL_BOUNCES",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "USER_ID") AS "UNIQUE_BOUNCES"
    FROM bounce_events
    GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
),

open_agg AS (
    SELECT
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "DEVICE_MODEL",
        "CARRIER",
        "BROWSER",
        COUNT(*) AS "TOTAL_OPENS",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "USER_ID") AS "UNIQUE_OPENS"
    FROM open_events
    GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8
),

influenced_open_agg AS (
    SELECT
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "DEVICE_MODEL",
        "CARRIER",
        "BROWSER",
        COUNT(*) AS "TOTAL_INFLUENCED_OPENS",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "USER_ID") AS "UNIQUE_INFLUENCED_OPENS"
    FROM influenced_open_events
    GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8
),

-- Combine all distinct grouping keys
all_keys AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        NULL::TEXT AS "DEVICE_MODEL",
        NULL::TEXT AS "CARRIER",
        NULL::TEXT AS "BROWSER"
    FROM send_events
    UNION
    SELECT DISTINCT
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        NULL::TEXT,
        NULL::TEXT,
        NULL::TEXT
    FROM bounce_events
    UNION
    SELECT DISTINCT
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "DEVICE_MODEL",
        "CARRIER",
        "BROWSER"
    FROM open_events
    UNION
    SELECT DISTINCT
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "DEVICE_MODEL",
        "CARRIER",
        "BROWSER"
    FROM influenced_open_events
)

-- Final result: left join aggregated metrics onto the key set
SELECT
    k."APP_GROUP_ID",
    k."CAMPAIGN_ID",
    k."USER_ID",
    k."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
    k."PLATFORM",
    k."DEVICE_MODEL",
    k."CARRIER",
    k."BROWSER",
    COALESCE(s."TOTAL_SENDS", 0) AS "PUSH_NOTIFICATION_SENDS",
    COALESCE(s."UNIQUE_SENDS", 0) AS "UNIQUE_PUSH_NOTIFICATION_SENDS",
    COALESCE(b."TOTAL_BOUNCES", 0) AS "PUSH_NOTIFICATION_BOUNCED",
    COALESCE(b."UNIQUE_BOUNCES", 0) AS "UNIQUE_PUSH_NOTIFICATION_BOUNCED",
    COALESCE(o."TOTAL_OPENS", 0) AS "PUSH_NOTIFICATION_OPEN",
    COALESCE(o."UNIQUE_OPENS", 0) AS "UNIQUE_PUSH_NOTIFICATION_OPENED",
    COALESCE(io."TOTAL_INFLUENCED_OPENS", 0) AS "PUSH_NOTIFICATION_INFLUENCED_OPEN",
    COALESCE(io."UNIQUE_INFLUENCED_OPENS", 0) AS "UNIQUE_PUSH_NOTIFICATION_INFLUENCED_OPEN"
FROM all_keys k
LEFT JOIN send_agg s
    ON  k."APP_GROUP_ID" = s."APP_GROUP_ID"
    AND k."USER_ID" = s."USER_ID"
    AND k."CAMPAIGN_ID" = s."CAMPAIGN_ID"
    AND k."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID" = s."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID"
    AND k."PLATFORM" = s."PLATFORM"
    AND (k."DEVICE_MODEL" IS NULL AND s."DEVICE_MODEL" IS NULL)
    AND (k."CARRIER" IS NULL AND s."CARRIER" IS NULL)
    AND (k."BROWSER" IS NULL AND s."BROWSER" IS NULL)
LEFT JOIN bounce_agg b
    ON  k."APP_GROUP_ID" = b."APP_GROUP_ID"
    AND k."USER_ID" = b."USER_ID"
    AND k."CAMPAIGN_ID" = b."CAMPAIGN_ID"
    AND k."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID" = b."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID"
    AND k."PLATFORM" = b."PLATFORM"
    AND (k."DEVICE_MODEL" IS NULL AND b."DEVICE_MODEL" IS NULL)
    AND (k."CARRIER" IS NULL AND b."CARRIER" IS NULL)
    AND (k."BROWSER" IS NULL AND b."BROWSER" IS NULL)
LEFT JOIN open_agg o
    ON  k."APP_GROUP_ID" = o."APP_GROUP_ID"
    AND k."USER_ID" = o."USER_ID"
    AND k."CAMPAIGN_ID" = o."CAMPAIGN_ID"
    AND k."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID" = o."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID"
    AND k."PLATFORM" = o."PLATFORM"
    AND (k."DEVICE_MODEL" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM o."DEVICE_MODEL")
    AND (k."CARRIER" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM o."CARRIER")
    AND (k."BROWSER" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM o."BROWSER")
LEFT JOIN influenced_open_agg io
    ON  k."APP_GROUP_ID" = io."APP_GROUP_ID"
    AND k."USER_ID" = io."USER_ID"
    AND k."CAMPAIGN_ID" = io."CAMPAIGN_ID"
    AND k."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID" = io."MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID"
    AND k."PLATFORM" = io."PLATFORM"
    AND (k."DEVICE_MODEL" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM io."DEVICE_MODEL")
    AND (k."CARRIER" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM io."CARRIER")
    AND (k."BROWSER" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM io."BROWSER")
ORDER BY
    "APP_GROUP_ID", "CAMPAIGN_ID", "USER_ID", "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
    "PLATFORM", "DEVICE_MODEL", "CARRIER", "BROWSER";
```
</details>

```sql
WITH 
-- Generate hourly slots for October 1, 2022 (local time assumed CDT)
hourly_slots AS (
    SELECT 
        DATEADD(HOUR, SEQ8(), '2022-10-01 00:00:00'::TIMESTAMP_NTZ) AS "datetime"
    FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 24))
),

-- Price node metadata
price_node_info AS (
    SELECT 
        "OBJECTID" AS "price_node_id",
        "PNODENAME" AS "price_node_name"
    FROM "YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA"."YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE"."PRICE_NODES_SAMPLE"
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000697078
),

-- Load zone metadata
load_zone_info AS (
    SELECT 
        "OBJECTID" AS "load_zone_id",
        "OBJECTNAME" AS "load_zone_name"
    FROM "YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA"."YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE"."DS_OBJECT_LIST_SAMPLE"
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
),

-- Hourly DART prices (DALMP and RTLMP)
price_data AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        "DALMP" AS "dalmp",
        "RTLMP" AS "rtlmp"
    FROM "YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA"."YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE"."DART_PRICES_SAMPLE"
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000697078
        AND "DATETIME" >= '2022-10-01 00:00:00'
        AND "DATETIME" < '2022-10-02 00:00:00'
),

-- Load forecasts (datatypeid 19060)
load_forecast_data AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",

    FROM "YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA"."YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE"."TS_FORECAST_SAMPLE"
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
        AND "DATATYPEID" = 19060
        AND "DATETIME" >= '2022-10-01 00:00:00'
        AND "DATETIME" < '2022-10-02 00:00:00'
),

-- Wind generation forecasts (datatypeid 9285)
wind_forecast_data AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        "VALUE" AS "wind_gen_forecast",
        "PUBLISHDATE" AS "wind_gen_forecast_publish_date"
    FROM "YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA"."YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE"."TS_FORECAST_SAMPLE"
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
        AND "DATATYPEID" = 9285
        AND "DATETIME" >= '2022-10-01 00:00:00'
        AND "DATETIME" < '2022-10-02 00:00:00'
),

-- Solar generation forecasts (datatypeid 662)
solar_forecast_data AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        "VALUE" AS "solar_gen_forecast",
        "PUBLISHDATE" AS "solar_gen_forecast_publish_date"
    FROM "YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA"."YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE"."TS_FORECAST_SAMPLE"
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
        AND "DATATYPEID" = 662
        AND "DATETIME" >= '2022-10-01 00:00:00'
        AND "DATETIME" < '2022-10-02 00:00:00'
),

-- Actual wind generation (datatypeid 16)
wind_actual_data AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        "VALUE" AS "wind_gen"
    FROM "YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA"."YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE"."TS_GEN_SAMPLE"
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
        AND "DATATYPEID" = 16
        AND "DATETIME" >= '2022-10-01 00:00:00'
        AND "DATETIME" < '2022-10-02 00:00:00'
),

-- Actual solar generation (datatypeid 650)
solar_actual_data AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        "VALUE" AS "solar_gen"
    FROM "YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA"."YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE"."TS_GEN_SAMPLE"
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
        AND "DATATYPEID" = 650
        AND "DATETIME" >= '2022-10-01 00:00:00'
        AND "DATETIME" < '2022-10-02 00:00:00'
),

-- Actual load (final settlement)
load_actual_data AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        "RTLOAD" AS "rtload"
    FROM "YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA"."YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE"."DART_LOADS_SAMPLE"
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
        AND "DATETIME" >= '2022-10-01 00:00:00'
        AND "DATETIME" < '2022-10-02 00:00:00'
        AND "RTFINAL" = 'Y'
),

-- Peak classifications from market times
peak_classification AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        "ONPEAK" AS "onpeak",
        "OFFPEAK" AS "offpeak",
        "WEPEAK" AS "wepeak",
        "WDPEAK" AS "wdpeak",
        "MARKETDAY" AS "marketday",
        "DATETIME_UTC" AS "datetime_utc"
    FROM "YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA"."YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE"."ISO_MARKET_TIMES_SAMPLE"
    WHERE "ISO" = 'ERCOT'
        AND "DATETIME" >= '2022-10-01 00:00:00'
        AND "DATETIME" < '2022-10-02 00:00:00'
),

-- Combine all data with the hourly calendar
combined_data AS (
    SELECT
        'ERCOT' AS "iso",
        h."datetime",
        COALESCE(p."timezone", lf."timezone", wf."timezone", sf."timezone",
                 wa."timezone", sa."timezone", la."timezone", pc."timezone", 'CDT') AS "timezone",
        pc."datetime_utc",
        COALESCE(pc."onpeak", 0) AS "onpeak",
        COALESCE(pc."offpeak", 0) AS "offpeak",
        COALESCE(pc."wepeak", 0) AS "wepeak",
        COALESCE(pc."wdpeak", 0) AS "wdpeak",
        pc."marketday",
        pni."price_node_name",
        pni."price_node_id",
        p."dalmp",
        p."rtlmp",
        lzi."load_zone_name",
        lzi."load_zone_id",
        lf."load_forecast",
        lf."load_forecast_publish_date",
        la."rtload",
        wf."wind_gen_forecast",
        wf."wind_gen_forecast_publish_date",
        wa."wind_gen",
        sf."solar_gen_forecast",
        sf."solar_gen_forecast_publish_date",
        sa."solar_gen"
    FROM hourly_slots h
    LEFT JOIN price_data p ON h."datetime" = p."datetime"
    LEFT JOIN load_forecast_data lf ON h."datetime" = lf."datetime"
    LEFT JOIN wind_forecast_data wf ON h."datetime" = wf."datetime"
    LEFT JOIN solar_forecast_data sf ON h."datetime" = sf."datetime"
    LEFT JOIN wind_actual_data wa ON h."datetime" = wa."datetime"
    LEFT JOIN solar_actual_data sa ON h."datetime" = sa."datetime"
    LEFT JOIN load_actual_data la ON h."datetime" = la."datetime"
    LEFT JOIN peak_classification pc ON h."datetime" = pc."datetime"
    CROSS JOIN price_node_info pni
    CROSS JOIN load_zone_info lzi
)

-- Final report with net load calculations
SELECT 
    "iso",
    "datetime",
    "timezone",
    "datetime_utc",
    "onpeak",
    "offpeak",
    "wepeak",
    "wdpeak",
    "marketday",
    "price_node_name",
    "price_node_id",
    ROUND("dalmp", 4) AS "dalmp",
    ROUND("rtlmp", 4) AS "rtlmp",
    "load_zone_name",
    "load_zone_id",
    ROUND("load_forecast", 4) AS "load_forecast",
    "load_forecast_publish_date",
    ROUND("rtload", 4) AS "rtload",
    ROUND("wind_gen_forecast", 4) AS "wind_gen_forecast",
    "wind_gen_forecast_publish_date",
    ROUND("wind_gen", 4) AS "wind_gen",
    ROUND("solar_gen_forecast", 4) AS "solar_gen_forecast",
    "solar_gen_forecast_publish_date",
    ROUND("solar_gen", 4) AS "solar_gen",
    -- Net load forecasts and real-time
    ROUND(COALESCE("load_forecast", 0) - COALESCE("wind_gen_forecast", 0) - COALESCE("solar_gen_forecast", 0), 4) AS "net_load_forecast",
    ROUND(COALESCE("rtload", 0) - COALESCE("wind_gen", 0) - COALESCE("solar_gen", 0), 4) AS "net_load_real_time"
FROM combined_data
ORDER BY "datetime" ASC;
```

```sql
WITH
price_cte AS (
    SELECT
        "datetime",
        "node_id" AS "price_node_id",
        "node_name" AS "price_node_name",
        "dalmp",
        "rtlmp"
    FROM "ERCOT"."PUBLIC"."PRICES"
    WHERE "node_id" = 10000697078
      AND "datetime" >= '2022-10-01 00:00:00'::TIMESTAMP_NTZ
      AND "datetime" <  '2022-10-02 00:00:00'::TIMESTAMP_NTZ
),
load_cte AS (
    SELECT
        "datetime",
        "load_zone_id",
        "load_zone_name",
        "load_forecast",
        "load_forecast_publish_date",
        "rtload"
    FROM "ERCOT"."PUBLIC"."LOAD"
    WHERE "load_zone_id" = 10000712973
      AND "datetime" >= '2022-10-01 00:00:00'::TIMESTAMP_NTZ
      AND "datetime" <  '2022-10-02 00:00:00'::TIMESTAMP_NTZ
),
wind_cte AS (
    SELECT
        "datetime",
        "wind_gen_forecast",
        "wind_gen_forecast_publish_date",
        "wind_gen"
    FROM "ERCOT"."PUBLIC"."WIND"
    WHERE "load_zone_id" = 10000712973
      AND "datetime" >= '2022-10-01 00:00:00'::TIMESTAMP_NTZ
      AND "datetime" <  '2022-10-02 00:00:00'::TIMESTAMP_NTZ
),
solar_cte AS (
    SELECT
        "datetime",
        "solar_gen_forecast",
        "solar_gen_forecast_publish_date",
        "solar_gen"
    FROM "ERCOT"."PUBLIC"."SOLAR"
    WHERE "load_zone_id" = 10000712973
      AND "datetime" >= '2022-10-01 00:00:00'::TIMESTAMP_NTZ
      AND "datetime" <  '2022-10-02 00:00:00'::TIMESTAMP_NTZ
),
combined AS (
    SELECT
        p."datetime",
        p."price_node_id",
        p."price_node_name",
        p."dalmp",
        p."rtlmp",
        l."load_zone_id",
        l."load_zone_name",
        l."load_forecast",
        l."load_forecast_publish_date",
        l."rtload",
        COALESCE(w."wind_gen_forecast", 0) AS "wind_gen_forecast",
        w."wind_gen_forecast_publish_date",
        COALESCE(w."wind_gen", 0) AS "wind_gen",
        COALESCE(s."solar_gen_forecast", 0) AS "solar_gen_forecast",
        s."solar_gen_forecast_publish_date",
        COALESCE(s."solar_gen", 0) AS "solar_gen"
    FROM price_cte p
    LEFT JOIN load_cte l ON p."datetime" = l."datetime"
    LEFT JOIN wind_cte w ON p."datetime" = w."datetime"
    LEFT JOIN solar_cte s ON p."datetime" = s."datetime"
)
SELECT
    'ERCOT' AS "iso",
    c."datetime" AS "datetime",
    'America/Chicago' AS "timezone",
    CONVERT_TIMEZONE('America/Chicago', c."datetime")::TIMESTAMP_TZ AS "datetime_utc",
    -- Peak classification flags (based on CST local time)
    CASE
        WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM CONVERT_TIMEZONE('America/Chicago', c."datetime")) BETWEEN 1 AND 5
             AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM CONVERT_TIMEZONE('America/Chicago', c."datetime")) BETWEEN 7 AND 22 THEN 1
        ELSE 0
    END AS "onpeak",
    CASE
        WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM CONVERT_TIMEZONE('America/Chicago', c."datetime")) BETWEEN 1 AND 5
             AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM CONVERT_TIMEZONE('America/Chicago', c."datetime")) BETWEEN 7 AND 22 THEN 0
        ELSE 1
    END AS "offpeak",
    CASE
        WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM CONVERT_TIMEZONE('America/Chicago', c."datetime")) IN (0,6) THEN 1
        ELSE 0
    END AS "wepeak",
    CASE
        WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM CONVERT_TIMEZONE('America/Chicago', c."datetime")) BETWEEN 1 AND 5
             AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM CONVERT_TIMEZONE('America/Chicago', c."datetime")) BETWEEN 7 AND 22 THEN 1
        ELSE 0
    END AS "wdpeak",
    DATE(c."datetime") AS "marketday",
    c."price_node_name",
    c."price_node_id",
    ROUND(c."dalmp", 4) AS "dalmp",
    ROUND(c."rtlmp", 4) AS "rtlmp",
    c."load_zone_name",
    c."load_zone_id",
    ROUND(c."load_forecast", 4) AS "load_forecast",
    c."load_forecast_publish_date",
    ROUND(c."rtload", 4) AS "rtload",
    ROUND(c."wind_gen_forecast", 4) AS "wind_gen_forecast",
    c."wind_gen_forecast_publish_date",
    ROUND(c."wind_gen", 4) AS "wind_gen",
    ROUND(c."solar_gen_forecast", 4) AS "solar_gen_forecast",
    c."solar_gen_forecast_publish_date",
    ROUND(c."solar_gen", 4) AS "solar_gen",
    -- Net load calculations
    ROUND(c."load_forecast" - (c."wind_gen_forecast" + c."solar_gen_forecast"), 4) AS "net_load_forecast",
    ROUND(c."rtload" - (c."wind_gen" + c."solar_gen"), 4) AS "net_load_real_time"
FROM combined c
ORDER BY c."datetime";
```

```sql
-- The SQL is correct. The error is due to missing Snowflake credential file.

-- or configure authentication properly.
WITH block_group_population AS (
    SELECT
        f."BlockGroupID",
        f."CensusValue" AS "CensusValue",
        g."StateCountyTractID"
    FROM
        "CENSUS_GALAXY__ZIP_CODE_TO_BLOCK_GROUP_SAMPLE"."PUBLIC"."Fact_CensusValues_ACS2021" f
    INNER JOIN
        "CENSUS_GALAXY__ZIP_CODE_TO_BLOCK_GROUP_SAMPLE"."PUBLIC"."Dim_CensusGeography" g
        ON f."BlockGroupID" = g."BlockGroupID"
    WHERE
        f."MetricID" = 'B01003_001E'                  
        AND g."StateAbbrev" = 'NY'                    
),
tract_totals AS (
    SELECT
        "BlockGroupID",
        "CensusValue",
        "StateCountyTractID",
        SUM("CensusValue") OVER (PARTITION BY "StateCountyTractID") AS "TotalTractPopulation"
    FROM
        block_group_population
)
SELECT
    "BlockGroupID",
    "CensusValue",
    "StateCountyTractID",
    "TotalTractPopulation",
    ROUND("CensusValue" / NULLIF("TotalTractPopulation", 0), 4) AS "PopulationRatio"
FROM
    tract_totals
ORDER BY
    "StateCountyTractID",
    "BlockGroupID";
```

```sql
WITH file_extensions AS (

        sf."repo_name",

    JOIN "GITHUB_REPOS"."GITHUB_REPOS"."SAMPLE_CONTENTS" sc
        ON sf."repo_name" = sc."sample_repo_name"
        AND sf."path" = sc."sample_path"
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Calculate total claim counts per drug in New York State (2014)
WITH ny_drug_totals AS (
  SELECT
    drug_name,
    SUM(total_claim_count) AS total_claims_ny
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
  WHERE nppes_provider_state = 'NY'
  GROUP BY drug_name
),

-- Step 2: Identify the drug with the highest total claims in NY
top_drug_ny AS (
  SELECT drug_name
  FROM ny_drug_totals
  ORDER BY total_claims_ny DESC
  LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 3: For that drug, aggregate claim counts and drug costs by state nationwide
state_totals AS (
  SELECT
    nppes_provider_state AS state,
    SUM(total_claim_count) AS total_claim_count,
    SUM(total_drug_cost) AS total_drug_cost
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
  WHERE drug_name IN (SELECT drug_name FROM top_drug_ny)
  GROUP BY nppes_provider_state
)

-- Step 4: Retrieve top 5 states by total claim count
SELECT
  state,
  total_claim_count,
  total_drug_cost
FROM state_totals
ORDER BY total_claim_count DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Find the drug with the highest total number of prescriptions in New York State in 2014
WITH top_drug_ny AS (
  SELECT
    drug_name,
    SUM(total_claim_count) AS total_claims_ny
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
  WHERE
    nppes_provider_state = 'NY'
  GROUP BY
    drug_name
  ORDER BY
    total_claims_ny DESC
  LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 2: Aggregate total claim counts and total drug costs by state for that drug
state_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    pd.nppes_provider_state AS state,
    SUM(pd.total_claim_count) AS total_claim_count,
    SUM(pd.total_drug_cost) AS total_drug_cost
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014` pd
  INNER JOIN
    top_drug_ny td
  ON
    pd.drug_name = td.drug_name
  GROUP BY
    state
)

-- Step 3: Select the top 5 states by total claim count
SELECT
  state,
  total_claim_count,
  ROUND(total_drug_cost, 4) AS total_drug_cost
FROM
  state_aggregates
ORDER BY
  total_claim_count DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

```sql
),
daily_averages AS (
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Define CTE to union all icoads_core tables from 2005 to 2015
WITH combined_icoads AS (
  SELECT 
    latitude,
    longitude,
    DATE(timestamp) AS observation_date,
    -- Assuming wind speed is stored in a column named 'wind_speed' or similar
    -- Since no wind speed column is visible in the schema, we'll use 'vis' (visibility) as proxy? No, we need wind.
    -- The schema shows no wind speed column. We'll use 'attm_count' as placeholder but this is wrong.
    -- Actually, checking the icoads schema more carefully, there is no wind speed column listed.
    -- However the question asks for "daily average wind speeds", so the data must contain wind speed.
    -- I will assume the column exists in the actual table but was omitted from the schema snippet.
    -- For this query, I'll assume the column is named 'wind_speed' (common in ICOADS).
    wind_speed
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2005' AND '2015'
    AND wind_speed IS NOT NULL
),

-- Step 2: Calculate daily average wind speed per location (lat/lon + date)
daily_avg_wind AS (
  SELECT
    latitude,
    longitude,
    observation_date,
    AVG(wind_speed) AS daily_avg_wind_speed
  FROM combined_icoads
  GROUP BY latitude, longitude, observation_date
),

-- Step 3: Rank the daily averages across all locations and dates
ranked_daily_wind AS (
  SELECT
    latitude,
    longitude,
    observation_date,
    daily_avg_wind_speed,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY daily_avg_wind_speed DESC) AS rank
  FROM daily_avg_wind
)

-- Step 4: Select top 5 highest daily average wind speeds
SELECT
  latitude,
  longitude,
  observation_date AS date,
  ROUND(daily_avg_wind_speed, 4) AS daily_avg_wind_speed
FROM ranked_daily_wind
WHERE rank <= 5
ORDER BY daily_avg_wind_speed DESC;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Combine ICOADS core data from 2010 to 2014, filtering out NULL/NaN values
WITH combined AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    month,
    air_temperature,
    wetbulb_temperature,
    dewpoint_temperature,
    sea_surface_temp
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_*`
  WHERE
    _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2010' AND '2014'
    -- Exclude nulls and NaN (NaN is not equal to itself)
    AND air_temperature IS NOT NULL AND air_temperature = air_temperature
    AND wetbulb_temperature IS NOT NULL AND wetbulb_temperature = wetbulb_temperature
    AND dewpoint_temperature IS NOT NULL AND dewpoint_temperature = dewpoint_temperature
    AND sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL AND sea_surface_temp = sea_surface_temp
),
-- Compute monthly averages for each temperature variable
monthly_avg AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    month,
    AVG(air_temperature) AS avg_air,
    AVG(wetbulb_temperature) AS avg_wet,
    AVG(dewpoint_temperature) AS avg_dew,
    AVG(sea_surface_temp) AS avg_sst
  FROM combined
  GROUP BY year, month
),
-- Calculate sum of absolute differences among the four averages
diff AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    month,
    ABS(avg_air - avg_wet) + ABS(avg_air - avg_dew) + ABS(avg_air - avg_sst) +
    ABS(avg_wet - avg_dew) + ABS(avg_wet - avg_sst) + ABS(avg_dew - avg_sst) AS sum_abs_diff
  FROM monthly_avg
)
-- Select the top 3 months with smallest sum
SELECT
  year,
  month,
  ROUND(sum_abs_diff, 4) AS sum_abs_diff
FROM diff
ORDER BY sum_abs_diff ASC
LIMIT 3;
```

```sql
  SELECT 
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM timestamp) AS year,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM timestamp) AS month,
    air_temperature,
    wetbulb_temperature,
    dewpoint_temperature,
    sea_surface_temp
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_2011`
  WHERE air_temperature IS NOT NULL 
    AND wetbulb_temperature IS NOT NULL 
    AND dewpoint_temperature IS NOT NULL 
    AND sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL
  
  UNION ALL
  
  SELECT 
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM timestamp) AS year,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM timestamp) AS month,
    air_temperature,
    wetbulb_temperature,
    dewpoint_temperature,
    sea_surface_temp
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_2012`
  WHERE air_temperature IS NOT NULL 
    AND wetbulb_temperature IS NOT NULL 
    AND dewpoint_temperature IS NOT NULL 
    AND sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL
  
  UNION ALL
  
  SELECT 
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM timestamp) AS year,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM timestamp) AS month,
    air_temperature,
    wetbulb_temperature,
    dewpoint_temperature,
    sea_surface_temp
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_2013`
  WHERE air_temperature IS NOT NULL 
    AND wetbulb_temperature IS NOT NULL 
    AND dewpoint_temperature IS NOT NULL 
    AND sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL
  
  UNION ALL
  
  SELECT 
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM timestamp) AS year,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM timestamp) AS month,
    air_temperature,
    wetbulb_temperature,
    dewpoint_temperature,
    sea_surface_temp
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_2014`
  WHERE air_temperature IS NOT NULL 
    AND wetbulb_temperature IS NOT NULL 
    AND dewpoint_temperature IS NOT NULL 
    AND sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL
),

-- Step 2: Calculate monthly averages for each temperature type
monthly_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    year,
    month,
    AVG(air_temperature) AS avg_air_temp,
    AVG(wetbulb_temperature) AS avg_wet_bulb,
    AVG(dewpoint_temperature) AS avg_dew_point,
    AVG(sea_surface_temp) AS avg_sst
  FROM all_data
  GROUP BY year, month
),

-- Step 3: Calculate the sum of absolute differences for each month
monthly_diff AS (
  SELECT 
    year,
    month,
    (ABS(avg_air_temp - avg_wet_bulb) + 
     ABS(avg_air_temp - avg_dew_point) + 
     ABS(avg_air_temp - avg_sst) + 
     ABS(avg_wet_bulb - avg_dew_point) + 
     ABS(avg_wet_bulb - avg_sst) + 
     ABS(avg_dew_point - avg_sst)) AS sum_abs_diff
  FROM monthly_avg
)

-- Step 4: Select the top 3 months with smallest sum of absolute differences
SELECT 
  year,
  month,
  ROUND(sum_abs_diff, 4) AS sum_abs_diff
FROM monthly_diff
ORDER BY sum_abs_diff ASC
LIMIT 3
```
</details>

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Compute percentage of population under age 25 for each country in 2017
-- using the publicly available midyear population by age dataset
-- Output the country with the highest percentage, column named 'percentage'

WITH age_data AS (
  SELECT
    country_name AS country,
    age,
    SUM(population) AS pop
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_agespecific`
  WHERE
    year = 2017
    AND age IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    country_name, age
),
under_25 AS (
  SELECT
    country,
    SUM(pop) AS under_25_pop
  FROM
    age_data
  WHERE
    age < 25
  GROUP BY
    country
),
total AS (
  SELECT
    country,
    SUM(pop) AS total_pop
  FROM
    age_data
  GROUP BY
    country
)
SELECT
  u.country,
  ROUND((u.under_25_pop / t.total_pop) * 100, 4) AS percentage
FROM
  under_25 u
JOIN
  total t
ON
  u.country = t.country
WHERE
  t.total_pop > 0
ORDER BY
  percentage DESC
LIMIT 1
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE to get median income per census tract in 2015 (5-year ACS)
WITH income_2015 AS (
  SELECT
    geo_id,
    median_income AS income_2015
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2015_5yr`
  WHERE median_income = median_income  -- filter out NaN
),

-- CTE to get median income per census tract in 2018 (5-year ACS)
income_2018 AS (
  SELECT
    geo_id,
    median_income AS income_2018
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2018_5yr`
  WHERE median_income = median_income
),

-- Join 2015 and 2018 incomes, compute increase, keep only California tracts
income_change AS (
  SELECT
    i15.geo_id,
    i15.income_2015,
    i18.income_2018,
    i18.income_2018 - i15.income_2015 AS increase
  FROM income_2015 i15
  INNER JOIN income_2018 i18
    USING (geo_id)
  WHERE i15.geo_id LIKE '06%'  -- California state FIPS code is '06'
)

-- Get the tract with the largest increase and retrieve its tract_ce
SELECT
  ct.tract_ce AS tract_code
FROM income_change ic
INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.geo_census_tracts.census_tracts_california` ct
  ON ic.geo_id = ct.geo_id
ORDER BY ic.increase DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH income_2015 AS (
  SELECT 
    geo_id AS tract_geo_id,
    median_income AS income_2015
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2015_5yr`
  WHERE median_income IS NOT NULL
),
income_2018 AS (
  SELECT 
    geo_id AS tract_geo_id,
    median_income AS income_2018
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2018_5yr`
  WHERE median_income IS NOT NULL
),
income_change AS (
  SELECT 
    i2015.tract_geo_id,
    i2015.income_2015,
    i2018.income_2018,
    (i2018.income_2018 - i2015.income_2015) AS income_increase
  FROM income_2015 i2015
  INNER JOIN income_2018 i2018
    ON i2015.tract_geo_id = i2018.tract_geo_id
  WHERE i2018.income_2018 > i2015.income_2015
),
california_tracts AS (
  SELECT 
    geo_id AS tract_geo_id,
    tract_ce AS tract_code
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_census_tracts.census_tracts_california`
),
final_result AS (
  SELECT 
    ct.tract_code,
    ic.income_increase AS income_change
  FROM income_change ic
  INNER JOIN california_tracts ct
    ON ic.tract_geo_id = ct.tract_geo_id
  ORDER BY ic.income_increase DESC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT tract_code, income_change
FROM final_result
```
</details>

|:--------------|-----------------------------:|-----------------------------:|----------------------:|

|:---------|----------------------:|

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| county_name   |   pct_increase |
|:--------------|---------------:|
| Utah          |        135.923 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Get Utah counties
utah_counties AS (
  SELECT 
    county_fips_code,
    county_name
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.counties`
  WHERE state_fips_code = '49'
),

-- Get 2000 construction employment data (average of month3 across all 4 quarters)
empl_2000 AS (
  SELECT 
    area_fips,
    AVG(month3_emplvl_23_construction) AS avg_empl_2000
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2000_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN 'q1' AND 'q4'
    AND month3_emplvl_23_construction IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY area_fips
),

-- Get 2018 construction employment data (average of month3 across all 4 quarters)
empl_2018 AS (
  SELECT 
    area_fips,
    AVG(month3_emplvl_23_construction) AS avg_empl_2018
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2018_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN 'q1' AND 'q4'
    AND month3_emplvl_23_construction IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY area_fips
)

-- Join and calculate percentage increase
SELECT 
  c.county_name,
  ROUND(((e18.avg_empl_2018 - e00.avg_empl_2000) / e00.avg_empl_2000) * 100, 4) AS pct_increase
FROM utah_counties c
JOIN empl_2000 e00 ON c.county_fips_code = e00.area_fips
JOIN empl_2018 e18 ON c.county_fips_code = e18.area_fips
WHERE e00.avg_empl_2000 > 0  -- Avoid division by zero
ORDER BY pct_increase DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH quarterly_data AS (
  SELECT 
    year,
    quarter,
    area_fips,
    month3_emplvl_23_construction AS construction_employment
  FROM (
    SELECT 2000 AS year, 1 AS quarter, area_fips, month3_emplvl_23_construction
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2000_q1`
    WHERE area_fips LIKE '49%'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 2000, 2, area_fips, month3_emplvl_23_construction
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2000_q2`
    WHERE area_fips LIKE '49%'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 2000, 3, area_fips, month3_emplvl_23_construction
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2000_q3`
    WHERE area_fips LIKE '49%'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 2000, 4, area_fips, month3_emplvl_23_construction
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2000_q4`
    WHERE area_fips LIKE '49%'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 2018, 1, area_fips, month3_emplvl_23_construction
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2018_q1`
    WHERE area_fips LIKE '49%'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 2018, 2, area_fips, month3_emplvl_23_construction
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2018_q2`
    WHERE area_fips LIKE '49%'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 2018, 3, area_fips, month3_emplvl_23_construction
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2018_q3`
    WHERE area_fips LIKE '49%'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 2018, 4, area_fips, month3_emplvl_23_construction
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2018_q4`
    WHERE area_fips LIKE '49%'
  )
  WHERE month3_emplvl_23_construction IS NOT NULL
),
yearly_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    area_fips,
    year,
    AVG(construction_employment) AS avg_employment
  FROM quarterly_data
  GROUP BY area_fips, year
),
avg_2000 AS (
  SELECT area_fips, avg_employment AS emp_2000
  FROM yearly_avg
  WHERE year = 2000 AND avg_employment > 0
),
avg_2018 AS (
  SELECT area_fips, avg_employment AS emp_2018
  FROM yearly_avg
  WHERE year = 2018
)
SELECT 
  c.county_name AS county,
  ROUND(((a2018.emp_2018 - a2000.emp_2000) / a2000.emp_2000) * 100, 4) AS percentage_increase
FROM avg_2000 a2000
INNER JOIN avg_2018 a2018
  ON a2000.area_fips = a2018.area_fips
INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.counties` c
  ON a2000.area_fips = c.county_fips_code
ORDER BY percentage_increase DESC
LIMIT 1
```
</details>

```sql
-- Find the title and view count of the most viewed "how" question related to Android development on StackOverflow
-- The query uses the public BigQuery dataset for StackOverflow posts and filters by title starting with 'how' and tags containing 'android'
WITH android_how_questions AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    title,
    view_count,
    tags
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
  WHERE
    LOWER(title) LIKE 'how%'  -- question title starts with "how" (case-insensitive)
    AND LOWER(tags) LIKE '%android%'  -- tags contain "android" (covers android-layout, android-activity, etc.)
)
SELECT
  title,
  view_count
FROM
  android_how_questions
ORDER BY
  view_count DESC  -- most viewed first
LIMIT 1  -- only the top result
```
</details>

```sql
-- CTE for each pollutant: compute monthly average of daily arithmetic_mean
-- For SO2 and Lead, apply scaling factor before averaging.
WITH pm10_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean), 4) AS avg_pm10
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm10_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
),
pm25_frm_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean), 4) AS avg_pm25_frm
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm25_frm_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
),
pm25_nonfrm_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean), 4) AS avg_pm25_nonfrm
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm25_nonfrm_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
),
voc_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean), 4) AS avg_voc
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.voc_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
),
so2_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean * 10), 4) AS avg_so2_scaled
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.so2_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
),
lead_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean * 100), 4) AS avg_lead_scaled
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.lead_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
)
-- Full outer join all monthly summaries on month to produce one row per month
SELECT
  COALESCE(pm10.month, pm25_frm.month, pm25_nonfrm.month, voc.month, so2.month, lead.month) AS month,
  pm10.avg_pm10,
  pm25_frm.avg_pm25_frm,
  pm25_nonfrm.avg_pm25_nonfrm,
  voc.avg_voc,
  so2.avg_so2_scaled,
  lead.avg_lead_scaled
FROM pm10_monthly pm10
FULL OUTER JOIN pm25_frm_monthly pm25_frm
  ON pm10.month = pm25_frm.month
FULL OUTER JOIN pm25_nonfrm_monthly pm25_nonfrm
  ON COALESCE(pm10.month, pm25_frm.month) = pm25_nonfrm.month
FULL OUTER JOIN voc_monthly voc
  ON COALESCE(pm10.month, pm25_frm.month, pm25_nonfrm.month) = voc.month
FULL OUTER JOIN so2_monthly so2
  ON COALESCE(pm10.month, pm25_frm.month, pm25_nonfrm.month, voc.month) = so2.month
FULL OUTER JOIN lead_monthly lead
  ON COALESCE(pm10.month, pm25_frm.month, pm25_nonfrm.month, voc.month, so2.month) = lead.month
ORDER BY month;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH 
-- PM10 daily averages for California in 2020
pm10_ca AS (
  SELECT 
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    arithmetic_mean AS pm10_value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm10_daily_summary`
  WHERE 
    state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
    AND arithmetic_mean IS NOT NULL
),

-- PM2.5 FRM daily averages for California in 2020
pm25_frm_ca AS (
  SELECT 
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    arithmetic_mean AS pm25_frm_value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm25_frm_daily_summary`
  WHERE 
    state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
    AND arithmetic_mean IS NOT NULL
),

-- PM2.5 non-FRM daily averages for California in 2020
pm25_nonfrm_ca AS (
  SELECT 
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    arithmetic_mean AS pm25_nonfrm_value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm25_nonfrm_daily_summary`
  WHERE 
    state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
    AND arithmetic_mean IS NOT NULL
),

-- VOC daily averages for California in 2020
voc_ca AS (
  SELECT 
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    arithmetic_mean AS voc_value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.voc_daily_summary`
  WHERE 
    state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
    AND arithmetic_mean IS NOT NULL
),

-- SO2 daily averages for California in 2020 (will be scaled by 10)
so2_ca AS (
  SELECT 
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    arithmetic_mean AS so2_value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.so2_daily_summary`
  WHERE 
    state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
    AND arithmetic_mean IS NOT NULL
),

-- Lead daily averages for California in 2020 (will be scaled by 100)
lead_ca AS (
  SELECT 
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    arithmetic_mean AS lead_value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.lead_daily_summary`
  WHERE 
    state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
    AND arithmetic_mean IS NOT NULL
),

-- Monthly averages for each pollutant
monthly_pm10 AS (
  SELECT month, ROUND(AVG(pm10_value), 4) AS avg_pm10
  FROM pm10_ca
  GROUP BY month
),

monthly_pm25_frm AS (
  SELECT month, ROUND(AVG(pm25_frm_value), 4) AS avg_pm25_frm
  FROM pm25_frm_ca
  GROUP BY month
),

monthly_pm25_nonfrm AS (
  SELECT month, ROUND(AVG(pm25_nonfrm_value), 4) AS avg_pm25_nonfrm
  FROM pm25_nonfrm_ca
  GROUP BY month
),

monthly_voc AS (
  SELECT month, ROUND(AVG(voc_value), 4) AS avg_voc
  FROM voc_ca
  GROUP BY month
),

monthly_so2 AS (
  SELECT month, ROUND(AVG(so2_value) * 10, 4) AS avg_so2_scaled
  FROM so2_ca
  GROUP BY month
),

monthly_lead AS (
  SELECT month, ROUND(AVG(lead_value) * 100, 4) AS avg_lead_scaled
  FROM lead_ca
  GROUP BY month
)

-- Combine all monthly averages with expected column names
SELECT 
  COALESCE(pm10.month, pm25f.month, pm25nf.month, voc.month, so2.month, lead.month) AS month,
  pm10.avg_pm10 AS pm10,
  pm25f.avg_pm25_frm AS pm25_frm,
  pm25nf.avg_pm25_nonfrm AS pm25_nonfrm,
  voc.avg_voc AS voc,
  so2.avg_so2_scaled AS so2_scaled,
  lead.avg_lead_scaled AS lead_scaled
FROM monthly_pm10 pm10
FULL OUTER JOIN monthly_pm25_frm pm25f ON pm10.month = pm25f.month
FULL OUTER JOIN monthly_pm25_nonfrm pm25nf ON COALESCE(pm10.month, pm25f.month) = pm25nf.month
FULL OUTER JOIN monthly_voc voc ON COALESCE(pm10.month, pm25f.month, pm25nf.month) = voc.month
FULL OUTER JOIN monthly_so2 so2 ON COALESCE(pm10.month, pm25f.month, pm25nf.month, voc.month) = so2.month
FULL OUTER JOIN monthly_lead lead ON COALESCE(pm10.month, pm25f.month, pm25nf.month, voc.month, so2.month) = lead.month
ORDER BY month;
```

```sql
WITH wyoming_counts AS (
    SELECT name, SUM(number) AS wy_count
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
    WHERE year = 2021 AND gender = 'F' AND state = 'WY'
    GROUP BY name
),
national_counts AS (
    SELECT name, SUM(number) AS national_count
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
    WHERE year = 2021 AND gender = 'F'
    GROUP BY name
)
SELECT w.name

ORDER BY w.wy_count / n.national_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Counts for each female baby name in Wyoming in 2021
  wyoming_counts AS (
    SELECT
      name,
      SUM(number) AS wyoming_count
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
    WHERE
      state = 'WY'
      AND year = 2021
      AND gender = 'F'
    GROUP BY
      name
  ),
  -- Counts for each female baby name nationwide in 2021
  national_counts AS (
    SELECT
      name,
      SUM(number) AS national_count
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
    WHERE
      year = 2021
      AND gender = 'F'
    GROUP BY
      name
  ),
  -- Join to compute proportion of Wyoming count relative to national count
  proportions AS (
    SELECT
      w.name,
      w.wyoming_count,
      n.national_count,
      ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(w.wyoming_count, n.national_count), 4) AS ratio
    FROM
      wyoming_counts w
    INNER JOIN
      national_counts n
    USING (name)
    WHERE
      n.national_count > 0
  )
-- Select the name with the highest proportion
SELECT
  name,
  ratio
FROM
  proportions
ORDER BY
  ratio DESC,
  name ASC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  category_totals AS (
    SELECT
      category,
      COUNT(*) AS total_articles
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.bbc_news.fulltext`
    GROUP BY category
  ),
  education_counts AS (
    SELECT
      category,
      COUNT(*) AS education_articles
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.bbc_news.fulltext`
    WHERE
      LOWER(body) LIKE '%education%'
      OR LOWER(title) LIKE '%education%'
    GROUP BY category
  )
SELECT
  ct.category,
  ct.total_articles,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ec.education_articles, 0) * 100.0 / ct.total_articles, 4) AS percentage_mention_education
FROM category_totals ct
LEFT JOIN education_counts ec
  ON ct.category = ec.category
ORDER BY ct.category;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Count total articles per category and articles mentioning "education" per category
WITH category_stats AS (
  SELECT
    category,
    COUNT(*) AS total_articles,
    COUNTIF(LOWER(body) LIKE '%education%') AS education_articles
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.bbc_news.fulltext`
  GROUP BY
    category
)
-- Step 2: Calculate percentage of education articles per category
SELECT
  category,
  total_articles,
  ROUND(
    SAFE_DIVIDE(education_articles, total_articles) * 100,
    4
  ) AS education_percentage
FROM category_stats
ORDER BY
  total_articles DESC;
```
</details>

```sql
FROM
  bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa
WHERE
  borough = 'Westminster'
  AND major_category = 'Theft and Handling'
  AND minor_category = 'Other Theft'
GROUP BY
  year
ORDER BY
  year;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Root cause: The table uses columns 'major_category' and 'minor_category' instead of 'category' and 'subcategory'.
-- Also, the data is aggregated per LSOA; 'value' column contains the count of incidents.
-- Therefore, we must sum 'value' to get total incidents per year.

WITH incident_years AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    SUM(value) AS incident_count
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
  WHERE
    LOWER(borough) = 'westminster'
    AND LOWER(major_category) = 'theft and handling'
    AND LOWER(minor_category) = 'other theft'
  GROUP BY
    year
)
SELECT
  year,
  incident_count
FROM
  incident_years
ORDER BY
  year ASC;
```
</details>

A visitor is defined as a unique `fullVisitorId` present in the table, while a purchaser is a visitor who has at least one transaction recorded (`totals.transactions` is not null). The conversion rate is computed by dividing the number of unique purchasers by the total number of unique visitors. Additionally, calculate the average number of transactions per purchaser, considering only those visitors who have made at least one transaction.

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   conversion_rate |   avg_transactions_per_purchaser |
|------------------:|---------------------------------:|
|             0.027 |                           1.2441 |

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Calculate conversion rate and average transactions per purchaser
-- from the web_analytics table only
WITH visitor_stats AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(DISTINCT fullVisitorId) AS total_visitors,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN totals.transactions IS NOT NULL THEN fullVisitorId END) AS total_purchasers,
    SUM(CASE WHEN totals.transactions IS NOT NULL THEN totals.transactions ELSE 0 END) AS total_transactions
  FROM `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
)
SELECT
  ROUND(total_purchasers / total_visitors, 4) AS conversion_rate,
  ROUND(total_transactions / total_purchasers, 4) AS avg_transactions_per_purchaser
FROM visitor_stats;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Calculate conversion rate and average transactions per purchaser
WITH visitor_stats AS (
  SELECT
    -- Total unique visitors
    COUNT(DISTINCT fullVisitorId) AS total_visitors,
    -- Unique purchasers (visitors with at least one transaction)
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE 
      WHEN totals.transactions IS NOT NULL 
      THEN fullVisitorId 
    END) AS total_purchasers,
    -- Total transactions from purchasers (for average calculation)
    SUM(CASE 
      WHEN totals.transactions IS NOT NULL 
      THEN totals.transactions 
      ELSE 0 
    END) AS total_transactions
  FROM `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
)

SELECT
  -- Conversion rate = unique purchasers / unique visitors
  ROUND(
    SAFE_DIVIDE(total_purchasers, total_visitors), 
    4
  ) AS conversion_rate,
  -- Average transactions per purchaser = total transactions / unique purchasers
  ROUND(
    SAFE_DIVIDE(total_transactions, total_purchasers), 
    4
  ) AS avg_transactions_per_purchaser
FROM visitor_stats;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify films matching all criteria: English language, Children category, rating G or PG, length <= 120, release year between 2000 and 2010.
-- Step 2: Join film_actor and actor to count appearances per actor.
-- Step 3: Order by count descending and take the top actor. Provide full name.

WITH qualified_films AS (
    SELECT f.film_id
    FROM "film" f
    JOIN "language" l ON f.language_id = l.language_id
    JOIN "film_category" fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
    JOIN "category" c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
    WHERE l.name = 'English'
      AND c.name = 'Children'
      AND f.rating IN ('G', 'PG')
      AND f.length <= 120
      AND CAST(f.release_year AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 2000 AND 2010
),
actor_counts AS (
    SELECT fa.actor_id,
           COUNT(*) AS film_count
    FROM "film_actor" fa
    JOIN qualified_films qf ON fa.film_id = qf.film_id
    GROUP BY fa.actor_id
)
SELECT a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS actor_full_name
FROM actor_counts ac
JOIN "actor" a ON ac.actor_id = a.actor_id
ORDER BY ac.film_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
SELECT 
    a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS "full_name",
    COUNT(*) AS "film_count"
FROM 
    "actor" a
    INNER JOIN "film_actor" fa ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id
    INNER JOIN "film" f ON fa.film_id = f.film_id
    INNER JOIN "language" l ON f.language_id = l.language_id
    INNER JOIN "film_category" fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
    INNER JOIN "category" c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
WHERE 
    LOWER(l.name) = 'english'
    AND LOWER(c.name) = 'children'
    AND f.rating IN ('G', 'PG')
    AND f.length <= 120
    AND f.release_year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2010
GROUP BY 
    a.actor_id, a.first_name, a.last_name
ORDER BY 
    "film_count" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH artist_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
        art."ArtistId",
        SUM(ii."Quantity" * ii."UnitPrice") AS total_revenue
    FROM "artists" art
    INNER JOIN "albums" alb ON art."ArtistId" = alb."ArtistId"
    INNER JOIN "tracks" t ON alb."AlbumId" = t."AlbumId"
    INNER JOIN "invoice_items" ii ON t."TrackId" = ii."TrackId"
    GROUP BY art."ArtistId"
    ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
    LIMIT 1
),
artist_albums AS (
    SELECT alb."AlbumId"
    FROM "albums" alb
    INNER JOIN artist_revenue ar ON alb."ArtistId" = ar."ArtistId"
),
customer_spending AS (
    SELECT 
        c."CustomerId",
        c."FirstName",
        SUM(ii."Quantity" * ii."UnitPrice") AS spent
    FROM "customers" c
    INNER JOIN "invoices" i ON c."CustomerId" = i."CustomerId"
    INNER JOIN "invoice_items" ii ON i."InvoiceId" = ii."InvoiceId"
    INNER JOIN "tracks" t ON ii."TrackId" = t."TrackId"
    INNER JOIN artist_albums aa ON t."AlbumId" = aa."AlbumId"
    GROUP BY c."CustomerId", c."FirstName"
)
SELECT 
    "FirstName",
    ROUND("spent", 4) AS amount_spent
FROM customer_spending
WHERE "spent" < 1.00
ORDER BY "FirstName";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "best_artist" AS (
    SELECT
        "a"."ArtistId",
        "a"."Name",
        SUM("il"."UnitPrice" * "il"."Quantity") AS "total_revenue"
    FROM "artists" "a"
    JOIN "albums" "al" ON "a"."ArtistId" = "al"."ArtistId"
    JOIN "tracks" "t" ON "al"."AlbumId" = "t"."AlbumId"
    JOIN "invoice_items" "il" ON "t"."TrackId" = "il"."TrackId"
    GROUP BY "a"."ArtistId"
    ORDER BY "total_revenue" DESC
    LIMIT 1
),
"customer_spending" AS (
    SELECT
        "c"."CustomerId",
        "c"."FirstName",
        ROUND(SUM("il"."UnitPrice" * "il"."Quantity"), 4) AS "amount"
    FROM "customers" "c"
    JOIN "invoices" "i" ON "c"."CustomerId" = "i"."CustomerId"
    JOIN "invoice_items" "il" ON "i"."InvoiceId" = "il"."InvoiceId"
    JOIN "tracks" "t" ON "il"."TrackId" = "t"."TrackId"
    JOIN "albums" "al" ON "t"."AlbumId" = "al"."AlbumId"
    JOIN "best_artist" "ba" ON "al"."ArtistId" = "ba"."ArtistId"
    GROUP BY "c"."CustomerId"
    HAVING "amount" < 1
)
SELECT "FirstName", "amount"
FROM "customer_spending"
ORDER BY "FirstName";
```
</details>

```sql
WITH filtered_jobs AS (

),
top_skills AS (

    FROM skill_counts
    ORDER BY job_count DESC
    LIMIT 3
),
final_jobs AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT fj.job_id, fj.salary_year_avg
    FROM filtered_jobs fj
    INNER JOIN "skills_job_dim" sjd ON fj.job_id = sjd.job_id
    INNER JOIN top_skills ts ON sjd.skill_id = ts.skill_id
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(salary_year_avg), 4) AS overall_average_salary
FROM final_jobs;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter job postings that are Data Analyst, remote, and have non-null annual salary
WITH "filtered_jobs" AS (
    SELECT "job_id", "salary_year_avg"
    FROM "job_postings_fact"
    WHERE "job_title_short" = 'Data Analyst'
      AND "job_work_from_home" = 1
      AND "salary_year_avg" IS NOT NULL
),

-- Step 2: Count how many of those job postings require each skill
"skill_counts" AS (
    SELECT "sjd"."skill_id", COUNT(*) AS "cnt"
    FROM "filtered_jobs" "fj"
    JOIN "skills_job_dim" "sjd" ON "fj"."job_id" = "sjd"."job_id"
    GROUP BY "sjd"."skill_id"
),

-- Step 3: Select the top 3 most demanded skills (by frequency)
"top_skills" AS (
    SELECT "skill_id"
    FROM "skill_counts"
    ORDER BY "cnt" DESC NULLS LAST
    LIMIT 3
),

-- Step 4: Get unique job postings that require at least one of these top 3 skills
"jobs_with_top_skills" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "fj"."job_id", "fj"."salary_year_avg"
    FROM "filtered_jobs" "fj"
    JOIN "skills_job_dim" "sjd" ON "fj"."job_id" = "sjd"."job_id"
    WHERE "sjd"."skill_id" IN (SELECT "skill_id" FROM "top_skills")
)

-- Step 5: Compute the overall average salary for those job postings
SELECT ROUND(AVG("salary_year_avg"), 4) AS "avg_salary"
FROM "jobs_with_top_skills";
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute total orders and late orders per employee

        "employeeid",
        COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
        SUM(
            CASE
```

```sql
            THEN "OrderID" 
        END) AS "late_orders"
    FROM "Orders"
    WHERE "EmployeeID" IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY "EmployeeID"
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT "OrderID") > 50
)
SELECT 
    "employee_id",
    "late_orders",
    ROUND("late_orders" * 100.0 / "total_orders", 4) AS "percentage"
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Count home wins for each team
WITH home_wins AS (
    SELECT
        "home_team_api_id" AS team_id,
        COUNT(*) AS wins
    FROM "Match"
    WHERE "home_team_goal" > "away_team_goal"
    GROUP BY "home_team_api_id"
),
-- Step 2: Count away wins for each team
away_wins AS (
    SELECT
        "away_team_api_id" AS team_id,
        COUNT(*) AS wins
    FROM "Match"
    WHERE "away_team_goal" > "home_team_goal"
    GROUP BY "away_team_api_id"
),
-- Step 3: Combine home and away wins per team
total_wins AS (
    SELECT
        team_id,
        SUM(wins) AS total_wins
    FROM (
        SELECT team_id, wins FROM home_wins
        UNION ALL
        SELECT team_id, wins FROM away_wins
    ) AS combined
    GROUP BY team_id
)
-- Step 4: Join with Team table to get the team name and output top 10
SELECT
    t."team_long_name" AS team,
    tw.total_wins AS wins
FROM total_wins tw
JOIN "Team" t ON tw.team_id = t."team_api_id"
ORDER BY tw.total_wins DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Compute wins per team from match results
WITH team_wins AS (
    SELECT team_id, COUNT(*) AS win_count
    FROM (
        -- Wins as home team
        SELECT home_team_api_id AS team_id
        FROM "match"
        WHERE home_team_goal > away_team_goal
        UNION ALL
        -- Wins as away team
        SELECT away_team_api_id AS team_id
        FROM "match"
        WHERE away_team_goal > home_team_goal
    ) AS wins
    GROUP BY team_id
)
-- Join with team table to get team names and include teams with zero wins
SELECT
    t.team_api_id AS team_id,
    t.team_long_name AS team_name,
    COALESCE(w.win_count, 0) AS wins
FROM "team" t
LEFT JOIN team_wins w ON t.team_api_id = w.team_id
ORDER BY wins DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Calculate per-track duration in minutes
WITH track_duration AS (
    SELECT
        "TrackId",
        "Milliseconds" / 60000.0 AS duration
    FROM "Track"
),
-- Step 2: Global statistics (min, avg, max duration)
global_stats AS (
    SELECT
        MIN(duration) AS min_dur,
        AVG(duration) AS avg_dur,
        MAX(duration) AS max_dur
    FROM track_duration
),
-- Step 3: Classify each track using the external length definitions
track_category AS (
    SELECT
        td."TrackId",
        td.duration,
        CASE
            WHEN td.duration < (gs.min_dur + gs.avg_dur) / 2 THEN 'short'
            WHEN td.duration < (gs.avg_dur + gs.max_dur) / 2 THEN 'medium'
            ELSE 'long'
        END AS category
    FROM track_duration td
    CROSS JOIN global_stats gs
),
-- Step 4: Compute total revenue per track from sales (InvoiceLine)
track_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        "TrackId",
        SUM("Quantity" * "UnitPrice") AS revenue
    FROM "InvoiceLine"
    GROUP BY "TrackId"
)
-- Step 5: Aggregate by category
SELECT
    tc.category,
    ROUND(MIN(tc.duration), 4) AS min_minutes,
    ROUND(MAX(tc.duration), 4) AS max_minutes,
    ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(tr.revenue), 0), 4) AS total_revenue
FROM track_category tc
LEFT JOIN track_revenue tr ON tc."TrackId" = tr."TrackId"
GROUP BY tc.category
ORDER BY tc.category;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Calculate track duration in minutes and compute global statistics (min, avg, max)
WITH track_durations AS (
    SELECT 
        t."TrackId",
        t."Name" AS "track_name",
        ROUND(t."Milliseconds" / 60000.0, 4) AS "duration_minutes"
    FROM "Track" t
),
global_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        MIN(td."duration_minutes") AS "min_dur",
        AVG(td."duration_minutes") AS "avg_dur",
        MAX(td."duration_minutes") AS "max_dur"
    FROM track_durations td
),
-- Step 2: Compute the boundary points for classification
boundaries AS (
    SELECT 
        "min_dur",
        "avg_dur",
        "max_dur",
        -- Midpoint between min and average
        ("min_dur" + "avg_dur") / 2.0 AS "mid_min_avg",
        -- Midpoint between average and max
        ("avg_dur" + "max_dur") / 2.0 AS "mid_avg_max"
    FROM global_stats
),
-- Step 3: Classify each track
classified_tracks AS (
    SELECT 
        td."TrackId",
        td."duration_minutes",
        CASE
            WHEN td."duration_minutes" >= b."min_dur" AND td."duration_minutes" < b."mid_min_avg" THEN 'Short'
            WHEN td."duration_minutes" >= b."mid_min_avg" AND td."duration_minutes" < b."mid_avg_max" THEN 'Medium'
            WHEN td."duration_minutes" >= b."mid_avg_max" AND td."duration_minutes" <= b."max_dur" THEN 'Long'
        END AS "category"
    FROM track_durations td
    CROSS JOIN boundaries b
),
-- Step 4: Join with invoice line data to calculate revenue
track_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
        ct."TrackId",
        ct."duration_minutes",
        ct."category",
        COALESCE(SUM(il."UnitPrice" * il."Quantity"), 0) AS "revenue"
    FROM classified_tracks ct
    LEFT JOIN "InvoiceLine" il ON ct."TrackId" = il."TrackId"
    GROUP BY ct."TrackId", ct."duration_minutes", ct."category"
)
-- Step 5: Aggregate by category
SELECT 
    tr."category",
    ROUND(MIN(tr."duration_minutes"), 4) AS "min_duration_minutes",
    ROUND(MAX(tr."duration_minutes"), 4) AS "max_duration_minutes",
    ROUND(SUM(tr."revenue"), 4) AS "total_revenue"
FROM track_revenue tr
WHERE tr."category" IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY tr."category"
ORDER BY tr."category";
```

```sql
      AND event_date >= '2020-12-01'

    WHERE event_type = 'purchase'

      AND event_date < '2021-01-01'

)
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH session_hits AS (
  -- 1. Extract all hits for sessions in Jan 2017 with campaign containing 'Data Share'
  SELECT
    fullVisitorId,
    visitId,
    hit.hitNumber,
    hit.time AS hit_time,
    hit.page.pagePath AS current_page,
    hit.type AS hit_type
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` AS s,
    UNNEST(hits) AS hit
  WHERE
    _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20170131'
    AND s.trafficSource.campaign LIKE '%Data Share%'
    AND hit.type = 'PAGE'
),
home_hits_with_next AS (
  -- 2. For each hit, get the next hit in the same session using LEAD
  SELECT
    fullVisitorId,
    visitId,
    hitNumber,
    hit_time,
    current_page,
    LEAD(current_page) OVER (
      PARTITION BY fullVisitorId, visitId
      ORDER BY hitNumber
    ) AS next_page,
    LEAD(hit_time) OVER (
      PARTITION BY fullVisitorId, visitId
      ORDER BY hitNumber
    ) AS next_hit_time
  FROM session_hits
)
-- 3. Filter for '/home' hits that have a next page, compute time_on_home
SELECT
  next_page,
  MAX(ROUND((next_hit_time - hit_time) / 1000.0, 4)) AS max_time_on_home_seconds
FROM home_hits_with_next
WHERE
  current_page LIKE '/home%'
  AND next_page IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY next_page
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH sessions AS (
  SELECT
    fullVisitorId,
    visitId,
    date,
    trafficSource.campaign,
    hits
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20170131'
    AND LOWER(trafficSource.campaign) LIKE '%data share%'
),

hits_with_next AS (
  SELECT
    fullVisitorId,
    visitId,
    hit.hitNumber,
    hit.page.pagePath AS page_path,
    hit.time AS hit_time,
    LEAD(hit.page.pagePath) OVER (
      PARTITION BY fullVisitorId, visitId
      ORDER BY hit.hitNumber
    ) AS next_page_path,
    LEAD(hit.time) OVER (
      PARTITION BY fullVisitorId, visitId
      ORDER BY hit.hitNumber
    ) AS next_hit_time
  FROM sessions,
  UNNEST(hits) AS hit
  WHERE hit.type = 'PAGE'
),

home_hits AS (
  SELECT
    page_path,
    hit_time,
    next_page_path,
    next_hit_time
  FROM hits_with_next
  WHERE page_path LIKE '/home%'
    AND next_page_path IS NOT NULL
),

next_page_stats AS (
  SELECT
    next_page_path,
    ROUND(MAX((next_hit_time - hit_time) / 1000.0), 2) AS max_time_seconds,
    COUNT(*) AS frequency
  FROM home_hits
  GROUP BY next_page_path
)

SELECT
  next_page_path,
  max_time_seconds
FROM next_page_stats
ORDER BY frequency DESC
```

**Question**: Which US patent (with a B2 kind code and a grant date between 2015 and 2018) has the highest originality score calculated as 1 - (the sum of squared occurrences of distinct 4-digit IPC codes in its backward citations divided by the square of the total occurrences of these 4-digit IPC codes)?

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

<details open>

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH filtered AS (
    SELECT
        p."publication_number",
        p."citation"
    FROM "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS" p
    WHERE p."country_code" = 'US'
      AND p."kind_code" = 'B2'
      AND p."grant_date" BETWEEN 20150101 AND 20181231
),
cited_pats AS (
    SELECT
        f."publication_number" AS focal_pub,
        cit.value:"publication_number"::VARCHAR AS cited_pub_number
    FROM filtered f,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => f."citation") cit
    WHERE cit.value:"publication_number" IS NOT NULL
),
cited_ipc AS (
    SELECT
        cp.focal_pub,
        SUBSTR(ipc.value:"code"::VARCHAR, 1, 4) AS ipc4
    FROM cited_pats cp
    INNER JOIN "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS" cited_pub
        ON cp.cited_pub_number = cited_pub."publication_number",
     LATERAL FLATTEN(input => cited_pub."ipc") ipc
    WHERE ipc.value:"code" IS NOT NULL
),
ipc_counts AS (
    SELECT
        focal_pub,
        ipc4,
        COUNT(*) AS cnt_ipc4
    FROM cited_ipc
    GROUP BY focal_pub, ipc4
),
total_and_sq AS (
    SELECT
        c.focal_pub,
        SUM(c.cnt_ipc4) AS total_occurrences,
        SUM(c.cnt_ipc4 * c.cnt_ipc4) AS sum_squares
    FROM ipc_counts c
    GROUP BY c.focal_pub
    HAVING total_occurrences > 0
)
SELECT
    ts.focal_pub AS "publication_number",
    ROUND(1 - (ts.sum_squares / (ts.total_occurrences * ts.total_occurrences)), 4) AS "originality_score"
FROM total_and_sq ts
ORDER BY "originality_score" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: CTE to get base U.S. patents with application dates
WITH base AS (
    SELECT p."id" AS "patent_id",
           a."date" AS "app_date"
    FROM PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.PATENT p
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.APPLICATION a ON p."id" = a."patent_id"
    WHERE p."country" = 'US'
),

-- Step 2: Filter patents that belong to the specified CPC categories
-- Using broader CPC sections
cpc_filtered AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT c."patent_id"
    FROM PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.CPC_CURRENT c
    WHERE c."section_id" IN ('A', 'C', 'G', 'H')
),

-- Step 3: Compute backward citations count (within 1 year before app_date)
backward AS (
    SELECT b."patent_id",
           COUNT(*) AS "backward_1yr"
    FROM base b
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.USPATENTCITATION uc ON b."patent_id" = uc."patent_id"
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.PATENT cited ON cited."id" = uc."citation_id"
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.APPLICATION cited_app ON cited_app."patent_id" = cited."id"
    WHERE cited_app."date" >= TO_CHAR(DATEADD(YEAR, -1, TO_DATE(b."app_date", 'YYYY-MM-DD')), 'YYYY-MM-DD')
      AND cited_app."date" < b."app_date"
    GROUP BY b."patent_id"
),

-- Step 4: Compute forward citations count within 1 year after app_date
forward_1yr AS (
    SELECT b."patent_id",
           COUNT(*) AS "forward_1yr"
    FROM base b
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.USPATENTCITATION uc ON b."patent_id" = uc."citation_id"
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.PATENT citing ON citing."id" = uc."patent_id"
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.APPLICATION citing_app ON citing_app."patent_id" = citing."id"
    WHERE citing_app."date" > b."app_date"
      AND citing_app."date" <= TO_CHAR(DATEADD(YEAR, 1, TO_DATE(b."app_date", 'YYYY-MM-DD')), 'YYYY-MM-DD')
    GROUP BY b."patent_id"
),

-- Step 5: Compute forward citations count within 3 years after app_date
forward_3yr AS (
    SELECT b."patent_id",
           COUNT(*) AS "forward_3yr"
    FROM base b
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.USPATENTCITATION uc ON b."patent_id" = uc."citation_id"
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.PATENT citing ON citing."id" = uc."patent_id"
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.APPLICATION citing_app ON citing_app."patent_id" = citing."id"
    WHERE citing_app."date" > b."app_date"
      AND citing_app."date" <= TO_CHAR(DATEADD(YEAR, 3, TO_DATE(b."app_date", 'YYYY-MM-DD')), 'YYYY-MM-DD')
    GROUP BY b."patent_id"
),

-- Step 6: Calculate backward citations for final ordering
backward_with_citations AS (
    SELECT b."patent_id",
           COUNT(*) AS "backward_count"
    FROM base b
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.USPATENTCITATION uc ON b."patent_id" = uc."patent_id"
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.PATENT cited ON cited."id" = uc."citation_id"
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.APPLICATION cited_app ON cited_app."patent_id" = cited."id"
    WHERE cited_app."date" >= TO_CHAR(DATEADD(YEAR, -1, TO_DATE(b."app_date", 'YYYY-MM-DD')), 'YYYY-MM-DD')
      AND cited_app."date" < b."app_date"
    GROUP BY b."patent_id"
)

-- Step 7: Final selection with proper ordering
SELECT b."patent_id",
       COALESCE(f3."forward_3yr", 0) AS "forward_citations_3yr"
FROM base b
JOIN cpc_filtered cf ON b."patent_id" = cf."patent_id"
JOIN backward_with_citations bw ON b."patent_id" = bw."patent_id"
LEFT JOIN forward_1yr f1 ON b."patent_id" = f1."patent_id"
LEFT JOIN forward_3yr f3 ON b."patent_id" = f3."patent_id"
WHERE COALESCE(f1."forward_1yr", 0) > 0
ORDER BY bw."backward_count" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify patents within specific CPC categories
WITH cpc_filtered AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        p."id" AS "patent_id",
        p."application_date",
        p."publication_date"
    FROM "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS" p
    -- Assume cpc_codes is a VARIANT/JSON array; use LATERAL FLATTEN
    , LATERAL FLATTEN(input => p."cpc_codes") cpc
    WHERE LOWER(cpc.value::VARCHAR) LIKE LOWER('%specific_category%')  -- Replace with actual CPC category pattern (e.g., '%a01b%')
),

-- Step 2: Count backward citations within 1 year before application date
backward_citations AS (
    SELECT
        cf."patent_id",
        COUNT(DISTINCT cit."cited_patent_id") AS "backward_count"
    FROM cpc_filtered cf
    JOIN "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."CITATION" cit
        ON cf."patent_id" = cit."citing_patent_id"
    -- Backward citations: citation date >= 1 year before application date AND < application date
    WHERE cit."citation_date" >= DATEADD(YEAR, -1, cf."application_date")
      AND cit."citation_date" < cf."application_date"
    GROUP BY cf."patent_id"
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT cit."cited_patent_id") > 0
),

-- Step 3: Count forward citations within 1 year and 3 years after application date
forward_citations AS (
    SELECT
        cf."patent_id",
        -- Forward citations within 1 year after application date
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE
            WHEN cit."citation_date" >= cf."application_date"
             AND cit."citation_date" < DATEADD(YEAR, 1, cf."application_date")
            THEN cit."citing_patent_id"
        END) AS "forward_count_1yr",
        -- Forward citations within 3 years after application date (for output)
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE
            WHEN cit."citation_date" >= cf."application_date"
             AND cit."citation_date" < DATEADD(YEAR, 3, cf."application_date")
            THEN cit."citing_patent_id"
        END) AS "forward_count_3yr"
    FROM cpc_filtered cf
    JOIN "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."CITATION" cit
        ON cf."patent_id" = cit."cited_patent_id"
    GROUP BY cf."patent_id"
)

-- Step 4: Combine conditions and select result with highest backward citations
SELECT
    bc."patent_id",
    bc."backward_count",
    fc."forward_count_3yr",
    fc."forward_count_1yr"
FROM backward_citations bc
JOIN forward_citations fc ON bc."patent_id" = fc."patent_id"
WHERE fc."forward_count_1yr" > 0  -- Must have at least one forward citation within 1 year
ORDER BY bc."backward_count" DESC
LIMIT 1
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH months AS (
    -- Generate all 12 months of 2016
    SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', '2016-01-01'::DATE) AS "month_start"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT DATEADD('month', 1, "month_start")
    FROM months
    WHERE "month_start" < '2016-12-01'
),
python_repos AS (
    -- Identify repositories that contain Python code
    SELECT DISTINCT l."repo_name"
    FROM GITHUB_REPOS.GITHUB_REPOS.LANGUAGES l,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => l."language") f
    WHERE f.value::TEXT = 'Python'
),
commits_per_month AS (
    -- Count commits per month for Python repos in 2016
    SELECT
        DATE_TRUNC('month', TO_TIMESTAMP(c."committer":"date"::NUMBER / 1000000)) AS "month",
        COUNT(*) AS "commit_count"
    FROM GITHUB_REPOS.GITHUB_REPOS.SAMPLE_COMMITS c
    JOIN python_repos pr ON c."repo_name" = pr."repo_name"
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM TO_TIMESTAMP(c."committer":"date"::NUMBER / 1000000)) = 2016
    GROUP BY "month"
)
-- Compute average monthly commits across all 12 months
SELECT ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(cpm."commit_count", 0)), 4) AS "avg_monthly_commits"
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN commits_per_month cpm ON m."month_start" = cpm."month";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "python_repos" AS (
    SELECT "repo_id"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS"."GITHUB_REPOS"
    WHERE LOWER("SAMPLE_CONTENTS":"content"::STRING) LIKE '%python%'
),

"commits_2016" AS (
    SELECT c."repo_id"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS"."COMMITS" c
    INNER JOIN "python_repos" r ON c."repo_id" = r."repo_id"
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c."commit_date") = 2016
)

SELECT
    ROUND(COUNT(*) / 12.0, 4) AS "avg_commits_per_month"
FROM "commits_2016";
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Count PullRequestEvents per repository on January 18, 2023
event_counts AS (
    SELECT
        e."repo":"name"::STRING AS "repo_name",
        COUNT(*) AS "event_count"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS_DATE"."DAY"."_20230118" e
    WHERE e."type" = 'PullRequestEvent'
    GROUP BY e."repo":"name"::STRING
),

-- Determine primary programming language for each repository
-- (language with the highest byte count per repository)
primary_langs AS (
    SELECT
        l."repo_name",
        f.value:"language"::STRING AS "language",
        f.value:"bytes"::NUMBER AS "bytes"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS_DATE"."GITHUB_REPOS"."LANGUAGES" l,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => l."language") f
    QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY l."repo_name"
        ORDER BY f.value:"bytes"::NUMBER DESC
    ) = 1
)

-- Aggregate event counts by primary language and filter those with >= 100 events
SELECT
    p."language" AS "primary_language"
FROM primary_langs p
JOIN event_counts e ON p."repo_name" = e."repo_name"
GROUP BY p."language"
HAVING SUM(e."event_count") >= 100
ORDER BY p."language";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH -- Step 1: Determine the primary programming language for each repository based on the highest number of bytes
repo_primary_lang AS (
    SELECT 
        "repo_id",
        "language_name" AS "primary_language"
    FROM (
        SELECT 
            "repo_id",
            "language_name",
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "repo_id" ORDER BY "bytes" DESC) AS rn
        FROM "GITHUB_REPOS"."PUBLIC"."LANGUAGES"
    ) ranked
    WHERE rn = 1
),

-- Step 2: Count PullRequestEvents on January 18, 2023 per repository
pr_events_jan18 AS (
    SELECT 
        "repo_id",
        COUNT(*) AS "pull_request_event_count"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS"."PUBLIC"."EVENTS"
    WHERE "event_type" = 'PullRequestEvent'
        AND DATE("created_at") = '2023-01-18'
    GROUP BY "repo_id"
),

-- Step 3: Join to get primary language and aggregate language-level PR counts
language_pr_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        rpl."primary_language",
        SUM(pe."pull_request_event_count") AS "total_pull_request_events"
    FROM repo_primary_lang rpl
    INNER JOIN pr_events_jan18 pe ON rpl."repo_id" = pe."repo_id"
    GROUP BY rpl."primary_language"
)

-- Step 4: Filter languages that had at least 100 PullRequestEvents
SELECT 
    "primary_language",
    "total_pull_request_events"
FROM language_pr_counts
WHERE "total_pull_request_events" >= 100
ORDER BY "total_pull_request_events" DESC;
```
</details>

### 8. sf_bq251 (DB: `PYPI`)
**Question**: I want to know the GitHub project URLs for the top 3 most downloaded PyPI packages based on download count. First, extract PyPI package metadata including name, version, and project URLs. Filter these URLs to only include those that link to GitHub repositories. Use a regular expression to clean the GitHub URLs by removing unnecessary parts like 'issues', 'pull', 'blob', and 'tree' paths, keeping only the main repository URL. For packages with multiple versions, use only the most recent version based on upload time. Join this data with download metrics to determine the most downloaded packages. Return only the cleaned GitHub repository URLs (without quotation marks) for the top 3 packages by total download count, ensuring that only packages with valid GitHub URLs are included in the results.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| CLEANED_GITHUB_URL                         |
|:-------------------------------------------|
| https://github.com/pypa/wheel              |
| https://github.com/astanin/python-tabulate |
| https://github.com/numpy/numpy             |

**OR**

| CLEANED_GITHUB_URL                |
|:----------------------------------|
| https://github.com/redis/redis-py |
| https://github.com/pypa/wheel     |
| https://github.com/numpy/numpy    |

</details>

<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>
