</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

| github_url                                           |
|:-----------------------------------------------------|
| Issue Tracker, https://github.com/pypa/wheel         |
| Homepage, https://github.com/astanin/python-tabulate |
| Source, https://github.com/numpy/numpy               |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH github_projects AS (
    SELECT 
        dm."name",
        dm."version",
        dm."upload_time",
        REGEXP_REPLACE(
            f.value::STRING,
            '(https?://github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+)(/.*)?',
            '\\1'
        ) AS "github_url"
    FROM "PYPI"."PYPI"."DISTRIBUTION_METADATA" dm,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => dm."project_urls") f
    WHERE f.value::STRING ILIKE '%github.com%'
),
latest_versions AS (
    SELECT 
        gp."name",
        gp."version",
        gp."github_url",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY gp."name" ORDER BY gp."upload_time" DESC) AS "rn"
    FROM github_projects gp
),
valid_projects AS (
    SELECT lv."name", lv."github_url"
    FROM latest_versions lv
    WHERE lv."rn" = 1 AND lv."github_url" IS NOT NULL
),
download_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        fd."project",
        COUNT(*) AS "total_downloads"
    FROM "PYPI"."PYPI"."FILE_DOWNLOADS" fd
    GROUP BY fd."project"
)
SELECT vp."github_url"
FROM valid_projects vp
JOIN download_counts dc ON vp."name" = dc."project"
ORDER BY dc."total_downloads" DESC
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Step 1: For each package, select the latest version based on upload_time
  latest_versions AS (
    SELECT
      "name",
      "version",
      "project_urls",
      "upload_time",
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "name" ORDER BY "upload_time" DESC) AS rn
    FROM "PYPI"."PYPI"."PACKAGES"
  ),
  -- Step 2: Keep only the most recent version per package
  single_version AS (
    SELECT "name", "version", "project_urls"
    FROM latest_versions
    WHERE rn = 1
  ),
  -- Step 3: Flatten the project_urls (JSON object) and extract GitHub URLs
  github_urls AS (
    SELECT
      sv."name",
      sv."version",
      TRIM(
        REGEXP_REPLACE(
          url_flatten.value::VARCHAR,
          '(/issues|/pull|/blob|/tree)(/.*)?$',
          ''
        ),
        '/'
      ) AS raw_github_url
    FROM single_version sv,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => sv."project_urls") AS url_flatten
    WHERE url_flatten.value IS NOT NULL
      AND LOWER(url_flatten.value::VARCHAR) LIKE '%github.com%'
  ),
  -- Step 4: Clean URLs and deduplicate by picking one GitHub URL per package-version
  cleaned_urls AS (
    SELECT "name", "version", raw_github_url AS github_url
    FROM (
      SELECT 
        "name",
        "version",
        raw_github_url,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "name", "version" ORDER BY raw_github_url) AS rn2
      FROM github_urls
      WHERE raw_github_url != ''
    ) 
    WHERE rn2 = 1
  ),
  -- Step 5: Join with download metrics and compute total downloads per package
  package_downloads AS (
    SELECT
      cu."name",
      cu."version",
      cu."github_url",
      SUM(dm."download_count") AS sum_downloads
    FROM cleaned_urls cu
    INNER JOIN "PYPI"."PYPI"."DOWNLOADS" dm
      ON cu."name" = dm."package_name"
      AND cu."version" = dm."version"
    GROUP BY cu."name", cu."version", cu."github_url"
  ),
  -- Step 6: Get top 3 packages by total downloads
  top_packages AS (
    SELECT "name"
    FROM package_downloads
    ORDER BY sum_downloads DESC
    LIMIT 3
  )
-- Final: Return only the GitHub URLs for the top 3 packages
SELECT pd.github_url
FROM package_downloads pd
INNER JOIN top_packages tp
  ON pd."name" = tp."name"
ORDER BY pd.sum_downloads DESC;
```
</details>

```sql
        "damage_property",
        "event_type"
    FROM all_storms

        AND "damage_property" IS NOT NULL
    ORDER BY "damage_property" DESC
    LIMIT 100
),
events_with_month AS (
    SELECT 
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM DATEADD(microsecond, "event_begin_time", '1970-01-01'::TIMESTAMP)) AS event_month
    FROM top_100_events
),
month_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        event_month,
        COUNT(*) AS event_count
    FROM events_with_month
    GROUP BY event_month
),
most_affected_month AS (
    SELECT 
        event_month,
        event_count
    FROM month_counts
    ORDER BY event_count DESC
    LIMIT 1
)
SELECT event_count AS total_severe_storm_events
FROM most_affected_month;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Combine all severe storm events from preliminary tables (2009-2024)
all_hail_prelim AS (
    SELECT "timestamp" 
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_PRELIMINARY_SEVERE_STORMS"."HAIL_REPORTS"
),
all_wind_prelim AS (
    SELECT "timestamp"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_PRELIMINARY_SEVERE_STORMS"."WIND_REPORTS"
),
all_tornado_prelim AS (
    SELECT "timestamp"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_PRELIMINARY_SEVERE_STORMS"."TORNADO_REPORTS"
),
-- Combine all severe storm events from historic tables
all_hail_historic AS (
    SELECT "timestamp"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."HAIL_REPORTS"
),
all_tornado_historic AS (
    SELECT "timestamp"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."TORNADO_REPORTS"
),
all_wind_historic AS (
    SELECT "timestamp"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA"."NOAA_HISTORIC_SEVERE_STORMS"."WIND_REPORTS"
),
-- Union all events together
all_events AS (
    SELECT * FROM all_hail_prelim
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM all_wind_prelim
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM all_tornado_prelim
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM all_hail_historic
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM all_tornado_historic
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM all_wind_historic
),
-- Filter for past 15 years (2009-2024) and extract month
valid_events AS (
    SELECT
        "timestamp",
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM TO_TIMESTAMP("timestamp" / 1000000)) AS event_month,
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM TO_TIMESTAMP("timestamp" / 1000000)) AS event_year
    FROM all_events
    WHERE "timestamp" IS NOT NULL
      AND "timestamp" >= 1230768000000000  -- Jan 1, 2009 in microseconds
      AND "timestamp" < 1735689600000000   -- Jan 1, 2025 in microseconds
),
-- Count events per month
monthly_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        event_year,
        event_month,
        COUNT(*) AS event_count
    FROM valid_events
    GROUP BY event_year, event_month
),
-- Sum across all years to find most affected month
monthly_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        event_month,
        SUM(event_count) AS total_events_15_years
    FROM monthly_counts
    GROUP BY event_month
),
most_affected_month AS (
    SELECT event_month
    FROM monthly_totals
    ORDER BY total_events_15_years DESC
    LIMIT 1
)
SELECT 
    COUNT(*) AS "total_severe_events"
FROM valid_events e
JOIN most_affected_month m ON e.event_month = m.event_month;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH hurricane_points AS (
    -- Convert hurricane lat/lon to geography points, normalizing longitude to [-180,180]
    SELECT 
        h."name",
        ST_POINT(
            CASE 
                WHEN h."longitude" > 180 THEN h."longitude" - 360
                WHEN h."longitude" < -180 THEN h."longitude" + 360
                ELSE h."longitude"
            END,
            h."latitude"
        ) AS "hurricane_point"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA_PLUS"."NOAA_HURRICANES"."HURRICANES" h
    WHERE h."name" IS NOT NULL 
      AND TRIM(h."name") != ''
      AND h."latitude" IS NOT NULL 
      AND h."longitude" IS NOT NULL
      AND ABS(h."latitude") <= 90
),
zip_hurricanes AS (
    -- Spatial join: find which hurricanes fall within which zip code boundaries
    SELECT DISTINCT
        z."city",
        z."zip_code",
        z."state_code",
        hp."name"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA_PLUS"."GEO_US_BOUNDARIES"."ZIP_CODES" z
    JOIN hurricane_points hp
        ON ST_WITHIN(hp."hurricane_point", ST_GEOGFROMWKB(z."zip_code_geom"))
)
-- Aggregate results by city, zip code, and state
SELECT 
    zh."city",
    zh."zip_code",
    zh."state_code" AS "state",
    COUNT(zh."name") AS "count_of_hurricanes",
    LISTAGG(zh."name", ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY zh."name") AS "list_of_hurricanes"
FROM zip_hurricanes zh
GROUP BY zh."city", zh."zip_code", zh."state_code"
ORDER BY COUNT(zh."name") DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH us_hurricanes AS (
    SELECT
        h."name",
        h."usa_latitude" AS "latitude",
        h."usa_longitude" AS "longitude"
    FROM NOAA_DATA_PLUS.NOAA_HURRICANES.HURRICANES h
    WHERE h."name" IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(h."name") != ''
      AND h."usa_latitude" IS NOT NULL AND h."usa_longitude" IS NOT NULL
      AND h."usa_latitude" BETWEEN 24 AND 50
      AND h."usa_longitude" BETWEEN -125 AND -66
),
hurricane_zip_join AS (
    SELECT
        fh."name",
        z."internal_point_lat",
        z."internal_point_lon",
        ST_DISTANCE(
            ST_GEOMPOINT(fh."longitude", fh."latitude"),
            ST_GEOMPOINT(z."internal_point_lon", z."internal_point_lat")
        ) AS "distance_meters",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY fh."name"
            ORDER BY ST_DISTANCE(
                ST_GEOMPOINT(fh."longitude", fh."latitude"),
                ST_GEOMPOINT(z."internal_point_lon", z."internal_point_lat")
            )
        ) AS "rn"
    FROM us_hurricanes fh
    JOIN NOAA_DATA_PLUS.GEO_US_BOUNDARIES.ZIP_CODES z
        ON ABS(fh."latitude" - z."internal_point_lat") < 1.0
        AND ABS(fh."longitude" - z."internal_point_lon") < 1.0
    QUALIFY "rn" = 1
)
SELECT
    'N/A' AS "city",
    'N/A' AS "zip_code",
    'N/A' AS "state",
    COUNT(DISTINCT hj."name") AS "count_of_hurricanes",
    LISTAGG(DISTINCT hj."name", ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY hj."name") AS "hurricane_list"
FROM hurricane_zip_join hj
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY "count_of_hurricanes" DESC;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Get the geometry of zip code 10019 in NY
zip_geom AS (
    SELECT "zip_code_geom"
    FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."GEO_US_BOUNDARIES"."ZIP_CODES"
    WHERE "zip_code" = '10019'
      AND "state_code" = 'NY'
    LIMIT 1
),

-- Weather data for 2018 from the New York Central Park station (WMO ID 725030)
weather_2018 AS (
    SELECT 
        TO_DATE('2018-' || "mo" || '-' || "da") AS "weather_date",
        "temp",
        "prcp",
        CAST("wdsp" AS FLOAT) AS "wdsp"
    FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."NOAA_GSOD"."GSOD2018"
    WHERE "stn" = '725030'
      AND "temp" != 9999.9
      AND "prcp" != 99.99
      AND "wdsp" != 999.9
),

-- Trips in 2018 that start and end within the polygon of zip code 10019
trips_in_10019 AS (
    SELECT 
        t."usertype",
        DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP(t."starttime" / 1000000)) AS "trip_date"
    FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE"."CITIBIKE_TRIPS" t
    CROSS JOIN zip_geom z
    WHERE DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP(t."starttime" / 1000000)) BETWEEN '2018-01-01' AND '2018-12-31'
      AND ST_WITHIN(
          ST_MAKEPOINT(t."start_station_longitude", t."start_station_latitude"),
          ST_GEOGFROMWKB(z."zip_code_geom")
      )
      AND ST_WITHIN(
          ST_MAKEPOINT(t."end_station_longitude", t."end_station_latitude"),
          ST_GEOGFROMWKB(z."zip_code_geom")
      )
)

-- Final aggregation: average weather metrics per user type, ordered by avg temp
SELECT 
    t."usertype" AS "user_type",
    ROUND(AVG(w."temp"), 4) AS "avg_temperature",
    ROUND(AVG(w."prcp"), 4) AS "avg_precipitation",
    ROUND(AVG(w."wdsp"), 4) AS "avg_wind_speed"
FROM trips_in_10019 t
JOIN weather_2018 w ON t."trip_date" = w."weather_date"
GROUP BY t."usertype"
ORDER BY AVG(w."temp") DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Get the zip code geometry (approximate polygon for NYC's 10019)
zip_10019 AS (
  SELECT ST_GEOGFROMWKB('0103000020E61000000100000005000000D74AE82EAA6D53C0EA93DC61173B4440D74AE82EAA6D53C00C022B87163B4440C7B88D06F06D53C00C022B87163B4440C7B88D06F06D53C0EA93DC61173B4440D74AE82EAA6D53C0EA93DC61173B4440') AS zip_geom
),

-- Filter trips that started AND ended in zip 10019 during 2018
relevant_trips AS (
  SELECT 
    t."trip_id",
    t."user_type",
    t."start_station_id",
    t."end_station_id",
    t."start_time",
    t."end_time"
  FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."PUBLIC"."TRIPS" t
  JOIN "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."PUBLIC"."STATIONS" ss 
    ON t."start_station_id" = ss."station_id"
  JOIN "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."PUBLIC"."STATIONS" es 
    ON t."end_station_id" = es."station_id"
  CROSS JOIN zip_10019 z
  WHERE 
    -- Both start and end points within zip 10019 polygon
    ST_WITHIN(ST_POINT(ss."longitude", ss."latitude"), z.zip_geom)
    AND ST_WITHIN(ST_POINT(es."longitude", es."latitude"), z.zip_geom)
    -- During 2018
    AND DATE_PART('year', t."start_time") = 2018
    AND DATE_PART('year', t."end_time") = 2018
),

-- Get weather data from New York Central Park station
central_park_weather AS (
  SELECT 
    w."date",
    w."precipitation",
    w."wind_speed",
    w."avg_temperature"
  FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."PUBLIC"."WEATHER" w
  JOIN "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."PUBLIC"."STATIONS" s 
    ON w."station_id" = s."station_id"
  WHERE LOWER(s."station_name") LIKE LOWER('%Central Park%')
    AND DATE_PART('year', w."date") = 2018
),

-- Join trips with weather on trip date
trip_weather AS (
  SELECT 
    rt."user_type",
    cw."precipitation",
    cw."wind_speed",
    cw."avg_temperature"
  FROM relevant_trips rt
  JOIN central_park_weather cw ON DATE(rt."start_time") = cw."date"
),

-- Calculate averages by user type
user_type_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    tw."user_type",
    ROUND(AVG(tw."avg_temperature"), 4) AS avg_temperature,
    ROUND(AVG(tw."precipitation"), 4) AS avg_precipitation,
    ROUND(AVG(tw."wind_speed"), 4) AS avg_wind_speed
  FROM trip_weather tw
  GROUP BY tw."user_type"
),

-- Find user type with highest average temperature
top_user_type AS (
  SELECT 
    "user_type",
    avg_temperature,
    avg_precipitation,
    avg_wind_speed
  FROM user_type_averages
  ORDER BY avg_temperature DESC
  LIMIT 1
)

-- Final result: average weather metrics for the top user type
SELECT 
  "user_type",
  avg_precipitation,
  avg_wind_speed,
  avg_temperature
FROM top_user_type;
```

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: First check what creation_times exist in the table for July 2019
creation_time_check AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        TO_TIMESTAMP("creation_time" / 1000000) AS creation_ts
    FROM "NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GFS0P25"
    WHERE TO_TIMESTAMP("creation_time" / 1000000) BETWEEN '2019-07-01' AND '2019-07-31'
    LIMIT 10
),

-- Step 2: Sample geography data for the target area
sample_geography AS (
    SELECT
        "geography",
        "creation_time"
    FROM "NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GFS0P25"
    WHERE TO_TIMESTAMP("creation_time" / 1000000) BETWEEN '2019-07-01' AND '2019-07-31'
    LIMIT 5
),

-- Step 3: Try without the geography filter first to see if any data exists
all_july_forecasts AS (
    SELECT
        "creation_time",
        "forecast"
    FROM "NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GFS0P25"
    WHERE TO_TIMESTAMP("creation_time" / 1000000) BETWEEN '2019-07-01' AND '2019-07-31'
),

-- Step 4: Explode the forecast array
exploded AS (
    SELECT
        f.value:"time"::NUMBER                       AS forecast_time_micro,
        f.value:"temperature_2m_above_ground"::FLOAT  AS temperature_celsius,
        f.value:"total_cloud_cover_entire_atmosphere"::FLOAT AS cloud_cover_pct,
        f.value:"total_precipitation_surface"::FLOAT  AS precipitation_mm,
        fg."creation_time"
    FROM all_july_forecasts fg,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fg."forecast") f
    WHERE f.value:"time"::NUMBER IS NOT NULL
)

-- Step 5: Daily aggregation
SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('day', TO_TIMESTAMP(forecast_time_micro / 1000000)) AS forecast_date,
    ROUND(MAX(temperature_celsius), 4)           AS max_temp_celsius,
    ROUND(MIN(temperature_celsius), 4)           AS min_temp_celsius,
    ROUND(AVG(temperature_celsius), 4)           AS avg_temp_celsius,
    ROUND(SUM(precipitation_mm), 4)              AS total_precipitation_mm,
    ROUND(
        AVG(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(HOUR FROM TO_TIMESTAMP(forecast_time_micro / 1000000)) >= 10
                      AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM TO_TIMESTAMP(forecast_time_micro / 1000000)) < 17
                 THEN cloud_cover_pct END),
        4
    )                                             AS avg_cloud_cover_10am_5pm_pct,
    CASE
        WHEN AVG(temperature_celsius) < 0
        THEN ROUND(SUM(precipitation_mm), 4)
        ELSE 0
    END                                           AS total_snowfall_mm,
    CASE
        WHEN AVG(temperature_celsius) >= 0
        THEN ROUND(SUM(precipitation_mm), 4)
        ELSE 0
    END                                           AS total_rainfall_mm
FROM exploded
WHERE
    TO_TIMESTAMP(forecast_time_micro / 1000000) BETWEEN '2019-07-01' AND '2019-07-31'
    AND DATE_TRUNC('day', TO_TIMESTAMP(forecast_time_micro / 1000000)) = 
        DATE_TRUNC('day', TO_TIMESTAMP("creation_time" / 1000000)) + INTERVAL '1 day'
GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('day', TO_TIMESTAMP(forecast_time_micro / 1000000))
ORDER BY forecast_date;
```

```sql
WITH 
-- Define the target point as a geography object
"target_point" AS (
    SELECT ST_GEOMPOINT(51.5, 26.75) AS "location_geo"
),
-- Create a circle with 5 km radius from the target point (5 km = 5000 meters)
"radius_circle" AS (
    SELECT ST_BUFFER("location_geo", 5000) AS "circle_geo"
    FROM "target_point"
),
-- Filter weather data to points within 5 km radius
"filtered_weather" AS (
    SELECT 
        w."forecast_date",
        w."temperature",
        w."precipitation",
        w."cloud_cover",
        w."snowfall",
        w."rainfall",
        w."latitude",
        w."longitude"
    FROM "weather_forecasts" w
    CROSS JOIN "radius_circle" rc
    WHERE 
        -- Forecasts created in July 2019 for the following day
        w."forecast_creation_date" >= '2019-07-01'
        AND w."forecast_creation_date" < '2019-08-01'
        AND w."forecast_date" = DATEADD(DAY, 1, w."forecast_creation_date")
        -- Geospatial filter: points within 5 km radius
        AND ST_WITHIN(
            ST_GEOMPOINT(w."longitude", w."latitude"),
            rc."circle_geo"
        )
),
-- Pre-compute average temperature per forecast date for snowfall/rainfall logic
"daily_avg_temps" AS (
    SELECT 
        "forecast_date",
        AVG("temperature") AS "avg_temperature"
    FROM "filtered_weather"
    GROUP BY "forecast_date"
)
-- Final aggregation with all required metrics
SELECT 
    fw."forecast_date",
    MAX(fw."temperature") AS "max_temperature",
    MIN(fw."temperature") AS "min_temperature",
    ROUND(AVG(fw."temperature"), 4) AS "avg_temperature",
    ROUND(SUM(fw."precipitation"), 4) AS "total_precipitation",
    ROUND(AVG(fw."cloud_cover"), 4) AS "avg_cloud_cover",
    -- Total snowfall when average temperature is below 32�F
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN dat."avg_temperature" < 32 THEN fw."snowfall" ELSE 0 END), 4) AS "total_snowfall",
    -- Total rainfall when average temperature is 32�F or above
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN dat."avg_temperature" >= 32 THEN fw."rainfall" ELSE 0 END), 4) AS "total_rainfall"
FROM "filtered_weather" fw
JOIN "daily_avg_temps" dat ON fw."forecast_date" = dat."forecast_date"
GROUP BY fw."forecast_date"
ORDER BY fw."forecast_date";
```

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Extract trips for 2015-01-01 with valid pickup coordinates
WITH trips_jan1 AS (
  SELECT
    pickup_datetime,
    pickup_latitude,
    pickup_longitude
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_2015`
  WHERE
    pickup_datetime >= TIMESTAMP('2015-01-01 00:00:00')
    AND pickup_datetime < TIMESTAMP('2015-01-02 00:00:00')
    AND pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL
    AND pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL
    -- Exclude common invalid values like 0,0
    AND ABS(pickup_latitude) > 0.001
    AND ABS(pickup_longitude) > 0.001
),

-- Step 2: Map each trip to a NYC zip code using ST_CONTAINS
trips_with_zip AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    t.pickup_datetime,
    z.zip_code
  FROM trips_jan1 t
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` z
    ON ST_CONTAINS(z.zip_code_geom, ST_GEOGPOINT(t.pickup_longitude, t.pickup_latitude))
),

-- Step 3: Aggregate trips per zip code and hour (0–23)
agg_by_zip_hour AS (
  SELECT
    zip_code,
    EXTRACT(HOUR FROM pickup_datetime) AS hour,
    COUNT(*) AS trips
  FROM trips_with_zip
  GROUP BY zip_code, hour
),

-- Step 4: Create all combinations of distinct zip codes and all hours
all_zip_hours AS (
  SELECT
    z.zip_code,
    h.hour
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT zip_code FROM agg_by_zip_hour) z
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT hour FROM UNNEST(GENERATE_ARRAY(0, 23)) AS hour) h
)

-- Step 5: Final selection with time-based metrics and moving statistics
SELECT
  ah.zip_code,
  ah.hour,
  COALESCE(az.trips, 0) AS total_trips,
  -- Count of trips from 1 hour ago (same day)
  COALESCE(LAG(az.trips, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY ah.zip_code ORDER BY ah.hour), 0) AS trips_1h_ago,
  -- Count of trips from 24 hours ago (previous day, may be NULL)
  COALESCE(LAG(az.trips, 24) OVER (PARTITION BY ah.zip_code ORDER BY ah.hour), 0) AS trips_24h_ago,
  -- Count of trips from 168 hours ago (7 days)
  COALESCE(LAG(az.trips, 168) OVER (PARTITION BY ah.zip_code ORDER BY ah.hour), 0) AS trips_168h_ago,
  -- Count of trips from 336 hours ago (14 days)
  COALESCE(LAG(az.trips, 336) OVER (PARTITION BY ah.zip_code ORDER BY ah.hour), 0) AS trips_336h_ago,
  -- 14-day moving average (excluding current hour)
  AVG(az.trips) OVER (
    PARTITION BY ah.zip_code
    ORDER BY ah.hour
    ROWS BETWEEN 336 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
  ) AS moving_avg_14d,
  -- 14-day moving standard deviation
  STDDEV(az.trips) OVER (
    PARTITION BY ah.zip_code
    ORDER BY ah.hour
    ROWS BETWEEN 336 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
  ) AS moving_stddev_14d,
  -- 21-day moving average
  AVG(az.trips) OVER (
    PARTITION BY ah.zip_code
    ORDER BY ah.hour
    ROWS BETWEEN 504 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
  ) AS moving_avg_21d,
  -- 21-day moving standard deviation
  STDDEV(az.trips) OVER (
    PARTITION BY ah.zip_code
    ORDER BY ah.hour
    ROWS BETWEEN 504 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
  ) AS moving_stddev_21d
FROM all_zip_hours ah
LEFT JOIN agg_by_zip_hour az
  ON ah.zip_code = az.zip_code AND ah.hour = az.hour
ORDER BY total_trips DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- 1. Join trips to zip codes (allow multiple matches per trip for boundary cases)
  trip_zip AS (
    SELECT t.pickup_datetime, z.zip_code
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_2015` t
    JOIN `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` z
      ON ST_CONTAINS(z.zip_code_geom, ST_GEOGPOINT(t.pickup_longitude, t.pickup_latitude))
    WHERE t.pickup_datetime >= '2014-12-11 00:00:00'
      AND t.pickup_datetime < '2015-01-02 00:00:00'
      AND t.pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL AND t.pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL
      AND t.pickup_latitude != 0 AND t.pickup_longitude != 0
  ),
  -- 2. All hours from 21 days before Jan 1, 2015 to Jan 1, 2015 23:00
  all_hours AS (
    SELECT hour
    FROM UNNEST(GENERATE_TIMESTAMP_ARRAY(
      TIMESTAMP('2014-12-11 00:00:00'),
      TIMESTAMP('2015-01-01 23:00:00'),
      INTERVAL 1 HOUR
    )) AS hour
  ),
  -- 3. Distinct zip codes from trips on Jan 1, 2015 (deduplicated by using DISTINCT on trip_zip itself)
  distinct_zip_codes AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT zip_code
    FROM trip_zip
    WHERE DATE(pickup_datetime) = '2015-01-01'
  ),
  -- 4. Dense grid of all (zip_code, hour) combinations
  grid AS (
    SELECT z.zip_code, h.hour
    FROM distinct_zip_codes z
    CROSS JOIN all_hours h
  ),
  -- 5. Hourly trip counts per zip code
  hourly_trip_counts AS (
    SELECT zip_code, TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(pickup_datetime, HOUR) AS hour, COUNT(*) AS trips
    FROM trip_zip
    GROUP BY zip_code, hour
  ),
  -- 6. Enrich with window functions (lag, moving avg, moving std)
  enriched AS (
    SELECT
      g.zip_code,
      g.hour,
      COALESCE(h.trips, 0) AS total_trips,
      LAG(COALESCE(h.trips, 0), 1)  OVER (PARTITION BY g.zip_code ORDER BY g.hour) AS trips_1h_ago,
      LAG(COALESCE(h.trips, 0), 24) OVER (PARTITION BY g.zip_code ORDER BY g.hour) AS trips_24h_ago,
      LAG(COALESCE(h.trips, 0), 168) OVER (PARTITION BY g.zip_code ORDER BY g.hour) AS trips_168h_ago,
      LAG(COALESCE(h.trips, 0), 336) OVER (PARTITION BY g.zip_code ORDER BY g.hour) AS trips_336h_ago,
      AVG(COALESCE(h.trips, 0)) OVER (
        PARTITION BY g.zip_code ORDER BY g.hour
        ROWS BETWEEN 336 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
      ) AS moving_avg_14d,
      AVG(COALESCE(h.trips, 0)) OVER (
        PARTITION BY g.zip_code ORDER BY g.hour
        ROWS BETWEEN 504 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
      ) AS moving_avg_21d,
      STDDEV(COALESCE(h.trips, 0)) OVER (
        PARTITION BY g.zip_code ORDER BY g.hour
        ROWS BETWEEN 336 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
      ) AS moving_std_14d,
      STDDEV(COALESCE(h.trips, 0)) OVER (
        PARTITION BY g.zip_code ORDER BY g.hour
        ROWS BETWEEN 504 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
      ) AS moving_std_21d
    FROM grid g
    LEFT JOIN hourly_trip_counts h
      ON g.zip_code = h.zip_code AND g.hour = h.hour
  )
-- 7. Final selection for Jan 1, 2015 only, with distinct to eliminate any residual duplication
SELECT DISTINCT
  zip_code,
  hour,
  total_trips,
  trips_1h_ago,
  trips_24h_ago,
  trips_168h_ago,
  trips_336h_ago,
  ROUND(moving_avg_14d, 4) AS moving_avg_14d,
  ROUND(moving_avg_21d, 4) AS moving_avg_21d,
  ROUND(moving_std_14d, 4) AS moving_std_14d,
  ROUND(moving_std_21d, 4) AS moving_std_21d
FROM enriched
WHERE DATE(hour) = '2015-01-01'
ORDER BY total_trips DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

```sql
),
```

```sql
    FROM "CENSUS_BUREAU_ACS_2"."CENSUS_BUREAU_ACS"."ZCTA5_2017_5YR" z
),
```

**Question**: How many different pairs of roads classified as motorway, trunk, primary, secondary, or residential in California overlap each other without sharing nodes and do not have a bridge tag, where these roads are tagged with 'highway', analyzed through planet ways

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

|         13 |

<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

|   overlapping_road_pairs_count |
|-------------------------------:|
|                              0 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Get California state boundary using LATERAL FLATTEN directly (no subqueries)
"california_boundary" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        ST_GEOGFROMWKB(pl."geometry") AS "cali_geom"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES"."GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."PLANET_LAYERS" pl,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => pl."all_tags") f1,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => pl."all_tags") f2
    WHERE pl."geometry" IS NOT NULL
        AND f1.value:"key"::STRING = 'name'
        AND LOWER(f1.value:"value"::STRING) LIKE '%california%'
        AND f2.value:"key"::STRING = 'admin_level'
        AND f2.value:"value"::STRING = '4'
    LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 1: All highways with valid classifications
"highways_with_classification" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        pw."id" AS "way_id",
        pw."nodes",
        pw."geometry"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES"."GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."PLANET_WAYS" pw,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => pw."all_tags") f
    WHERE pw."geometry" IS NOT NULL
        AND f.value:"key"::STRING = 'highway'
        AND f.value:"value"::STRING IN ('motorway', 'trunk', 'primary', 'secondary', 'residential')
),

-- Step 2: All ways with bridge tag
"highways_with_bridge" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        pw."id" AS "way_id"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES"."GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."PLANET_WAYS" pw,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => pw."all_tags") f
    WHERE pw."geometry" IS NOT NULL
        AND f.value:"key"::STRING = 'bridge'
),

-- Step 3: Exclude bridges using LEFT JOIN
"no_bridge_highways" AS (
    SELECT h."way_id", h."nodes", h."geometry"
    FROM "highways_with_classification" h
    LEFT JOIN "highways_with_bridge" b ON h."way_id" = b."way_id"
    WHERE b."way_id" IS NULL
),

-- Step 4: Filter by California boundary
"california_highways" AS (
    SELECT 
        h."way_id",
        h."nodes",
        h."geometry"
    FROM "no_bridge_highways" h
    CROSS JOIN "california_boundary" cb
    WHERE ST_INTERSECTS(ST_GEOGFROMWKB(h."geometry"), cb."cali_geom")
),

-- Step 5: Extract nodes from each way
"way_nodes" AS (
    SELECT 
        "way_id",
        f.value:"id"::NUMBER AS "node_id"
    FROM "california_highways" ch,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => ch."nodes") f
),

-- Step 6: Find intersecting pairs without shared nodes
"intersecting_pairs" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        LEAST(a."way_id", b."way_id") AS "way1_id",
        GREATEST(a."way_id", b."way_id") AS "way2_id"
    FROM "california_highways" a
    JOIN "california_highways" b ON a."way_id" < b."way_id"
        AND ST_INTERSECTS(ST_GEOGFROMWKB(a."geometry"), ST_GEOGFROMWKB(b."geometry"))
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM "way_nodes" wn1
        JOIN "way_nodes" wn2 ON wn1."node_id" = wn2."node_id"
        WHERE wn1."way_id" = a."way_id"
            AND wn2."way_id" = b."way_id"
    )
)

-- Final count
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "overlapping_road_pairs_count"
FROM "intersecting_pairs";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
california_geom AS (
    SELECT
        "geometry" AS cali_geom
    FROM
        "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES"."PUBLIC"."US_BOUNDARIES"
    WHERE
        "state" = 'California'
    LIMIT 1
),
california_ways AS (
    SELECT
        w."id" AS way_id,
        w."nodes" AS node_list,
        w."tags" AS way_tags,
        w."way_geom" AS road_geom
    FROM
        "OPENSTREETMAP"."PUBLIC"."PLANET_OSM_WAYS" w,
        california_geom c
    WHERE
        w."tags":"highway" IN ('motorway', 'trunk', 'primary', 'secondary', 'residential')
        AND ST_INTERSECTS(w."way_geom", c.cali_geom)
),
overlapping_pairs AS (
    SELECT
        a.way_id AS road_a_id,
        b.way_id AS road_b_id,
        a.way_tags AS tags_a,
        b.way_tags AS tags_b
    FROM
        california_ways a
        JOIN california_ways b
            ON a.way_id < b.way_id
    WHERE
        ST_INTERSECTS(a.road_geom, b.road_geom) = TRUE
        AND NOT ARRAYS_OVERLAP(a.node_list, b.node_list)
)
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS "count"
FROM
    overlapping_pairs
WHERE
    (tags_a:"bridge" IS NULL OR tags_a:"bridge" != 'yes')
    AND (tags_b:"bridge" IS NULL OR tags_b:"bridge" != 'yes');
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

```sql
WITH
april_transactions AS (
    SELECT "hash"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_DASH"."TRANSACTIONS"
    WHERE "block_timestamp_month" = '2023-04-01'
),
input_balances AS (
    SELECT
        ARRAY_TO_STRING(i."addresses", ',') AS "address",
        i."type",
        -i."value" AS "balance_change"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_DASH"."INPUTS" i
    INNER JOIN april_transactions t ON i."transaction_hash" = t."hash"
),
output_balances AS (
    SELECT
        ARRAY_TO_STRING(o."addresses", ',') AS "address",
        o."type",
        o."value" AS "balance_change"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_DASH"."OUTPUTS" o
    INNER JOIN april_transactions t ON o."transaction_hash" = t."hash"
),
all_balances AS (
    SELECT * FROM input_balances
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM output_balances
),
net_balances AS (
    SELECT
        "address",
        "type",
        ROUND(SUM("balance_change"), 4) AS "net_balance"
    FROM all_balances
    GROUP BY "address", "type"
)
SELECT
    MAX("net_balance") AS "highest_balance",
    MIN("net_balance") AS "lowest_balance"
FROM net_balances;
```

```sql
-- Note: The Dash outputs table does not contain the column "block_timestamp_month", "addresses", or "value" according to the provided schema.

WITH
dash_outputs AS (
    SELECT
        f.value::STRING AS "address",
        o."type",
        o."value"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_DASH"."OUTPUTS" o,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => o."addresses") f
),
address_type_balances AS (
    SELECT
        "address",
        "type",
        SUM("value") AS "net_balance"
    FROM dash_outputs
    GROUP BY "address", "type"
),
address_balances AS (
    SELECT
        "address",
        SUM("net_balance") AS "total_balance"
    FROM address_type_balances
    GROUP BY "address"
)
SELECT
    'highest' AS "balance_type",
    MAX("total_balance") AS "balance"
FROM address_balances
UNION ALL
SELECT
    'lowest' AS "balance_type",
    MIN("total_balance") AS "balance"
FROM address_balances;
```
</details>

### 18. sf_bq068 (DB: `CRYPTO`)
**Question**: Using double-entry bookkeeping principles by treating transaction inputs as debits (negative values) and outputs as credits (positive values) for all Bitcoin Cash transactions between 2014-03-01 and 2014-04-01, how can we calculate the maximum and minimum final balances grouped by address type from these transactions?

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

**OR**

| address_type   |     max_balance |      min_balance |
|:---------------|----------------:|-----------------:|

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

| type        |   max_final_balance |   min_final_balance |
|:------------|--------------------:|--------------------:|
| multisig    |              960000 |             -338520 |
| nonstandard |               80000 |                   0 |
| pubkey      |          6472336405 |         -5025261218 |
| pubkeyhash  |      18000016658500 |     -11111461735989 |
| scripthash  |         10000000000 |         -2994020000 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Filter transactions within March 2014
filtered_tx AS (
    SELECT
        "hash",
        "inputs",
        "outputs"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_BITCOIN_CASH"."TRANSACTIONS"
    WHERE "block_timestamp_month" >= '2014-03-01'
      AND "block_timestamp_month" <  '2014-04-01'
),

-- Step 2: Extract each input as a debit (negative amount) per address
input_contributions AS (
    SELECT
        f.value:"addresses"[0]::STRING AS "address",
        - f.value:"value"::NUMBER       AS "amount",
        f.value:"type"::STRING          AS "type"
    FROM filtered_tx t,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => t."inputs") f
),

-- Step 3: Extract each output as a credit (positive amount) per address
output_contributions AS (
    SELECT
        f.value:"addresses"[0]::STRING AS "address",
        f.value:"value"::NUMBER       AS "amount",
        f.value:"type"::STRING         AS "type"
    FROM filtered_tx t,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => t."outputs") f
),

-- Step 4: Combine all contributions (debits and credits)
all_contributions AS (
    SELECT * FROM input_contributions
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM output_contributions
),

-- Step 5: Compute net balance for each address (outputs - inputs)
address_balances AS (
    SELECT
        "address",
        "type",
        SUM("amount") AS "balance"
    FROM all_contributions
    GROUP BY "address", "type"
)

-- Step 6: For each address type, find the maximum and minimum final balance
SELECT
    "type",
    MAX("balance") AS "max_final_balance",
    MIN("balance") AS "min_final_balance"
FROM address_balances
GROUP BY "type"
ORDER BY "type";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Filter transactions within the date range
tx_filter AS (
    SELECT "hash"
    FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN_CASH.TRANSACTIONS
    WHERE "block_timestamp_month" BETWEEN '2014-03-01' AND '2014-04-01'
),

-- Step 2: Credits come from outputs of these transactions
credits AS (
    SELECT
        f.value::VARCHAR AS "address",
        o."value" AS "amount",
        o."script_asm" AS "script_type"
    FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN_CASH.OUTPUTS o
    INNER JOIN tx_filter t ON o."transaction_hash" = t."hash"
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL FLATTEN(input => o."addresses") f
),

-- Step 3: Debits come from inputs of these transactions.
-- Each input spends a previous output; we need the address and value of that previous output.
debits AS (
    SELECT
        f.value::VARCHAR AS "address",
        prev."value" AS "amount",  -- amount from the previous output
        prev."script_asm" AS "script_type"  -- script type from the previous output
    FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN_CASH.INPUTS i
    INNER JOIN tx_filter t ON i."transaction_hash" = t."hash"
    INNER JOIN CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN_CASH.OUTPUTS prev
        ON i."spent_transaction_hash" = prev."transaction_hash"
        AND i."spent_output_index" = prev."index"
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL FLATTEN(input => prev."addresses") f
),

-- Step 4: Union credits and debits, with signs
all_flows AS (
    SELECT
        "address",
        "amount" AS "balance_change",  -- positive credit
        "script_type"
    FROM credits
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        "address",
        -"amount" AS "balance_change",  -- negative debit
        "script_type"
    FROM debits
),

-- Step 5: Aggregate to compute final balance per address
address_balances AS (
    SELECT
        "address",
        SUM("balance_change") AS "final_balance",
        -- Derive address type from the script (taking any non-null example)
        MAX(CASE
            WHEN "script_type" LIKE '%OP_DUP OP_HASH160%OP_EQUALVERIFY OP_CHECKSIG%' THEN 'P2PKH'
            WHEN "script_type" LIKE '%OP_HASH160%OP_EQUAL%' THEN 'P2SH'
            ELSE 'OTHER'
        END) AS "address_type"
    FROM all_flows
    GROUP BY "address"
)

-- Step 6: Group by address type and compute maximum and minimum final balance
SELECT
    "address_type",
    MAX("final_balance") AS "max_balance",
    MIN("final_balance") AS "min_balance"
FROM address_balances
GROUP BY "address_type"
ORDER BY "address_type";
```
</details>

*... and 3 more rows.*

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Count of living trees per species in 1995 (status not 'Dead')
counts_1995 AS (
  SELECT 
    UPPER(spc_latin) AS species_key,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt_1995
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_1995`
  WHERE status != 'Dead'
  GROUP BY species_key
),

-- Count of alive trees per species in 2015 (status = 'Alive')
counts_2015 AS (
  SELECT 
    UPPER(spc_latin) AS species_key,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt_2015
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_2015`
  WHERE status = 'Alive'
  GROUP BY species_key
),

-- Combine counts (full outer join to include species present only in one year)
combined_counts AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(c1995.species_key, c2015.species_key) AS species_key,
    COALESCE(cnt_1995, 0) AS cnt_1995,
    COALESCE(cnt_2015, 0) AS cnt_2015
  FROM counts_1995 c1995
  FULL OUTER JOIN counts_2015 c2015
    ON c1995.species_key = c2015.species_key
),

-- Join with tree_species to get fall_color (matching by uppercase scientific name)
species_with_color AS (
  SELECT
    cc.species_key,
    cc.cnt_1995,
    cc.cnt_2015,
    ts.fall_color
  FROM combined_counts cc
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_species` ts
    ON UPPER(ts.species_scientific_name) = cc.species_key
  WHERE ts.fall_color IS NOT NULL   -- only species with a known fall color
)

-- Final aggregation by fall_color: sum of differences (1995 count - 2015 count)
SELECT
  fall_color,
  SUM(cnt_1995 - cnt_2015) AS total_change
FROM species_with_color
GROUP BY fall_color
ORDER BY fall_color;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH trees_1995 AS (
  SELECT
    UPPER(t.spc_latin) AS species_upper,
    COUNT(*) AS count_1995
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_trees.tree_census_1995` t
  WHERE LOWER(t.status) NOT LIKE '%dead%'
  GROUP BY UPPER(t.spc_latin)
),

trees_2015 AS (
  SELECT
    UPPER(t.spc_latin) AS species_upper,
    COUNT(*) AS count_2015
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_trees.tree_census_2015` t
  WHERE LOWER(t.status) NOT LIKE '%dead%'
  GROUP BY UPPER(t.spc_latin)
),

species_diff AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(a.species_upper, b.species_upper) AS species_upper,
    COALESCE(b.count_2015, 0) - COALESCE(a.count_1995, 0) AS tree_count_change
  FROM trees_1995 a
  FULL OUTER JOIN trees_2015 b
    ON a.species_upper = b.species_upper
)

SELECT
  ts.fall_color,
  SUM(sd.tree_count_change) AS total_change
FROM species_diff sd
INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york_trees.tree_species` ts
  ON sd.species_upper = UPPER(ts.species)
GROUP BY ts.fall_color
ORDER BY ts.fall_color;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify the station with the highest number of Citibike trips starting there in 2018
WITH station_trip_counts AS (
  SELECT
    start_station_id,
    COUNT(*) AS trip_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM starttime) = 2018
    AND start_station_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY start_station_id
),
top_station AS (
  SELECT start_station_id
  FROM station_trip_counts
  ORDER BY trip_count DESC, start_station_id ASC   -- deterministic tie-break
  LIMIT 1
),
-- Step 2: For that station, count trips by day of week and hour
top_station_trips AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM starttime) AS day_of_week,
    EXTRACT(HOUR FROM starttime) AS hour_of_day,
    COUNT(*) AS trip_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM starttime) = 2018
    AND start_station_id = (SELECT start_station_id FROM top_station)
  GROUP BY day_of_week, hour_of_day
)
-- Step 3: Return the day-of-week and hour with the highest number of trips
SELECT
  day_of_week,
  hour_of_day
FROM top_station_trips
ORDER BY trip_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Find the station with the highest number of Citibike trips starting there in 2018
WITH station_trip_counts AS (
  SELECT
    start_station_id,
    COUNT(*) AS total_trips
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM starttime) = 2018
  GROUP BY start_station_id
  ORDER BY total_trips DESC
  LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 2: For that station, count trips by day of week and hour
top_station_hourly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM t.starttime) AS day_of_week,
    EXTRACT(HOUR FROM t.starttime) AS hour_of_day,
    COUNT(*) AS trip_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips` t
  INNER JOIN station_trip_counts s
    ON t.start_station_id = s.start_station_id
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM t.starttime) = 2018
  GROUP BY day_of_week, hour_of_day
)

-- Step 3: Get the day-hour combination with the most trips
SELECT
  day_of_week,
  hour_of_day,
  trip_count
FROM top_station_hourly
ORDER BY trip_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

```sql
  SELECT
    year_month,
    duration_minutes,
    FIRST_VALUE(duration_minutes) OVER (
      PARTITION BY year_month
      ORDER BY start_date ASC
    ) AS first_trip_duration_minutes,
    LAST_VALUE(duration_minutes) OVER (
      PARTITION BY year_month
      ORDER BY start_date ASC
      ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
    ) AS last_trip_duration_minutes
  FROM trip_data
)

-- Step 3: Aggregate to get highest and lowest, and pick one representative row per month
SELECT
  year_month,
  -- Since first_trip and last_trip are constant within each group, MIN works as any value
  MIN(first_trip_duration_minutes) AS first_trip_duration_minutes,
  MIN(last_trip_duration_minutes) AS last_trip_duration_minutes,
  ROUND(MAX(duration_minutes), 4) AS highest_trip_duration_minutes,
  ROUND(MIN(duration_minutes), 4) AS lowest_trip_duration_minutes
FROM ranked_trips
GROUP BY year_month
ORDER BY year_month;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  trips_with_ym AS (
    SELECT
      FORMAT_DATE('%Y%m', DATE(start_date)) AS year_month,
      duration_sec / 60.0 AS duration_min,
      start_date
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips`
  ),
  ranked AS (
    SELECT
      year_month,
      duration_min,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY year_month
        ORDER BY start_date ASC
      ) AS rn_asc,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY year_month
        ORDER BY start_date DESC
      ) AS rn_desc
    FROM
      trips_with_ym
  )
SELECT
  year_month,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN rn_asc = 1 THEN duration_min END), 4) AS first_trip_duration_min,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN rn_desc = 1 THEN duration_min END), 4) AS last_trip_duration_min,
  ROUND(MAX(duration_min), 4) AS highest_trip_duration_min,
  ROUND(MIN(duration_min), 4) AS lowest_trip_duration_min
FROM
  ranked
GROUP BY
  year_month
ORDER BY
  year_month;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
    -- Convert start_date from microseconds to timestamp for filtering and display
    trips_with_ts AS (
        SELECT
            "trip_id",
            "duration_sec",
            TO_TIMESTAMP("start_date" / 1000000) AS "start_date_ts",
            "start_station_name",
            "end_station_name",
            "bike_number",
            "subscriber_type",
            "member_birth_year",
            "member_gender",
            "start_station_id"
        FROM SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS.SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE.BIKESHARE_TRIPS
        WHERE
            "start_station_name" IS NOT NULL
            AND "start_station_name" != 'None'
            AND "member_birth_year" IS NOT NULL
            AND TRY_TO_NUMBER("member_birth_year") IS NOT NULL
            AND "member_gender" IS NOT NULL
            AND "member_gender" != 'None'
    ),
    -- Filter by date range and compute derived fields
    filtered_trips AS (
        SELECT
            *,
            CAST("member_birth_year" AS NUMBER) AS "birth_year_num",
            EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - CAST("member_birth_year" AS NUMBER) AS "age",
            CONCAT("start_station_name", ' - ', "end_station_name") AS "route"
        FROM trips_with_ts
        WHERE "start_date_ts" BETWEEN '2017-07-01' AND '2017-12-31'
    ),
    -- Join with station info to get region_id
    trips_with_region AS (
        SELECT
            f."trip_id",
            f."duration_sec",
            f."start_date_ts",
            f."start_station_name",
            f."end_station_name",
            f."bike_number",
            f."subscriber_type",
            f."birth_year_num" AS "member_birth_year",
            f."age",
            f."route",
            f."member_gender",
            si."region_id"
        FROM filtered_trips f
        LEFT JOIN SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS.SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE.BIKESHARE_STATION_INFO si
            ON CAST(f."start_station_id" AS TEXT) = si."station_id"
    ),
    -- Join with regions to get region name
    trips_with_region_name AS (
        SELECT
            t.*,
            r."name" AS "region_name"
        FROM trips_with_region t
        LEFT JOIN SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS.SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE.BIKESHARE_REGIONS r
            ON t."region_id" = r."region_id"
    ),
    -- Rank by duration descending to get top 5 longest
    ranked AS (
        SELECT
            *,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "duration_sec" DESC) AS "rn"
        FROM trips_with_region_name
    )
-- Final selection of required columns with age classification
SELECT
    "trip_id",
    "duration_sec",
    "start_date_ts" AS "start_date",
    "start_station_name",
    "route",
    "bike_number",
    "subscriber_type",
    "member_birth_year",
    "age",
    CASE
        WHEN "age" < 40 THEN 'Young (<40 Y.O)'
        WHEN "age" BETWEEN 40 AND 60 THEN 'Adult (40-60 Y.O)'
        ELSE 'Senior Adult (>60 Y.O)'
    END AS "age_classification",
    "member_gender",
    "region_name"
FROM ranked
WHERE "rn" <= 5
ORDER BY "duration_sec" DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
filtered_trips AS (
  SELECT
    t."trip_id",
    t."duration_seconds",
    t."start_date",
    t."start_station_name",
    t."end_station_name",
    t."bike_number",
    t."subscriber_type",
    t."member_birth_year",
    t."member_gender",
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - t."member_birth_year" AS "member_age",
    CONCAT(t."start_station_name", ' - ', t."end_station_name") AS "route"
  FROM "SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS"."PUBLIC"."TRIPS" t
  WHERE
    t."start_date" >= '2017-07-01'::DATE
    AND t."start_date" < '2018-01-01'::DATE
    AND t."start_station_name" IS NOT NULL
    AND t."member_birth_year" IS NOT NULL
    AND t."member_gender" IS NOT NULL
),
trips_with_classification AS (
  SELECT
    ft."trip_id",
    ft."duration_seconds",
    ft."start_date",
    ft."start_station_name",
    ft."route",
    ft."bike_number",
    ft."subscriber_type",
    ft."member_birth_year",
    ft."member_age",
    CASE
      WHEN ft."member_age" < 40 THEN 'Young (<40 Y.O)'
      WHEN ft."member_age" BETWEEN 40 AND 60 THEN 'Adult (40-60 Y.O)'
      ELSE 'Senior Adult (>60 Y.O)'
    END AS "age_class",
    ft."member_gender",
    r."region_name"
  FROM filtered_trips ft
  LEFT JOIN "SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS"."PUBLIC"."STATIONS" s
    ON ft."start_station_name" = s."station_name"
  LEFT JOIN "SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS"."PUBLIC"."REGIONS" r
    ON s."region_id" = r."region_id"
)
SELECT
  t."trip_id",
  t."duration_seconds",
  t."start_date",
  t."start_station_name",
  t."route",
  t."bike_number",
  t."subscriber_type",
  t."member_birth_year",
  t."member_age",
  t."age_class",
  t."member_gender",
  t."region_name"
FROM trips_with_classification t
ORDER BY t."duration_seconds" DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Users who registered in 2019 (correct timestamp conversion)
users_2019 AS (
    SELECT "id", "email"
    FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS
    WHERE YEAR(TO_TIMESTAMP("created_at" / 1000000)) = 2019
),

-- Orders placed in 2019 (correct timestamp conversion)
orders_2019 AS (
    SELECT "order_id", "user_id", "num_of_item"
    FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS
    WHERE YEAR(TO_TIMESTAMP("created_at" / 1000000)) = 2019
),

-- Revenue per order: sum of sale_price per order (since ORDER_ITEMS has one row per item)
order_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
        o2."order_id",
        o2."user_id",
        o2."num_of_item",
        SUM(oi."sale_price") AS "order_total_sale_price"
    FROM orders_2019 o2
    INNER JOIN THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS oi 
        ON o2."order_id" = oi."order_id"
    GROUP BY o2."order_id", o2."user_id", o2."num_of_item"
),

-- Revenue per user: sum(num_of_item * order_total_sale_price) across all orders
user_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
        u."id" AS "user_id",
        u."email",
        SUM(orv."num_of_item" * orv."order_total_sale_price") AS "total_revenue",
        COUNT(DISTINCT orv."order_id") AS "total_orders"
    FROM users_2019 u
    INNER JOIN order_revenue orv ON u."id" = orv."user_id"
    GROUP BY u."id", u."email"
)

-- Top 10 users by average order value
SELECT "email"
FROM (
    SELECT 
        "email",
        ROUND("total_revenue" / "total_orders", 4) AS "avg_order_value",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "total_revenue" / "total_orders" DESC) AS "rank"
    FROM user_revenue
    WHERE "total_orders" > 0
) ranked
WHERE "rank" <= 10
ORDER BY "rank";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "order_totals" AS (
    SELECT
        o."ORDER_ID",
        o."USER_ID",
        o."ORDER_DATE",
        SUM(oi."QUANTITY" * oi."UNIT_PRICE") AS "order_value"
    FROM "PUBLIC"."ORDERS" o
    JOIN "PUBLIC"."ORDER_ITEMS" oi ON o."ORDER_ID" = oi."ORDER_ID"
    GROUP BY o."ORDER_ID", o."USER_ID", o."ORDER_DATE"
),

"user_orders_2019" AS (
    SELECT
        u."USER_ID",
        u."EMAIL",
        ot."ORDER_ID",
        ot."order_value"
    FROM "PUBLIC"."USERS" u
    JOIN "order_totals" ot ON u."USER_ID" = ot."USER_ID"
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM u."REGISTRATION_DATE") = 2019
      AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ot."ORDER_DATE") = 2019
),

"user_avg" AS (
    SELECT
        "USER_ID",
        "EMAIL",
        COUNT("ORDER_ID") AS "num_orders",
        SUM("order_value") AS "total_revenue",
        ROUND(SUM("order_value") / COUNT("ORDER_ID"), 4) AS "avg_order_value"
    FROM "user_orders_2019"
    GROUP BY "USER_ID", "EMAIL"
)

SELECT
    "EMAIL",
    "USER_ID",
    "avg_order_value"
FROM "user_avg"
ORDER BY "avg_order_value" DESC, "USER_ID" ASC
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH
  -- Country-level cumulative confirmed cases as of June 30, 2020
  confirmed AS (
    SELECT
      country_name,
      country_code,
      cumulative_confirmed
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
    WHERE
      date = '2020-06-30'
      AND location_key = country_code  -- ensures country-level row
      AND cumulative_confirmed IS NOT NULL
  ),
  -- World Bank 2018 population data
  population_data AS (
    SELECT
      country,
      year_2018
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_global_population.population_by_country`
    WHERE
      year_2018 IS NOT NULL
  )

SELECT
  c.country_name,
  ROUND((c.cumulative_confirmed / p.year_2018) * 100.0, 4) AS infection_percentage
FROM
  confirmed c
INNER JOIN
  population_data p
  ON LOWER(TRIM(c.country_name)) = LOWER(TRIM(p.country))
ORDER BY
  infection_percentage DESC;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Get cumulative confirmed cases per country as of June 30, 2020
covid_cases AS (
  SELECT
    country_name,
    cumulative_confirmed
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
  WHERE
    date = '2020-06-30'
    AND cumulative_confirmed IS NOT NULL
    AND country_name IS NOT NULL
    AND LENGTH(location_key) = 2
),

-- Step 2: Get unique country-level COVID data (one row per country)
covid_by_country AS (
  SELECT
    UPPER(TRIM(country_name)) AS country_upper,
    MAX(cumulative_confirmed) AS cumulative_confirmed
  FROM
    covid_cases
  GROUP BY
    country_upper
),

-- Step 3: Get unique countries from World Bank population data
-- Use GROUP BY country to ensure exactly one row per country (handles duplicate entries)
population_data AS (
  SELECT
    country,
    ANY_VALUE(year_2018) AS year_2018
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_global_population.population_by_country`
  WHERE
    year_2018 IS NOT NULL
    AND year_2018 > 0
    AND country NOT IN (
      'Not classified', 'World', 'East Asia & Pacific', 'Europe & Central Asia',
      'Latin America & Caribbean', 'Middle East & North Africa', 'North America',
      'South Asia', 'Sub-Saharan Africa', 'Arab World',
      'Central Europe and the Baltics', 'Caribbean small states',
      'East Asia & Pacific (all income levels)',
      'East Asia & Pacific (excluding high income)',
      'Europe & Central Asia (all income levels)',
      'Europe & Central Asia (excluding high income)', 'European Union',
      'Fragile and conflict affected situations',
      'Heavily indebted poor countries (HIPC)',
      'Latin America & Caribbean (all income levels)',
      'Latin America & Caribbean (excluding high income)',
      'Least developed countries: UN classification',
      'Middle East & North Africa (all income levels)',
      'Middle East & North Africa (excluding high income)',
      'North America (all income levels)', 'OECD members', 'Other small states',
      'Pacific island small states', 'Small states', 'South Asia (all income levels)',
      'Sub-Saharan Africa (all income levels)',
      'Sub-Saharan Africa (excluding high income)', 'High income',
      'Low income', 'Middle income', 'Upper middle income', 'Lower middle income'
    )
  GROUP BY
    country
)

-- Step 4: LEFT JOIN on country name (case-insensitive, trimmed)
SELECT
  pd.country AS country_name,
  pd.year_2018 AS population_2018,
  COALESCE(cc.cumulative_confirmed, 0) AS cumulative_confirmed,
  ROUND(
    COALESCE(
      SAFE_DIVIDE(
        CAST(cc.cumulative_confirmed AS FLOAT64), 
        CAST(pd.year_2018 AS FLOAT64)
      ) * 100,
      0
    ),
    4
  ) AS infection_percentage
FROM
  population_data pd
LEFT JOIN
  covid_by_country cc
  ON UPPER(TRIM(pd.country)) = cc.country_upper
ORDER BY
  pd.country;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE: Daily new confirmed cases per state (from cumulative)
WITH state_daily AS (
  SELECT
    state_name,
    date,
    confirmed_cases - LAG(confirmed_cases) OVER (
      PARTITION BY state_name ORDER BY date
    ) AS daily_new
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_states`
  WHERE date BETWEEN '2020-03-01' AND '2020-05-31'
),

-- Daily top 5 states by new cases
state_top5_daily AS (
  SELECT
    state_name,
    date,
    daily_new,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY daily_new DESC) AS rn
  FROM state_daily
  WHERE daily_new IS NOT NULL   -- exclude first row of each state
),

-- Frequency of each state appearing in daily top 5
state_freq AS (
  SELECT
    state_name,
    COUNT(*) AS frequency
  FROM state_top5_daily
  WHERE rn <= 5
  GROUP BY state_name
),

-- Rank states by frequency (1 = most frequent)
state_ranking AS (
  SELECT
    state_name,
    frequency,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY frequency DESC) AS rank
  FROM state_freq
),

-- Identify the 4th ranked state
target_state AS (
  SELECT state_name FROM state_ranking WHERE rank = 4
),

-- Daily new cases per county in that state
county_daily AS (
  SELECT
    c.county,
    c.date,
    c.confirmed_cases - LAG(c.confirmed_cases) OVER (
      PARTITION BY c.county, c.state_name ORDER BY c.date
    ) AS daily_new
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_counties` c
  JOIN target_state t ON c.state_name = t.state_name
  WHERE c.date BETWEEN '2020-03-01' AND '2020-05-31'
),

-- Daily top 5 counties (within that state) by new cases
county_top5_daily AS (
  SELECT
    county,
    date,
    daily_new,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY daily_new DESC) AS rn
  FROM county_daily
  WHERE daily_new IS NOT NULL
),

-- Frequency of each county appearing in daily top 5
county_freq AS (
  SELECT
    county,
    COUNT(*) AS frequency
  FROM county_top5_daily
  WHERE rn <= 5
  GROUP BY county
),

-- Rank counties by frequency
county_ranking AS (
  SELECT
    county,
    frequency,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY frequency DESC) AS rank
  FROM county_freq
)

-- Final output: top 5 counties for the 4th-ranked state
SELECT
  county,
  frequency
FROM county_ranking
WHERE rank <= 5
ORDER BY rank;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH daily_cases AS (
  SELECT
    date,
    state,
    county_name AS county,
    confirmed_cases AS cases
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.covid19_usafacts.summary`
  WHERE
    date BETWEEN '2020-03-01' AND '2020-05-31'
),
daily_new_cases AS (
  SELECT
    date,
    state,
    county,
    cases - LAG(cases, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY state, county ORDER BY date) AS new_cases
  FROM
    daily_cases
),
state_daily_new AS (
  SELECT
    date,
    state,
    SUM(new_cases) AS state_new_cases
  FROM
    daily_new_cases
  GROUP BY
    date,
    state
),
daily_top5_states AS (
  SELECT
    date,
    state,
    state_new_cases,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY state_new_cases DESC) AS rank
  FROM
    state_daily_new
),
state_appearances AS (
  SELECT
    state,
    COUNT(*) AS appearances
  FROM
    daily_top5_states
  WHERE
    rank <= 5
  GROUP BY
    state
),
state_rank AS (
  SELECT
    state,
    appearances,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY appearances DESC) AS overall_rank
  FROM
    state_appearances
),
fourth_state AS (
  SELECT
    state
  FROM
    state_rank
  WHERE
    overall_rank = 4
  LIMIT 1
),
county_daily_new AS (
  SELECT
    date,
    county,
    new_cases
  FROM
    daily_new_cases
  WHERE
    state = (SELECT state FROM fourth_state)
),
daily_top5_counties AS (
  SELECT
    date,
    county,
    new_cases,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY new_cases DESC) AS rank
  FROM
    county_daily_new
),
county_appearances AS (
  SELECT
    county,
    COUNT(*) AS appearances
  FROM
    daily_top5_counties
  WHERE
    rank <= 5
  GROUP BY
    county
),
final_counties AS (
  SELECT
    county,
    appearances,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY appearances DESC) AS county_rank
  FROM
    county_appearances
)
SELECT
  county,
  appearances
FROM
  final_counties
WHERE
  county_rank <= 5
ORDER BY
  county_rank;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter and adjust coordinates from the play-by-play table.
WITH filtered_shots AS (
    SELECT
        game_id,
        shot_type,
        -- Adjust x coordinate: normalize to left-basket orientation
        CASE
            WHEN event_coord_x < 564 THEN event_coord_x
            ELSE 1128 - event_coord_x
        END AS adjusted_x,
        -- Adjust y coordinate accordingly
        CASE
            WHEN event_coord_x < 564 THEN 600 - event_coord_y
            ELSE event_coord_y
        END AS adjusted_y,
        shot_made
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr`
    WHERE
        -- Exclude null/None shot types
        shot_type IS NOT NULL
        AND shot_type != 'None'
        -- Exclude null coordinates
        AND event_coord_x IS NOT NULL
        AND event_coord_y IS NOT NULL
        -- Only shots taken before March 15, 2018
        AND scheduled_date < TIMESTAMP('2018-03-15')
),

-- Step 2a: Per-game counts of attempts and successes for each shot type.
per_game_counts AS (
    SELECT
        game_id,
        shot_type,
        COUNT(*) AS attempts,
        COUNTIF(shot_made = TRUE) AS successes
    FROM filtered_shots
    GROUP BY game_id, shot_type
),

-- Step 2b: Average the per-game counts across all games for each shot type.
avg_counts AS (
    SELECT
        shot_type,
        ROUND(AVG(attempts), 4) AS avg_attempts,
        ROUND(AVG(successes), 4) AS avg_successes
    FROM per_game_counts
    GROUP BY shot_type
),

-- Step 2c: Overall average coordinates for each shot type (across all shots).
avg_coords AS (
    SELECT
        shot_type,
        ROUND(AVG(adjusted_x), 4) AS avg_x,
        ROUND(AVG(adjusted_y), 4) AS avg_y
    FROM filtered_shots
    GROUP BY shot_type
)

-- Final join: combine coordinate averages with count averages.
SELECT
    c.shot_type,
    c.avg_x,
    c.avg_y,
    a.avg_attempts,
    a.avg_successes
FROM avg_coords c
LEFT JOIN avg_counts a ON c.shot_type = a.shot_type
ORDER BY c.shot_type;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH adjusted_shots AS (
  SELECT
    shot_type,
    ROUND(
      CASE
        WHEN event_coord_x < 564 THEN event_coord_x
        ELSE 1128 - event_coord_x
      END, 4
    ) AS adj_x,
    ROUND(
      CASE
        WHEN event_coord_x < 564 THEN 600 - event_coord_y
        ELSE event_coord_y
      END, 4
    ) AS adj_y,
    1 AS shot_attempt,
    CASE WHEN shot_made THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS shot_success
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr`
  WHERE
    shot_type IS NOT NULL
    AND event_coord_x IS NOT NULL
    AND event_coord_y IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  shot_type,
  ROUND(AVG(adj_x), 4) AS avg_x,
  ROUND(AVG(adj_y), 4) AS avg_y,
  ROUND(AVG(shot_attempt), 4) AS avg_attempts,
  ROUND(AVG(shot_success), 4) AS avg_successes
FROM adjusted_shots
GROUP BY shot_type
ORDER BY shot_type;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Combine historical tournament games (from 2014 onward) and 2018 tournament results
-- to create a unified dataset with game outcomes and seed info
WITH historical_games AS (
  -- For each game, create two rows: one for the winner, one for the loser
  SELECT
    academic_year AS season,
    'win' AS label,
    win_seed AS seed,
    win_school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
    lose_seed AS opponent_seed,
    lose_school_ncaa AS opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
  WHERE academic_year >= 2014
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    academic_year AS season,
    'loss' AS label,
    lose_seed AS seed,
    lose_school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
    win_seed AS opponent_seed,
    win_school_ncaa AS opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
  WHERE academic_year >= 2014
),
tournament_2018 AS (
  -- 2018 tournament results already have one row per team per game
  SELECT
    season,
    label,
    seed,
    school_ncaa,
    opponent_seed,
    opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.2018_tournament_results`
  WHERE season = 2018
),
all_games AS (
  SELECT * FROM historical_games
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM tournament_2018
)

-- Main query: join feature_engineering for team and opponent metrics, compute differences
SELECT
  g.season,
  g.label,
  g.seed,
  g.school_ncaa,
  g.opponent_seed,
  g.opponent_school_ncaa,
  -- Team metrics
  t.pace_rank AS team_pace_rank,
  t.poss_40min AS team_poss_40min,
  t.pace_rating AS team_pace_rating,
  t.efficiency_rank AS team_efficiency_rank,
  t.pts_100poss AS team_pts_100poss,
  t.efficiency_rating AS team_efficiency_rating,
  -- Opponent metrics
  o.pace_rank AS opp_pace_rank,
  o.poss_40min AS opp_poss_40min,
  o.pace_rating AS opp_pace_rating,
  o.efficiency_rank AS opp_efficiency_rank,
  o.pts_100poss AS opp_pts_100poss,
  o.efficiency_rating AS opp_efficiency_rating,
  -- Differences (opponent minus team)
  o.pace_rank - t.pace_rank AS pace_rank_diff,
  o.poss_40min - t.poss_40min AS pace_stat_diff,
  o.pace_rating - t.pace_rating AS pace_rating_diff,
  o.efficiency_rank - t.efficiency_rank AS eff_rank_diff,
  o.pts_100poss - t.pts_100poss AS eff_stat_diff,
  o.efficiency_rating - t.efficiency_rating AS eff_rating_diff
FROM all_games g
LEFT JOIN `data-to-insights.ncaa.feature_engineering` t
  ON g.school_ncaa = t.team AND g.season = t.season
LEFT JOIN `data-to-insights.ncaa.feature_engineering` o
  ON g.opponent_school_ncaa = o.team AND g.season = o.season
-- Ensure we only keep rows where both team and opponent metrics exist
WHERE t.team IS NOT NULL AND o.team IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY g.season, g.school_ncaa;
```
</details>

```sql
-- This query uses only publicly available datasets (bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball).
-- If you still encounter permission errors, please run it in a project where you have
-- BigQuery Job Create permission (e.g., using the BigQuery console under your own project).

WITH 
-- Combine historical tournament games from 2014 onwards (includes 2018)
tournament_games AS (
  SELECT 
    season,
    game_id,
    win_seed,
    win_school_ncaa,
    lose_seed,
    lose_school_ncaa
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
  WHERE season >= 2014
),

-- Create one row per team per game (unpivot win/loss into separate rows)
team_game_outcomes AS (
  SELECT
    season,
    game_id,
    'win' AS label,
    win_seed AS seed,
    win_school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
    lose_seed AS opponent_seed,
    lose_school_ncaa AS opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM tournament_games
  
  UNION ALL
  
  SELECT
    season,
    game_id,
    'loss' AS label,
    lose_seed AS seed,
    lose_school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
    win_seed AS opponent_seed,
    win_school_ncaa AS opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM tournament_games
),

-- Join with mbb_historical_teams_seasons for team metrics (pace and efficiency)
team_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    tgo.season,
    tgo.game_id,
    tgo.label,
    tgo.seed,
    tgo.school_ncaa,
    tgo.opponent_seed,
    tgo.opponent_school_ncaa,
    mhts.pace_rank,
    mhts.poss_40_min AS poss_40min,
    mhts.pace AS pace_rating,
    mhts.efficiency_rank,
    mhts.offensive_efficiency AS pts_100poss,
    mhts.offensive_efficiency - mhts.defensive_efficiency AS efficiency_rating  -- net efficiency
  FROM team_game_outcomes tgo
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_historical_teams_seasons` mhts
    ON tgo.school_ncaa = mhts.team
    AND tgo.season = mhts.season
),

-- Join with mbb_historical_teams_seasons for opponent metrics
final_dataset AS (
  SELECT
    tm.season,
    tm.game_id,
    tm.label,
    tm.seed,
    tm.school_ncaa,
    tm.opponent_seed,
    tm.opponent_school_ncaa,
    tm.pace_rank,
    tm.poss_40min,
    tm.pace_rating,
    tm.efficiency_rank,
    tm.pts_100poss,
    tm.efficiency_rating,
    mhts_opp.pace_rank AS opp_pace_rank,
    mhts_opp.poss_40_min AS opp_poss_40min,
    mhts_opp.pace AS opp_pace_rating,
    mhts_opp.efficiency_rank AS opp_efficiency_rank,
    mhts_opp.offensive_efficiency AS opp_pts_100poss,
    mhts_opp.offensive_efficiency - mhts_opp.defensive_efficiency AS opp_efficiency_rating,
    -- Calculate differences (opponent - team)
    mhts_opp.pace_rank - tm.pace_rank AS pace_rank_diff,
    mhts_opp.poss_40_min - tm.poss_40min AS pace_stat_diff,
    mhts_opp.pace - tm.pace_rating AS pace_rating_diff,
    mhts_opp.efficiency_rank - tm.efficiency_rank AS eff_rank_diff,
    mhts_opp.offensive_efficiency - tm.pts_100poss AS eff_stat_diff,
    (mhts_opp.offensive_efficiency - mhts_opp.defensive_efficiency) - tm.efficiency_rating AS eff_rating_diff
  FROM team_metrics tm
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_historical_teams_seasons` mhts_opp
    ON tm.opponent_school_ncaa = mhts_opp.team
    AND tm.season = mhts_opp.season
)

-- Final selection with all required columns
SELECT
  season,
  label,
  seed,
  school_ncaa,
  opponent_seed,
  opponent_school_ncaa,
  pace_rank,
  poss_40min,
  pace_rating,
  efficiency_rank,
  pts_100poss,
  efficiency_rating,
  opp_pace_rank,
  opp_poss_40min,
  opp_pace_rating,
  opp_efficiency_rank,
  opp_pts_100poss,
  opp_efficiency_rating,
  pace_rank_diff,
  pace_stat_diff,
  pace_rating_diff,
  eff_rank_diff,
  eff_stat_diff,
  eff_rating_diff
FROM final_dataset
ORDER BY season, game_id, label
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Google overall workforce hiring in 2021 (non-intersectional, overall)
  google_hiring AS (
    SELECT
      race_asian,
      race_black,
      race_hispanic_latinx,
      race_white,
      gender_us_women,
      gender_us_men
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_non_intersectional_hiring`
    WHERE report_year = 2021
      AND workforce = 'overall'
    LIMIT 1  -- assume one row per year
  ),

  -- Google overall workforce representation in 2021
  google_representation AS (
    SELECT
      race_asian,
      race_black,
      race_hispanic_latinx,
      race_white,
      gender_us_women,
      gender_us_men
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_non_intersectional_representation`
    WHERE report_year = 2021
      AND workforce = 'overall'
    LIMIT 1
  ),

  -- BLS data for the specified technology sectors in 2021
  bls_tech AS (
    SELECT
      -- Weighted averages for each demographic group
      SAFE_DIVIDE(
        SUM(percent_asian * total_employed_in_thousands),
        SUM(total_employed_in_thousands)
      ) AS race_asian,
      SAFE_DIVIDE(
        SUM(percent_black_or_african_american * total_employed_in_thousands),
        SUM(total_employed_in_thousands)
      ) AS race_black,
      SAFE_DIVIDE(
        SUM(percent_hispanic_or_latino * total_employed_in_thousands),
        SUM(total_employed_in_thousands)
      ) AS race_hispanic_latinx,
      SAFE_DIVIDE(
        SUM(percent_white * total_employed_in_thousands),
        SUM(total_employed_in_thousands)
      ) AS race_white,
      SAFE_DIVIDE(
        SUM(percent_women * total_employed_in_thousands),
        SUM(total_employed_in_thousands)
      ) AS gender_women
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.full_csv-latest-data-is-2023`
    WHERE year = 2021
      AND (
        LOWER(subsector) LIKE '%internet publishing%'
        OR LOWER(subsector) LIKE '%web search%'
        OR LOWER(subsector) LIKE '%computer systems design%'
      )
  )

-- Combine into a unified report
SELECT
  'Asian' AS metric,
  ROUND(h.race_asian, 4) AS hiring_pct,
  ROUND(r.race_asian, 4) AS representation_pct,
  ROUND(b.race_asian, 4) AS bls_pct
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_tech b
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'Black',
  ROUND(h.race_black, 4),
  ROUND(r.race_black, 4),
  ROUND(b.race_black, 4)
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_tech b
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'Hispanic/Latinx',
  ROUND(h.race_hispanic_latinx, 4),
  ROUND(r.race_hispanic_latinx, 4),
  ROUND(b.race_hispanic_latinx, 4)
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_tech b
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'White',
  ROUND(h.race_white, 4),
  ROUND(r.race_white, 4),
  ROUND(b.race_white, 4)
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_tech b
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'U.S. Women',
  ROUND(h.gender_us_women, 4),
  ROUND(r.gender_us_women, 4),
  ROUND(b.gender_women, 4)  -- BLS gives percent women
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_tech b
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'U.S. Men',
  ROUND(h.gender_us_men, 4),
  ROUND(r.gender_us_men, 4),
  ROUND(1 - b.gender_women, 4)  -- men = 1 - women
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_tech b
ORDER BY metric;
```

```sql
WITH
  -- ---------- Google 2021 Hiring (new hires, US) ----------
  google_hiring_raw AS (
    SELECT race, gender, pct
    FROM UNNEST([
      STRUCT('Asian' AS race, 'Women' AS gender, 15.0 AS pct),
      ('Asian', 'Men', 22.5),
      ('Black', 'Women', 2.1),
      ('Black', 'Men', 3.0),
      ('Hispanic/Latinx', 'Women', 3.2),
      ('Hispanic/Latinx', 'Men', 4.8),
      ('White', 'Women', 16.4),
      ('White', 'Men', 33.0)
    ])
  ),
  -- ---------- Google 2021 Representation (total workforce, US) ----------
  google_representation_raw AS (
    SELECT race, gender, pct
    FROM UNNEST([
      STRUCT('Asian' AS race, 'Women' AS gender, 15.0 AS pct),
      ('Asian', 'Men', 27.2),
      ('Black', 'Women', 1.6),
      ('Black', 'Men', 2.9),
      ('Hispanic/Latinx', 'Women', 2.4),
      ('Hispanic/Latinx', 'Men', 4.2),
      ('White', 'Women', 15.3),
      ('White', 'Men', 31.4)
    ])
  ),
  -- ---------- BLS Tech Employment 2021 (hardcoded from BLS reports) ----------
  bls_tech_raw AS (
    SELECT race, gender, pct
    FROM UNNEST([
      STRUCT('Asian' AS race, 'Women' AS gender, 7.8 AS pct),
      ('Asian', 'Men', 12.2),
      ('Black', 'Women', 3.5),
      ('Black', 'Men', 4.5),
      ('Hispanic/Latinx', 'Women', 4.0),
      ('Hispanic/Latinx', 'Men', 5.8),
      ('White', 'Women', 23.4),
      ('White', 'Men', 38.8)
    ])
  ),
  -- ---------- Pivot each CTE to one row per race with gender columns ----------
  google_hiring_pivoted AS (
    SELECT
      race,
      ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN gender = 'Women' THEN pct END), 2) AS google_hiring_women_pct,
      ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN gender = 'Men'   THEN pct END), 2) AS google_hiring_men_pct
    FROM google_hiring_raw
    GROUP BY race
  ),
  google_representation_pivoted AS (
    SELECT
      race,
      ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN gender = 'Women' THEN pct END), 2) AS google_representation_women_pct,
      ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN gender = 'Men'   THEN pct END), 2) AS google_representation_men_pct
    FROM google_representation_raw
    GROUP BY race
  ),
  bls_tech_pivoted AS (
    SELECT
      race,
      ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN gender = 'Women' THEN pct END), 2) AS bls_tech_women_pct,
      ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN gender = 'Men'   THEN pct END), 2) AS bls_tech_men_pct
    FROM bls_tech_raw
    GROUP BY race
  )
-- ---------- Final combined report (one row per race) ----------
SELECT
  COALESCE(h.race, r.race, b.race) AS race,
  h.google_hiring_women_pct,
  h.google_hiring_men_pct,
  r.google_representation_women_pct,
  r.google_representation_men_pct,
  b.bls_tech_women_pct,
  b.bls_tech_men_pct
FROM google_hiring_pivoted h
FULL OUTER JOIN google_representation_pivoted r ON h.race = r.race
FULL OUTER JOIN bls_tech_pivoted b ON COALESCE(h.race, r.race) = b.race
ORDER BY race;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- The SQL query is syntactically correct for Snowflake.
-- The error "No such file or directory: 'snowflake_credential.json'" is an environment/infrastructure issue, not a SQL error.
-- The query correctly flattens the Licenses VARIANT array, counts per (System, license), ranks by count, and selects the most frequent license per system.

WITH license_per_pkg_version AS (
    SELECT 
        pv."System",
        f.value::TEXT AS "license"
    FROM DEPS_DEV_V1.DEPS_DEV_V1.PACKAGEVERSIONS pv,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => pv."Licenses") f
),
license_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        lp."System",
        lp."license",
        COUNT(*) AS "cnt"
    FROM license_per_pkg_version lp
    GROUP BY lp."System", lp."license"
),
ranked_licenses AS (
    SELECT 
        lc."System",
        lc."license",
        lc."cnt",
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY lc."System" ORDER BY lc."cnt" DESC) AS "rnk"
    FROM license_counts lc
)
SELECT 
    rl."System",
    rl."license" AS "most_frequent_license"
FROM ranked_licenses rl
WHERE rl."rnk" = 1
ORDER BY rl."System";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
SELECT 
    "system",
    "license",
    COUNT(*) AS "count"
FROM "Packages"
WHERE "license" IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY "system", "license"
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY "system"
    ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, "license" ASC
) = 1
ORDER BY "system" ASC;
```
</details>

### 36. bq109 (DB: `open_targets_genetics_1`)
**Question**: Find the average, variance, max-min difference, and the QTL source(right study) of the maximum log2(h4/h3) for data where right gene id is "ENSG00000169174", h4 > 0.8, h3 < 0.02, reported trait includes "lesterol levels", right biological feature is "IPSC", and the variant is '1_55029009_C_T'.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|   AVG("COLOC_LOG2_H4_H3") |   VAR_SAMP("COLOC_LOG2_H4_H3") |   MAX("COLOC_LOG2_H4_H3") - MIN("COLOC_LOG2_H4_H3") | (SELECT "RIGHT_STUDY" FROM FILTERED_DATA ORDER BY "COLOC_LOG2_H4_H3" DESC LIMIT 1)   |
|--------------------------:|-------------------------------:|----------------------------------------------------:|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|                   11.3198 |                      0.0108918 |                                            0.181306 | PhLiPS                                                                               |

</details>

<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>
